Reproduces identically at the base commit; unrelated to this diff. | Harnesses (`*-harness.mjs`, `probe-*.mjs`) are the scripts that produced the above; they import the worktree's own modules and write nothing into the repo. ```
- Outcome: ⚠️ 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) across 1 run (22m21s) ## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
⏭️ **intent** - skipped ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ⚠️ `src/subprocess.js:145` - quoteShimArg escapes an embedded double quote as `\"` (MSVCRT style), but the command line is first parsed by cmd.exe, which does not honour backslash escapes: the `"` closes cmd's quoted section, so everything after it — including later arguments — is parsed outside quotes. Trace: quoteShimArg('a"&whoami&"b') yields `"a\"&whoami&\"b"`; cmd sees quote-open, `a`, literal `\`, quote-close, then `&whoami&` unquoted and executes it as a separate command. The same toggle silently corrupts any later argument even without metacharacters. The fix that satisfies both parsers is doubling (`""` inside the quoted run), which cmd treats as close+reopen with nothing in between and MSVCRT decodes as a literal quote. Carriage return / newline in an argument is likewise not neutralised by quoting and should be refused like `%`. The existing assertion in test/subprocess.test.js ('has\"quote') encodes the current behaviour and must move with the fix. - ⚠️ `src/subprocess.js:28` - The new ERR_WINDOWS_SHIM_UNSAFE_ARG refusal resolves as `{ code: null, spawnError }`, but classifyAcpxFailure (src/acpx.js:86) only special-cases ENOENT and its stderr regex does not match the new message. Concrete path: a repo whose path contains two `%` characters is passed as `--cwd`; openSession (src/acpx.js:375-386) sees code !== 0 and an unclassified failure, so it throws `acpx <agent> has no session support: exit null` with unsupported = true, and sessionPrompt (src/acpx.js:506) then falls back to an exec one-shot that fails again for the same reason. The user is told the harness lacks session support when the real cause is an argument backpass refused to pass. Surface the refusal distinctly at the acpx boundary instead of letting it fall through the session-support branch. - ℹ️ `src/subprocess.js:127` - EXPANDABLE_PERCENT (/%[^%]*%/) refuses any argument containing two `%` characters anywhere, not only a plausible variable reference: `C:\\dev\\50%-off\\repo`, `a%b%c` with no such variable defined, and even a literal `%%` all trip it, and cmd.exe leaves an undefined `%foo%` literal anyway. On Windows that turns an otherwise working run (the repo path is passed as `--cwd`) into a hard refusal. The loud fail is a deliberate, documented choice; narrowing the predicate to a plausible variable-name shape is a product-behaviour call, so flagging rather than changing it. - ℹ️ `src/harness-invoke.js:323` - The generated harness wrapper still launches a `.cmd`/`.bat` through Node's `shell: true`, which is exactly the argv-joining-without-quoting behaviour the new windowsShimLaunch doc rejects: any forwarded argument containing a space is split. Reachable on Windows when CODEX_PATH points at `codex.cmd` (applyCodexWriteAccess, src/harness-invoke.js:216-224) and the acpx codex adapter forwards a path with spaces. This is pre-existing, not introduced here, and the remedy would mean inlining the quoting policy into the standalone wrapper text (the wrapper is a separate process and cannot import subprocess.js) — i.e. it extends the change beyond its stated intent, so it needs authorization rather than a mechanical fix. 🔧 Fix: refuse unquotable shim args and surface refusal at acpx 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `src/acpx.js:487` - The shim-refusal surfacing was wired into probeSession (260), execOneShot (336) and openSession's `sessions new` (395), but not into the per-turn `prompt` closure — and that is the only acpx call that actually puts a repo path on argv, so the mislabel the fix round targeted is still reachable on the dominant path. Concrete trace, Windows, repo at `C:\dev\%BUILD%\repo`: probeSession runs `sessions new --name backpass-probe-…` (cwd is a spawn option, not argv) → no refusal, verdict ok. openSession's create call carries only `--model`/agent args → no refusal, session opens. The first `prompt()` builds `baseArgs({cwd})` → `--cwd C:\dev\%BUILD%\repo` → windowsShimLaunch refuses → `{code:null, stderr:<refusal>, spawnError}` → line 487 throws `AcpxError("acpx codex session prompt failed (exit null)")`. classifyAcpxFailure returns null (correct — no demotion), but src/analyze.js:352 fail-softs every non-UserError: it warns `err.message` only and records the transcript as failed, so the user sees N transcripts failing with "exit null" and the named refusal sitting in `err.stderr` is never printed. Remedy is the same three lines already used at the other sites: `const refusal = shimRefusalError(result); if (refusal) throw refusal;` before the timedOut check at 486. The same gap exists at verifyHarnessInvocation (src/acpx.js:200-207), which also passes `--cwd` on argv; there the impact is milder because the UserError already embeds `firstLine(result.stderr)`, so the refused value is at least named. - ℹ️ `test/subprocess.test.js:300` - The test that claims "a shim refusal reaches acpx as its own named error, not as missing session support" calls `shimRefusalError(failure)` directly. It proves the helper builds a UserError, not that any acpx entry point invokes it — the wiring is the entire content of the finding it was added for. That is exactly why the `prompt` closure gap above passed the suite: nothing exercises probeSession/execOneShot/openSession with a refusing argument. A test that stubs runCapture (or points BACKPASS_ACPX_BIN at a fixture shim with the platform seam) and asserts that `openSession(...).prompt(...)` rejects with a UserError naming the refused value would fail before the fix above and pass after it. 🔧 Fix: raise shim refusal at the acpx run funnel 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) still open: - ⚠️ `src/subprocess.js:188` - resolveOnPath splits PATH and joins each entry verbatim, without stripping surrounding double quotes. Windows PATH entries may legally be quoted (e.g. PATH=C:\Windows\system32;"~\AppData\Roaming\npm"), and this repo already compensates for exactly that 40 lines away, inside the generated wrapper: src/harness-invoke.js:312 does entry.replace(/^"|"$/g, "") before resolving. Concrete failing sequence: acpx.cmd lives in the quoted npm entry -> path.join('"~\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm"', 'acpx.cmd') never stats -> resolveOnPath returns null -> resolveShimPath returns null -> runCapture falls back to the plain spawn("acpx"), whose CreateProcess appends only .exe -> ENOENT -> notFoundError prints 'acpx not found on PATH', which is verbatim the misleading failure issue #43 closes. The fix silently does not apply for that PATH shape. Remedy is the same one-line strip already used in harness-invoke.js, applied to `dir` before path.join. - ℹ️ `src/apply/lavish.js:107` - The same change wired windowsShimLaunch into runLavish, but the acpx rule the fix round applied ('raise the refusal before any generic handling') was not extended to the lavish surface. On Windows with a repo at C:\dev\%BUILD%\repo, `backpass apply` (which runs without any model call, so it is reachable independently of analysis) passes <repo>\.backpass\apply\apply.html on argv, windowsShimLaunch refuses, runLavish resolves { code: null, spawnError }, the ENOENT branch at line 101 does not match, and line 107 reports the headline 'lavish-axi failed to open the apply surface'. This is cosmetic only: the detail argument is result.stderr, which is the full refusal message naming the refused path, so the user is not left without the cause. pollDecisions (line 145) already names spawnError.message directly. Noting the asymmetry rather than asking for a change. 🔧 Fix: strip quoted PATH entries and name lavish shim refusal 3 infos still open: - ℹ️ `test/subprocess.test.js:329` - The comment points readers to `test/acpx-shim-refusal.test.js`, but commit 804771a renamed that file to `test/shim-refusal.test.js` (it now also covers the lavish boundary). The referenced path no longer exists, so the pointer to "how the acpx boundary does surface it" dead-ends. Update the name to `test/shim-refusal.test.js`. - ℹ️ `.github/workflows/ci.yml:24` - Tradeoff note, not a defect. The whole change is Windows-only behavior, and the CI matrix is ubuntu-latest + macos-latest (windows-latest deliberately deferred, line 22-23). The new tests are the right design for that constraint - they drive the real `runCapture`/`openSession`/`openApplySurface` through injected `platform`/`spawnFn`/ComSpec seams, so they run and can fail everywhere - but what they assert is the command line backpass *constructs* (`cmd.exe /d /s /c "<shim> ... "`), never what cmd.exe *does* with it. The `/s` quote-stripping, the `%*` forwarding through the npm shim, and the MSVCRT trailing-backslash rule are correct by reasoning and by matching libuv's own idiom, but no automated environment executes them. A single manual smoke on a real Windows box (one `backpass scan` from a path containing a space, and one `backpass apply`) would close the last gap; nothing here needs a code change. - ℹ️ `AGENTS.md:233` - The change creates a contract that now spans three modules and has no entry in the Sharp edges list: on Windows every spawn of an npm `.cmd` goes through `windowsShimLaunch`, and a refused argument arrives as `{ code: null, spawnError.code === "ERR_WINDOWS_SHIM_UNSAFE_ARG" }` that each boundary must raise by name *before* any generic result inspection - otherwise it silently degrades into "no session support" / "exit null" / "failed to open the apply surface". That exact degradation is what rounds 2 and 3 of this run were spent chasing at two separate boundaries, so a fourth spawn boundary added later would very likely reintroduce it. The remedy is documentation, not code: one Sharp-edges bullet naming `src/subprocess.js` as the launch policy, the error code, and the rule that `src/acpx.js`'s `run` funnel and `src/apply/lavish.js` are the two places that surface it. Flagging rather than writing it, since what goes in AGENTS.md is the author's call under this repo's stated bar. 🔧 Fix: document shim refusal contract, fix stale test reference 1 info still open: - ℹ️ `src/subprocess.js:124` - `quoteShimArg` quotes `!` (line 167) and `unsafeShimReason` does not refuse it, but double quotes do not protect `!` from cmd.exe's delayed expansion — that phase runs after quote parsing and ignores quotes. `cmd /d /s /c` does not disable it: delayed expansion is off by default but is turned on globally by HKCU/HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Command Processor\DelayedExpansion=1, and the npm shim's bare `SETLOCAL` inherits that state. Concrete path: a user with that registry value, repo at `C:\dev\build!x!\repo` -> `backpass scan` -> `baseArgs` puts `--cwd C:\dev\build!x!\repo` on argv -> `windowsShimLaunch` finds `acpx.cmd`, sees no unsafe reason, emits `"C:\dev\build!x!\repo"` -> cmd expands the undefined `!x!` to nothing -> acpx receives `C:\dev\build\repo`. backpass reports no error; acpx just analyzes (or fails on) the wrong directory, which is the silent-wrong-value class this module's own policy comment says must not reach the shim. Remedy is mechanical and matches the existing intent: add `/v:off` ahead of `/c` in the args array at line 124 (`["/d", "/s", "/v:off", "/c", ...]`), which overrides the registry for this invocation. Not proposing a widening of `EXPANDABLE_PERCENT` — that would trade this for over-refusal of legal paths the tests deliberately protect.
⚠️ **Test** - 2 issues (1 warning, 1 info) - ⚠️ `src/apply/writer.js:172` - Poza zakresem tego diffu, ale blokuje ostatni krok demonstracji na Windowsie i dotyczy dokładnie platformy, którą ta gałąź naprawia: `backpass apply` zawiesza się na zawsze, zanim zapisze jakikolwiek bajt. `resolveRepo` zwraca `repo.root` z `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, czyli na Windowsie z ukośnikami w przód (`~/repo`), podczas gdy cele zaakceptowanych edycji są budowane przez `path.join`, czyli z backslashami. Pętla `for (let current = path.dirname(file); current !== root; current = path.dirname(current))` nigdy nie trafia w warunek stopu, dochodzi do `C:\` i kręci się w miejscu, bo `path.dirname("C:\\") === "C:\\"`. Potwierdzone sondą (evidence/apply-hang-root-cause.txt) oraz przez uruchomienie tego samego `applyDecisions` z drzewa commita bazowego 698d57f — zawiesza się identycznie, więc jest to błąd wcześniej istniejący, nie regresja tej zmiany. Do decyzji autora, czy naprawić tutaj (gałąź jest o wsparciu Windows), czy zgłosić osobno. - ℹ️ `test/proposal.test.js:2039` - `node --test test/proposal.test.js` daje na Windowsie 2 awarie ('apply measures a legacy skill rewrite missing descriptionDelta' oraz 'a skill-only shrink reports the remaining always-loaded overage'). Uruchomiłem ten sam plik z drzewa commita bazowego 698d57f — identyczne 70 pass / 2 fail, więc to wcześniej istniejąca luka platformowa (CI to ubuntu+macos), a nie skutek tej zmiany. Odnotowuję wyłącznie informacyjnie, bo gałąź dotyczy wsparcia Windows. - `node --test test/subprocess.test.js test/shim-refusal.test.js` — 12 pass, 2 skip (oba skipy to testy grup procesów POSIX, wykonywane na CI linux/macos) - Manualny roundtrip przez prawdziwy cmd.exe: produkcyjny `runCapture("acpx", ...)` przeciw realnemu shimowi `acpx.cmd` forwardującemu `%*` do node.exe, 14 kształtów argumentów, ramię bazowe (698d57f) vs docelowe (da8ff31) — `evidence/roundtrip-harness.mjs` - Manualny transkrypt CLI: `backpass propose --synthesis-agent claude --synthesis-model fake-model` z `acpx.cmd` na PATH (bez `.exe`), ramię pre-fix (drzewo commita 698d57f wyeksportowane przez `git archive`) vs post-fix (worktree) — `evidence/cli-transcript-harness.mjs` - Manualny transkrypt CLI: `backpass apply --no-open` z `lavish-axi.cmd` na PATH, oba ramiona, z fikstur¹ `test/fixtures/fake-lavish` - Izolowany `pollDecisions(...)` przez shim `.cmd` — zwraca `{e1: accepted, e2: accepted}` w 499 ms - `node --test test/proposal.test.js` na worktree i na drzewie commita bazowego — identyczny wynik 70 pass / 2 fail w obu, czyli awarie są wcześniej istniejące i windowsowo-specyficzne - Sonda root-cause zawieszenia `applyDecisions` — `evidence/probe-apply-writer.mjs` i `evidence/apply-hang-root-cause.txt`
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Lint** - 1 issue found → auto-fixed ✅ - 🚨 `test/shim-refusal.test.js:82` - `pnpm run typecheck` (tsc --noEmit, checkJs over test/**) fails with 8 errors in the new test/shim-refusal.test.js, which will turn CI red: lines 82, 101, 117 read `err.name` / `err.message` inside the message argument of `assert.ok(err instanceof UserError, ...)`, i.e. before the assertion narrows `err` from `unknown` (TS2339 on 'name' and 'message'); lines 85 and 103 read `err.unsupported` after narrowing to `UserError`, which does not declare that field (TS2339). I fixed the three source-side counterparts (src/acpx.js:79 and test/subprocess.test.js:292 both read `spawnError.value`) by giving src/subprocess.js a `ShimError` typedef (`NodeJS.ErrnoException & { value?: string }`) and using it in the JSDoc return types of `runCapture` and `windowsShimLaunch`; these 8 remain because the fix has to be made inside a test file and this phase must not change tests. Mechanical remedy, behaviour-preserving: annotate each rejects callback parameter as `(/** @type {any} */ err) =>`, or follow the repo idiom in test/synthesize.test.js:334 (narrow with a bare `assert.ok(err instanceof UserError)` first, then assert on the message) plus one cast for the `err.unsupported` reads. Verified with the locked toolchain (typescript 5.9.3, @types/node 25.9.5); eslint and prettier are clean. 🔧 Fix: narrow error types in shim refusal test asserts ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: fix(skills): parse YAML block-scalar descriptions correctly
body:
## Intent Fix parseFrontmatter to correctly handle YAML block-scalar indicators (>, >-, >+, |, |-, |+) on a frontmatter value: the parsed value must be the actual folded (spaces-joined) or literal (newline-preserved) text with the indicator and chomping marker removed, not leaked into the value (observed as '>- ' prepended to skill description text, e.g. firstmate skill description fields, polluting every synthesis/analysis prompt). Reproduce first with a failing test on a real skill-description-shaped folded-scalar fixture asserting the parsed value has no leading >/|/- marker and reads as the intended text, covering both > and | variants and all chomping suffixes, then fix. Do not over-reach into a full YAML library; handle the block-scalar indicators cleanly within the existing minimal parser. Additionally, add ONE short, plainly-worded sentence to the synthesis/proposal prompt instructing the model not to assert or dramatize motives/intent it cannot support from the evidence; keep it to a single sentence and do not restructure the prompt. Verify the no-motive sentence through the real prompt-construction/rendering path (not a raw source grep of a string constant). No other parser or prompt behavior should change; all existing tests must still pass. ## What Changed - Parse folded and literal skill-description scalars with all YAML chomping suffixes without leaking indicator markers. - Instruct synthesis to avoid unsupported claims about agent motives or intent, with coverage through the rendered prompt path. ## Risk Assessment 🚨 High: The parser silently returns incorrect text for reachable block-scalar inputs and contradicts an explicit required acceptance criterion, so it should not merge without resolution or explicit approval. ## Testing Inspected the targeted diff, ran the focused parser and real synthesis-path tests, and captured an end-to-end skill-index and rendered-prompt artifact confirming block markers do not leak and the no-motive instruction reaches the generated prompt; all checks passed and the worktree remained unchanged.
Evidence: End-to-end frontmatter parsing and rendered synthesis prompt Source: [End-to-end frontmatter parsing and rendered synthesis prompt](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/blob/0ca15046cede16b0c9b1652c14c6a00a1129a6c9/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/backpass-frontmatter-polish-r1/frontmatter-prompt-e2e.txt) ```text Analysis prompt skill index (loaded from real SKILL.md files): - fold-clip (.agents/skills/fold-clip/SKILL.md) :: Use this skill for firstmate release operations. - fold-keep (.agents/skills/fold-keep/SKILL.md) :: Use this skill for firstmate release operations. - fold-strip (.agents/skills/fold-strip/SKILL.md) :: Use this skill for firstmate release operations. - literal-clip (.agents/skills/literal-clip/SKILL.md) :: Use this skill for firstmate release operations. - literal-keep (.agents/skills/literal-keep/SKILL.md) :: Use this skill for firstmate release operations. - literal-strip (.agents/skills/literal-strip/SKILL.md) :: Use this skill for firstmate release operations. Marker leak check: PASS - no block indicators leaked Rendered synthesis prompt policy: 10. Do not assert or dramatize an agent's motives or intent beyond what the evidence supports. ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 error - 🚨 `src/skills.js:127` - The required "actual folded ... or literal ... text" is not produced for block scalars with blank lines or chomping suffixes. The regex recognizes `+`/`-` but discards which suffix was present, while line 131 skips blank content lines. For example, a `|+` description containing two paragraphs and trailing blank lines silently loses the paragraph blank line and all trailing newlines; `|`, `|-`, and `|+` therefore produce the same value. The new expectations at test/skills.test.js:75-80 codify this incorrect result. Preserve block blank lines, fold or retain them according to style, and apply strip/clip/keep chomping at parseFrontmatter before returning.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `node --test test/skills.test.js` - `node --test --test-name-pattern='synthesis edits the staging copy natively' test/synthesize.test.js` - Manual end-to-end Node check using `loadSkills`, `renderSkillIndexForAnalysis`, and `renderPrompt` across `>`, `>-`, `>+`, `|`, `|-`, and `|+` skill descriptions
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Lint** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Push** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: Proposal: user-level backward pass (skills and instructions at ~/.claude, not just the project)
body:
Requested by @kunchenguid for @petergyang's setup: Peter keeps all of his skills and instructions at user level (for Claude Code: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `~/.claude/skills/*`, plus the equivalents for other harnesses). A project-level run never sees or improves the files he actually relies on. This issue is a design proposal for a **user-level backward pass**. It is a proposal only; nothing is implemented.

## TL;DR

- Add a second run **scope**, selected explicitly with `--scope user` (default stays `project`). A run has exactly one scope and only ever writes inside it.
- In user scope the **weights** are the user's always-loaded instruction file(s) plus the user-level skills directories the harnesses load; the **corpus** is every session of that user on the machine, across all projects and harnesses, minus backpass's own sessions.
- Every existing gate stays (verbatim quotes, `minGapEvidence` sessions, harm floor for removals, budget gate, staging-copy synthesis, per-edit human apply). One gate is added: a user-level edit must corroborate across **`minGapProjects` distinct projects** (default 2), so project-specific rules cannot land in a global file.
- Project scope never writes to user files and user scope never writes to project files. Cross-scope facts are **read-only context** used to attribute a loss to the right layer.
- This conflicts with `VISION.md` ("It does not train a person's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`") and the H-8 ruling in `VISION-ANSWERS.md`. Section 8 explains why this proposal is not H-8 and what the vision amendment would say. Adopting it is the captain's call and is Phase 0.

## 1. How a run is scoped today (codebase facts)

Everything below was read from the source at `b7a6044` (v0.1.17).

**Project identity is required at the entry point.** `main()` in `src/cli.js` calls `resolveRepo(process.cwd())` (`src/repo.js`) before dispatching any command. Outside a git checkout it throws `not inside a git repository` with the hint `backpass runs per-repo; cd into a repo and retry`. The returned `repo` object (`root`, `realRoot`, `name`, `worktrees`, `remotes`, `cloneRemotes`, `siblingWorktrees`) is then threaded into every stage. `grep -rn "repo\.\(root\|name\|...\)" src` finds about 40 call sites outside `src/repo.js`, concentrated in `src/commands/*.js`, `src/analyze.js`, `src/synthesize.js`, `src/workspace.js`, `src/apply/writer.js`, and `src/discovery/association.js`.

**Config already has a user layer.** `loadConfig(repo.root, overrides)` in `src/config.js` merges defaults < `~/.config/backpass/config.json` (honours `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`) < `<repo>/.backpassrc.json` < CLI flags. There is no scope concept; the user file is just a lower-precedence layer of project config.

**State is per repo.** `new State(repo.root)` (`src/state.js`) puts everything under `<repo>/.backpass/` (scan cache, evidence, summary, proposal, rejections, gap ledger, probe cache, prompts, synthesis workspace, apply surface) and `ensure()` writes `.backpass/` into `.git/info/exclude`. That exclude step is already fail-soft outside git (`ensureLocalExclude` returns `no-git`).

**Discovery is machine-wide; project scoping is a filter.** Each adapter enumerates its whole store: `enumerate()` in `src/discovery/adapters/claude.js` walks every directory under `~/.claude/projects/` (and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects`), `codex.js` walks every `YYYY/MM/DD` shard under `~/.codex/sessions/`, `opencode.js` and `hermes.js` query every session row, `grok.js` and `cursor-cli.js` list every cwd directory, `pi.js` covers `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` and the BB bridge dirs. `discoverTranscripts()` in `src/discovery/index.js` then calls `associate()` (`src/discovery/association.js`) per descriptor, which keeps a session only when its cwd is under a worktree (tier 1), under a sibling clone sharing a remote (tier 1.5), its recorded remote matches (tier 2), or a dead path ends in the repo name or matches a glob (tier 3). The scan cache (`.backpass/scan-cache.json`) stores the adapter **descriptor** (id, cwd, remotes, interaction signals), not the verdict, so its contents are repo-independent even though the file lives per repo. Self-sessions are dropped by `isSelfSession()` (`src/discovery/self.js`) via `SELF_SESSION_SENTINEL` in the first user message.

**Sampling is scope-agnostic.** `capTranscripts()` (`src/sample.js`) caps at `maxTranscripts` (100) with a deterministic recency-weighted draw keyed by `transcriptIdentity`, stratified only by interactive vs non-interactive (`mixAllocations`). Nothing knows about projects because a project run has exactly one.

**The weights are resolved relative to `repo.root`.** `primaryMemoryFile()` in `src/commands/analyze.js` calls `resolveMemoryFiles(repo.root, config.memoryFiles)` (`src/memory.js`), which is `readMemoryFile(repoRoot, relative)` = `path.join(repoRoot, relative)`; the first existing file is canonical, an `@AGENTS.md`-only `CLAUDE.md` is a pointer (`isPointerTo`), any other full file is warned about. Skills come from `loadProjectSkills(repo.root, overflow.dir)` over `resolveProjectSkillDirs()` (`.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, plus a configured dir) in `src/skills.js`. The cache key is `memorySurfaceHash(setHash, skills)`: memory files plus every skill description line.

**The analysis model never sees user-level files.** `analyzeOne()` in `src/analyze.js` renders `src/prompts/analysis.md` with exactly `MEMORY_PATH`, `INSTRUCTION_INDEX` (the project file's `AG-nnn` units), `SKILLS` (the project skill index), `OPEN_GAPS`, and `TRACE`. `sanitizeEvidence()` drops any evidence whose `instruction` id is not in that index. No module in `src/` references `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or any other user-level path (grep confirms); the README's "treated as context, never an edit target" is generous - in code it is neither. Consequence for Peter's setup: a steer that came from `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is invisible, and a mistake one of his user-level skills would have prevented is reported as a **project** gap (or not at all), because `coveredBySkill` can only name a project skill.

**Fold, ledger, and rejections are keyed to the project file.** `foldForRun()` (`src/commands/propose.js`) keeps evidence where `e.memoryPath === memoryFile.path` and the surface hash matches; `gapEntryId(memoryPath, proposedInstruction)` (`src/gap-ledger.js`) keys the ledger by memory path; evidence records (`analyzeTranscripts`) stamp `transcript.{harness,id,identity,path,mtimeMs,bytes,startedAt,association,interaction}` but **not** the session cwd or project, so nothing downstream can currently say "this gap was seen in three different repos".

**Synthesis and apply assume one repo root.** `prepareWorkspace()` (`src/workspace.js`) copies the memory file and skill dirs from `repo.root` into `.backpass/synthesis/`; the synthesis and annotate prompts carry `REPO_NAME`/`REPO_ROOT` so the agent can ground edits by reading the repo; `repoFingerprint`/`assertRepoUntouched` guard that root. Analysis and consolidation acpx calls run with `cwd: repo.root` (`src/analyze.js`, `src/consolidate.js`). `applyDecisions()` in `src/apply/writer.js` resolves every target as `path.join(repo.root, relative)`, checks `proposal.memoryFile.hash` and `proposal.targetFiles` hashes, composes each file whole-or-nothing, writes skills before the memory file, rolls back on failure, and `ensureSkillsLayout(repo.root)` creates `.agents/skills` plus the `.claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills` symlink. `atomicReplace()` writes through `fs.realpathSync`, so a symlinked memory file gets its target replaced (and a read-only target fails loudly and rolls back).

**Vision.** `VISION.md` line 5: "The project file is the one it trains; a person's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is handwritten preference, and anything learned belongs in project memory instead." Scope: "It does not train a person's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`." `VISION-ANSWERS.md` H-8 ("Edit global memory across repos") was ruled **off mission** with the reasoning "for now, my philosophy is that global memory should be handwritten by the user and only contains their preferences." The word "for now" is why this proposal exists; see section 8.

## 2. Scope model

A **scope** is the triple (weights surface, session corpus, state directory). Today there is one kind, `project`. This adds `user`.

| | `project` (today) | `user` (proposed) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weights | `<repo>/AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) + `<repo>/.agents/skills` | the user's always-loaded instruction file(s) + user-level skills dirs (section 4) |
| Corpus | sessions associated with this repo (tiers 1 to 3) | every session of this user on this machine, all projects, all configured harnesses |
| Identity | `resolveRepo(cwd)` | `os.homedir()` (+ `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `XDG_*` as the harnesses define) |
| State | `<repo>/.backpass/` | `$XDG_STATE_HOME/backpass/user/` (default `~/.local/state/backpass/user/`), mode 0700 |
| Config | `~/.config/backpass/config.json` < `.backpassrc.json` < flags | `~/.config/backpass/config.json` `user` block < flags; `.backpassrc.json` is never read |

**Why "all sessions" and not "sessions where a user-level instruction was in play".** No harness records which instructions or skills were loaded. User-level instruction files load in every session by definition, so "in play" is all sessions. Skill triggers are exactly what needs measuring, including the sessions where a skill should have fired and did not (the failed-trigger signal the fold already computes via `coveredBySkill`); filtering the corpus to sessions where a skill fired would hide the most valuable negative evidence. Relevance per instruction and per skill falls out of the fold, as it does today.

**Coexistence: an explicit mode, never automatic tiering.** A run is exactly one scope, chosen by `--scope`. Rejected alternatives:

- *Automatic promotion* ("when a gap corroborates in N repos, propose it in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`") is precisely the H-8 proposal that was ruled off mission, and it turns a project run into a writer of a file the user did not point it at. `VISION.md`: "A change should be resisted when it widens what writes."
- *Both scopes in one run* doubles the surfaces one apply review covers and makes the budget gate ambiguous (which surface's cap applies to an addition?). Two separate runs with two separate apply reviews are the honest shape.

Both scopes keep their own evidence, ledger, rejections, and proposal. A user who never passes `--scope user` gets exactly today's behaviour.

## 3. Session discovery at user level

**Roots.** Unchanged: the seven adapters already enumerate their whole stores (section 1). Claude Code (`~/.claude/projects/**`, `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects/**`) and Codex (`~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl`) are the first cut; Pi, OpenCode, Grok, Cursor CLI, and Hermes come for free at discovery because association is the only per-scope step. Hermes stays `cli`/`acp` only for the same reason as today (gateway/cron rows share a process cwd).

**Association.** `discoverTranscripts({ repo, ... })` becomes `discoverTranscripts({ scope, ... })`. The project scope keeps `associate()` unchanged. The user scope accepts every descriptor with a cwd and stamps a **project key** instead of a tier: realpath of the git toplevel when the cwd still exists inside a checkout, else the normalized recorded remote (`normalizeRemote`, tier-2 style, so Codex and Grok sessions of deleted worktrees still group), else the cwd string. The key is what stratified sampling, the `minGapProjects` gate, and the per-project relevance split (section 5) need. `--strict` in user scope means "sessions whose cwd or remote resolves to a real project"; sessions with only a dead unrecognisable cwd are still counted but grouped under their own key.

**Self-exclusion.** The sentinel check stays. Two additions: (a) backpass's own analysis and synthesis calls in user scope run with `cwd` = the user state dir (there is no repo), and the sentinel excludes them as today; (b) any session whose cwd is under a backpass state dir or synthesis workspace is dropped by cwd, which also closes the existing hole for SQLite-backed stores where `isSelfSession` has no file head to inspect.

**Volume and sampling.** On the machine this was read on: 191 Claude project directories, 503 Codex rollouts, 132 Pi cwd directories. The defaults already bound cost: `since 30d`, `maxTranscripts 100`, recency-weighted sticky sampling, incremental evidence cache. A user run therefore costs about the same number of analysis calls as a project run; what changes is who the 100 are. Controls:

- `discovery.includeProjects` / `discovery.excludeProjects` (globs over project keys and cwds) in the `user` config block, and `--project <glob>` on the CLI. `backpass scan --scope user` prints the per-project table before any model call.
- `discovery.maxTranscriptsPerProject` (default unset) so one hot repo cannot fill the whole sample. Phase 2 replaces it with project-aware proportional-with-floor allocation nested inside the interaction split, reusing the `mixAllocations` shape in `src/sample.js`.
- Everything else (`--since`, `--max-transcripts`, `--seed`, `--limit`, `--harness`) works unchanged.

**Privacy and cost of reading every project's transcripts.** The run reads work, client, and personal repos into one corpus, distills each session (`src/distill.js`, `src/redact.js`), and sends the distilled trace to the harness the user already authenticated (no new key, per the vision). What is new is concentration: quotes from every project land in one `evidence/` directory and one gap ledger. Mitigations: the state dir is created 0700; `excludeProjects` is honoured before distillation; `backpass scan --scope user` is the preflight that names every project about to be read; redaction stays a coarse net that warns, never blocks (H-10). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` split profiles are honoured exactly as today, which is how a user keeps a work profile out of a personal user run.

## 4. Targets: user-level instruction files and skills

**What each harness loads at user level.** Verified on this machine where noted; the rest must be confirmed against the harness before it becomes a target (and pinned by a fixture, as adapters are).

| Harness | Always-loaded user file | User-level skills | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE.md`) | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | present here; Peter's setup |
| Codex | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | `~/.codex/skills/` | both present here; confirm Codex's skill discovery order (`~/.codex/skills` vs `~/.agents/skills`) |
| cross-harness convention | none | `~/.agents/skills/` | present here, mirrored to `~/.claude/skills`; the user-level twin of `.agents/skills` |
| OpenCode | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` | `~/.config/opencode/skills/` (to verify) | file present here |
| Pi | to verify | `~/.pi/agent/skills/` | skills dir present here |
| Grok, Cursor CLI, Hermes | to verify | to verify | not in the first cut |

**Memory file resolution.** Reuse `resolveMemoryFiles` with an ordered `user.memoryFiles` list, default `["~/.claude/CLAUDE.md", "~/.codex/AGENTS.md", "~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md"]`: the first existing file is canonical, pointers are fine, a second full file is warned about each run exactly as today. `isPointerTo` needs to accept absolute and `~/` import targets (Claude Code's `@path` import supports them), so a user who wants one source of truth can make `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` a pointer. Whether Codex or OpenCode support an import is an open question; until then a multi-harness user gets the same "separate file, not updated" warning a divergent repo gets.

**Skills.** `user.skillsDirs` default `["~/.agents/skills", "~/.claude/skills", "~/.codex/skills"]`, deduplicated by realpath as `resolveProjectSkillDirs` does. The overflow target for extractions (`resolveOverflowTarget` equivalent): `~/.agents/skills` with the `~/.claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills` symlink when `~/.claude/skills` is missing or already that symlink; when `~/.claude/skills` is a real directory (Peter's case, and most Claude Code users), write extractions **there** rather than warning, because a skill only counts if a harness loads it and that is the directory Claude Code loads. Configurable via `user.skillsDir`.

**Attribution to a specific user-level file or skill.** The mechanism is the one that exists: `parseMemoryUnits` gives the user file `AG-nnn` ids; the analysis prompt is the same template with `MEMORY_PATH` = `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and `SKILLS` = the user skill index; positive/negative evidence attaches to `AG-nnn`; a gap a user skill's content covers cites `coveredBySkill`, and the fold turns corroborated citations into a failed-trigger edit on that skill's `description:` line. Distillation keeps one line per tool call, so a Claude Code `Skill` invocation carrying the skill name is visible to the analysis model and quotable. Phase 2 adds stable `SK-<name>` ids for skill descriptions so positive/negative evidence can attach to a skill that *was* in play and the fold can report per-skill relevance; this is a general improvement that helps project scope equally.

**Budget.** `user.budgetTokens` (default 5000) gates the user surface: user memory file plus every user skill description line, measured the same way (`skillDescriptionTokens`, `budgetStatus`). A project session actually pays user file + project file + both skill layers; each scope gates its own share and the banner says which surface it measures. A user file that starts over budget makes the first runs shrink plans, which is the design working and must be printed as such.

**Safe apply.** `src/apply/writer.js` stays the only writer. Every existing gate applies unchanged: memory-file hash freshness (`memoryFileSnapshot`), `targetFiles` hash freshness for every skill file, `budgetGateKind` on the accepted subset, whole-or-nothing composition per file, created targets must be absent, skills before the memory file, rollback on failure. Added for user scope because the targets are outside git:

- `--scope user` is required on `apply` as on every other command; nothing about a project run can reach a user file.
- **Pre-image backups.** Before the first write, copy each file to `<state>/backups/<ISO-timestamp>/<path>` and print the restore path. `git diff` is not available for `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; this is the equivalent safety net, written by the same module.
- **Dotfile-managed targets.** When the resolved target is a symlink into a read-only store (home-manager/nix, chezmoi, stow), `atomicReplace` already fails and rolls back; the failure message should name the link target and say "edit the source that generates it". On this machine the Claude, Codex, and OpenCode user files and skills dirs are such symlinks, so this is not hypothetical.
- `--dry-run` prints the full unified diff per file. The Lavish surface and `--no-ui` review are unchanged, one card per edit with quotes and sources, and rejections are remembered per scope.

## 5. Attribution and conflict: project vs user

A run writes only its own scope, so the conflict is about **where evidence is counted**, not where writes go. Three rules, the first two enforced in code, the third prompt guidance (the same status the >= 20% placement table has today, by the captain's earlier decision).

**Rule 1 (code): a user-level addition needs `minGapProjects` distinct projects.** Every gap observation in user scope carries the session's project key; `clusterGapObservations` counts `projects` per cluster alongside `sessions`; eligibility for synthesis is `sessions >= minGapEvidence && projects >= minGapProjects` (default 2). A cluster that clears the session bar in a single project is **report-only**, labelled "project-specific: seen in `<project>` only; run `backpass` there". This is the direct answer to H-8's own observation that a gap corroborating across repos is "by definition not repo-specific", turned into a gate rather than a router.

**Rule 2 (code): a sighting the session's project already covers is not a user gap.** When the session's cwd still resolves to a checkout with a memory file, its instruction units are loaded and the gap's `proposedInstruction` is checked against them with the existing `GAP_COVERED_THRESHOLD` similarity (`reanchor` bar, Dice >= 0.6). A covered sighting is recorded as project-covered and does not count toward the user cluster. The same check in reverse runs in project scope once the user index is rendered read-only (Phase 2): a gap the user file already covers becomes `non-compliance` against that user instruction, never a project gap.

**Rule 3 (prompt): project wins whenever the text names a project artifact.** The user-scope synthesis prompt says: a rule that names a path, command, service, or convention specific to one repository belongs in that repository's memory file, whatever its session count; write it at user level only as a general rule that would hold in a third unrelated project. Removals at user level need harm from `minGapEvidence` sessions **and** `minGapProjects` projects; harm concentrated in one project is reported as "add a project-level exception in `<project>`", not as a global deletion.

**Per-project relevance.** The fold already splits relevance by interactive vs non-interactive so a robot-heavy corpus cannot hide a category signal. User scope adds the same split by project (top-k projects plus "other"), so an instruction that is 80% relevant in one repo and 0% elsewhere reads as project-shaped: an extraction candidate (narrow, detectable trigger) or a "belongs in that project" note, never a broad user-level rule.

**Read-only cross-scope context (Phase 2).** Project scope renders the user file's units as `UG-nnn` and user skills as context, so a project run stops proposing what the user layer already says and can report "failed trigger of user skill X: fix at user level with `backpass --scope user`". User scope renders the current project file of the session's cwd as `PG-nnn` context per analysis call (only when the checkout still exists, capped by tokens). Both are context, never targets, and both cost prompt tokens, so both are opt-in until measured.

## 6. CLI and UX

```
backpass [scan|analyze|propose|apply|status|init] --scope <project|user>   [project]
backpass --scope user                 full pass over the user surface; never writes
backpass scan --scope user            per-harness table + PROJECT column + per-project summary
backpass apply --scope user           review and write; backups + dotfile-target check
backpass init --scope user            write the `user` block into ~/.config/backpass/config.json,
                                      create ~/.local/state/backpass/user/ (0700)
```

- `--scope` is a flag on every command, not a subcommand (project memory: never a multi-word subcommand). Default `project`, so today's behaviour is untouched. In user scope the cwd need not be a git checkout; if it is, a one-line info says the repo is not a target in this scope.
- Config, `user` block of `~/.config/backpass/config.json`:

```json
{
  "user": {
    "memoryFiles": ["~/.claude/CLAUDE.md", "~/.codex/AGENTS.md", "~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md"],
    "skillsDir": "~/.agents/skills",
    "skillsDirs": ["~/.agents/skills", "~/.claude/skills", "~/.codex/skills"],
    "budgetTokens": 5000,
    "minGapEvidence": 2,
    "minGapProjects": 2,
    "discovery": {
      "harnesses": ["claude", "codex", "pi", "opencode", "grok", "cursor", "hermes"],
      "since": "30d",
      "includeProjects": [],
      "excludeProjects": [],
      "maxTranscriptsPerProject": null
    }
  }
}
```

- Output: the banner reads `backpass v0.1.x · user scope · ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md + skill descriptions · 100 of 1,204 sessions across 37 projects · since 30d`. The proposal line per edit gains `projects=N` next to `transcripts`. The apply surface and `--no-ui` review show `sessions · projects` per card. `backpass status --scope user` shows the user budget bar, evidence counts, and the cross-surface overlap report. `--json` gains `scope` and `projects` fields. Training-loop vocabulary (collect samples, calculate loss, aggregate gradients, gradient descent) is unchanged; the only new user-facing words are "user scope" and "project scope".
- Failure text follows the existing rule of naming the fix: `no user memory file found (looked for ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ...)` with `set user.memoryFiles in ~/.config/backpass/config.json`; a read-only target names the link and its source.

## 7. Phased plan

**Phase 0 - decision, no code.** Amend `VISION.md` and record the ruling in `VISION-ANSWERS.md` (section 8). Without this, every reviewer of the implementation PR is entitled to reject it on the resist test.

**Phase 1 - smallest useful cut: Claude Code + Codex, full pipeline, all gates.**

- `src/scope.js` (new): `resolveScope(cwd, flags, config)` returning `{ kind: "project", repo, root, name, stateDir, memoryFiles, skillDirs, overflowDir, associate }` or the `user` equivalent. `src/cli.js` builds the scope once and passes it where `repo` goes today; `State` takes a directory. The roughly 40 `repo.root`/`repo.name` sites become `scope.root`/`scope.name`; `REPO_ROOT` in the synthesis prompts becomes a grounding-roots list (the top project roots of the sample) in user scope.
- `src/discovery/index.js`: association by `scope.associate`; user scope stamps `project` on each transcript. Evidence records gain `transcript.cwd` and `transcript.project` (also useful in project scope).
- `src/discovery/self.js`: cwd-under-state-dir exclusion.
- `src/memory.js`: `~/` and absolute import targets in `isPointerTo`; `readMemoryFile` accepts absolute paths.
- `src/skills.js`: user skill roots and the overflow rule from section 4.
- `src/fold.js`, `src/gap-ledger.js`: `projects` per cluster, `minGapProjects` gate, project-covered sightings (Rule 2), per-project relevance split.
- `src/proposal.js`: `projects` on each edit; the annotate schema gains `projects`; gate text names the floor.
- `src/apply/writer.js`: root from scope, pre-image backups, dotfile-target message.
- `src/config.js`: `user` block and validation; `backpass init --scope user`.
- Tests, all offline: `resolveScope` fixtures; user-scope discovery over the existing `test/fixtures/claude-session.jsonl` and `codex-rollout.jsonl` with differing cwds; fold `minGapProjects` and project-covered cases; writer against a temp home with a symlinked read-only target; `sample` per-project cap. Every test exercises a public interface and asserts behaviour, per the repo's test rule.

**Phase 2.** Project-aware sampling allocation; read-only cross-scope context (`UG-nnn` in project scope, `PG-nnn` in user scope); `SK-<name>` ids and per-skill relevance; `backpass status --scope user` overlap report between the user file and each project file (a project file restating a user rule is a project-level shrink candidate).

**Phase 3.** Remaining harness user surfaces (Pi, OpenCode, Grok, Cursor CLI, Hermes), each verified against the harness and pinned by a fixture; multi-machine pooling of derived evidence, which the vision already allows as a change of scale.

**Risks.**

- A large user file makes the first runs shrink plans and the analysis prompt heavier; the budget gate and banner must make that legible rather than surprising.
- Quote concentration across all projects in one state dir; mitigated by 0700, `excludeProjects`, and the scan preflight, but it is a real change in blast radius and should be said in the README.
- Cross-project paraphrase makes the consolidation call (`src/consolidate.js`) see more diverse phrasings; keep its "when unsure, do not merge" rule and watch merge rates on production ledgers before loosening anything.
- Dotfile-managed user files will refuse to apply on many power users' machines (this one included); the fix is a named message, not a workaround.
- Harness user-level layouts are less documented than project layouts and drift the same way transcripts do; each target needs the fixture-and-fail-soft treatment adapters get.

## 8. Relationship to VISION.md and H-8

H-8 proposed that a **project** run write to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when a gap corroborated across N repos. It was ruled off mission because a global file "has no repo to scope evidence to and no owner in the sense the design assumes, and one wrong instruction pollutes every project at once", with the author's reasoning that global memory is handwritten preference, "for now".

This proposal differs in three ways that address each half of that reasoning:

1. **Ownership and intent.** The user names the user surface as the target with `--scope user`; a project run never touches it. The user file is treated as *that user's weights*, which is what it already is for Peter: he keeps everything there, so for him "anything learned belongs in project memory" has no project file to land in. `VISION.md` already says "choosing how their own weights get updated is the human in control, but that is an explicit choice and never a default" (H-3); this is that clause applied to which file is the weights.
2. **Evidence scope.** The `minGapProjects` gate gives the global file a scoping rule stronger than the project file's: not only two sessions, but two projects. A project-specific rule cannot clear it. The pollution risk H-8 named is the thing Rule 1 refuses.
3. **Skills are the main target, not the instruction file.** Peter's user-level *skills* are exactly what the failed-trigger mechanism exists to tune. The "handwritten preference" framing describes `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` well and `~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` poorly: a skill's description is a trigger condition, and a trigger that failed in two projects is a defect with evidence, not a preference.

Proposed amendment, for the captain to accept, edit, or refuse: the opener's "a person's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is handwritten preference, and anything learned belongs in project memory instead" becomes "By default the project file is the one it trains. A person's user-level surface (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, user-level skills) is a target only when they name it as the scope of a run, and a rule reaches it only with evidence from more than one project." The Scope non-goal changes from "It does not train a person's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`" to "It never writes a user-level file from a project-scoped run." A new `VISION-ANSWERS.md` entry (H-13, "A user-level scope for a user whose weights live at `~/.claude`") records the ruling and this issue as its evidence base. The resist tests are unchanged: nothing here widens what writes without an explicit scope, lowers the two-session bar, or makes anything but per-edit review the default.

## 9. Open questions

1. Vision: accept the amendment in section 8, edit it, or keep H-8 as is (which closes this issue)?
2. Canonical user memory file when several harness files exist: first-existing with divergence warnings (as proposed), or one run per harness file with sessions filtered by harness?
3. `minGapProjects` default: 2 (proposed) or 3?
4. Should project scope render the user-level index read-only by default once Phase 2 lands, or stay behind a flag because of prompt cost?
5. State location: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/backpass/user/` (proposed) or under `~/.config/backpass/`?
6. Pre-image backups for non-git targets: keep forever, prune by count, or leave to the user?
7. Extraction target when `~/.claude/skills` is a real directory: write there (proposed) or insist on `~/.agents/skills` plus a warning as project scope does?
8. Which harnesses support an import/pointer in their user file, so one canonical user file can serve several harnesses?

title: docs: make VISION.md the single alignment surface

## Intent Fold backpass's VISION-ANSWERS.md into VISION.md and delete it, so VISION.md is the single vision-alignment surface. CAPTAIN DIRECTION (2026-09-02): VISION.md should contain the key principles, enough to run the accept/resist test on its own; no hypotheticals record. title: fix(acpx): send --agent session prompts through the prompt subcommand
body:
## Intent Fix kunchenguid/backpass so a pinned grok synthesis (or analysis) agent works through acpx, and ship it upstream as a PR from the 1955m GitHub account. backpass propose with synthesis.agent = grok fails every time with `acpx grok session prompt failed (exit 2)`. For grok, src/harness-invoke.js (grokInvocation) always routes through acpx's `--agent ` escape hatch (a generated argv wrapper around `grok ... agent stdio`), because synthesis needs write access and/or a model or effort override. In src/acpx.js, openSession()'s prompt() builds `acpx [globals] --agent -s --file `. acpx 0.13.1 and 0.13.2 both reject that for a raw `--agent` command: `[acpx] error: USAGE error: unknown option '-s'` (exit 2). Built-in agents (`acpx codex -s ... --file ...`) accept it, which is why codex/claude analysis works and grok does not. The working form is the explicit prompt subcommand: `acpx [globals] --agent prompt -s --file ` returns the model's answer (exit 0). Verified with `acpx --cwd --approve-reads --non-interactive-permissions deny --timeout 120 --format quiet --agent "grok -m grok-4.6 agent stdio" prompt -s --file `. `acpx codex prompt --help` documents `-s, --session ` and `-f, --file ` as options of `prompt`. `acpx --agent ... sessions new --name ` and `acpx --agent ... sessions close ` already work (they are subcommands), so only the prompt call is wrong. Requirements (current accepted form): 1. In src/acpx.js prompt(): emit the prompt subcommand when the invocation uses acpxAgentCommand (the --agent escape hatch). Decide, with evidence from `acpx codex prompt --help` and a live check, whether using prompt unconditionally for built-in agents is also correct; prefer the smallest change that is correct for both, and explain the choice in a short code comment (what and why, no chatter). 2. Check the other -s-before-subcommand calls in openSession() (set-mode, set) for the same escape-hatch problem. grok currently sets neither sessionMode nor setEffortKey, so they may be unreachable for grok today; fix them only if the same bug is reachable, and say so either way in the PR body. 3. Add a regression test in test/harness-invoke.test.js (it already fakes acpx and asserts argv shapes for openSession/sessionPrompt): a grok session prompt must pass prompt before -s; a built-in agent's argv must keep whatever shape is settled on. Keep tests offline and fixture-based. 4. Keep README.md accurate if any user-facing wording about grok/acpx changes. Do not touch CHANGELOG.md or .release-please-manifest.json: CI rejects that. 5. Conventional-commit message, because release-please cuts releases from it, e.g. `fix(acpx): send --agent session prompts through the prompt subcommand`. Mention the exact acpx error and versions in the body. Do not open the PR manually. The repo gate requires the no-mistakes attestation in the PR body. Submit with git push no-mistakes; the pipeline creates/updates the PR against upstream main. The code fix is already on branch fm/backpass-grok-acpx. PR https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/pull/100 is open against kunchenguid/backpass from fork 1955m/backpass. HEAD is e6a99ae (pipeline follow-up "no-mistakes: apply CI fixes"); the original fix is d560997. Remaining required author action: run a new no-mistakes validation so the pipeline rewrites the PR body with an attestation bound to the resulting HEAD. The current PR body attestation is bound to d560997 while HEAD is e6a99ae; the Require no-mistakes workflow does not re-fire on synchronize. Do not add further code, do not open another PR, do not reply to the maintainer comment. git push no-mistakes reported Everything up-to-date on the unchanged head, so use the documented rerun path rather than inventing a change. ## What Changed - Emit the explicit `prompt` subcommand before `-s` in `openSession().prompt()` when the invocation uses acpx's `--agent` escape hatch (`acpxAgentCommand`), fixing Grok synthesis/analysis failures where acpx 0.13.1/0.13.2 rejected `unknown option '-s'` (exit 2). Built-in agents keep the implicit `acpx codex -s ... --file ...` form. - Add offline regression tests that assert Grok argv includes `prompt` before `-s` and built-in codex argv omits the subcommand; the fake acpx shim mirrors the acpx 0.13.x `-s` rejection for `--agent` without `prompt`. - Document the `--agent` prompt shape in AGENTS.md. The `set-mode` and `set` paths in `openSession()` use the same `-s`-before-subcommand shape but are unchanged: Grok's `grokInvocation` never sets `sessionMode` or `setEffortKey`, so those calls are unreachable for Grok today. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The fix is a single conditional argv insertion gated on the existing `acpxAgentCommand` flag (only set for grok overlays), preserves the working built-in-agent path, and is covered by behavioral regression tests through the public `openSession`/`prompt` API. ## Testing Ran the new harness-invoke regression tests plus four related grok harness tests (all passed), reproduced the acpx 0.13.2 `unknown option '-s'` failure on the pre-fix argv shape and confirmed the fixed shape passes usage parsing (reaches session lookup), and captured emitted argv showing grok uses `--agent ... prompt -s ...` while codex keeps `codex -s ...` without a prompt subcommand.

title: feat: add user-level memory scope
body:
## Intent Phase 1 of issue #97: smallest useful cut of --scope user. A run is exactly one scope, chosen by --scope; default stays project. User scope discovers Claude and Codex sessions across projects, excludes self-sessions, and edits only user-level memory files and skills. Project-scope fixture behavior must stay unchanged. No cross-scope writes. User state is ~/.config/backpass/user/ (mode 0700, honour XDG_CONFIG_HOME), isolated from every project's .backpass/ (evidence, ledgers, rejections, apply surfaces). Apply refuses a symlink into a read-only store with the named message: "{absolute} is a symlink to {real}, which is not writable; edit the source that generates it". Captain answers on issue #97 (2026-09-02): (1) vision already amended in Phase 0 (H-13; H-8 stays off-mission for a project-scoped write to a user-level file); (2) canonical user memory is first-existing with divergence warnings; (3) minGapProjects default 1 so the gate exists but cross-project corroboration is not required, and section 8's "more than one project" is not folded into VISION.md; (4) isolate project vs user state as much as possible; (5) user state under ~/.config/backpass/, not XDG_STATE_HOME; (6) pre-image backups follow project scope (atomicReplace + rollback only, no new backup dir); (7) extraction target follows project (.agents/skills plus a warning if .claude/skills is a real directory); (8) AGENTS.md is canonical; CLAUDE.md may be a pointer (verified: Claude Code inlines @ imports including ~/ and absolute; Codex follows AGENTS.md and is not assumed to honour @ imports). Captain 2026-09-02 (containment): no hard containment; edit scope is instruction-based. Do not add a write allowlist, deny-default sandbox, or further OS containment machinery for the user-scope synthesis invariant. Out of scope for this PR: Phase 2/3 (cross-scope UG/PG ids, SK ids, status overlap report, other harness user surfaces, multi-machine pooling). Tests must be offline and behavioral. Required coverage: resolveScope fixtures; user discovery over existing claude/codex fixtures with differing cwds; fold minGapProjects + project-covered; writer vs temp home + read-only symlink; sample per-project cap. ## What Changed - Add `--scope user` across the CLI to manage canonical user memory and skills with isolated, XDG-aware state. - Discover Claude and Codex sessions across projects with project filters, self-session exclusion, sticky per-project sampling, and project-aware gap folding. - Keep writes scoped to the selected surface, support user memory pointers and relocated skill directories, and refuse read-only symlink targets with actionable errors. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The implementation matches the stated Phase 1 scope and prior decisions, with no material source-verifiable defects found. ## Testing Targeted behavioral tests and an end-to-end CLI scan validated user-scope resolution, cross-project Claude/Codex discovery, self-session exclusion, per-project sampling, project coverage and gap gating, isolated 0700 state, relocated memory and skills, scope-safe apply, and the named read-only symlink refusal. The reviewer-visible CLI transcript confirms the intended user experience and state isolation. No visual UI changed, so screenshot evidence was not applicable.
Evidence: End-to-end user-scope scan across two projects with state isolation checks Source: [End-to-end user-scope scan across two projects with state isolation checks](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/blob/fe9c8f6eef659cafbd60374c79eef3bc095829aa/.no-mistakes/evidence/fm/backpass-user-level-scope-p1-r1/user-scope-scan.txt) ```text COMMAND: backpass scan --scope user --since all --harness claude,codex user scope: this checkout is not a write target; edits go to the user-level memory file and skills user scope · since all HARNESS SCANNED MATCHED SELF CACHED NOTE claude 1 1 0 0 codex 1 1 0 0 2 transcript(s) across 2 project(s) · tier1 2 (git) · tier2 0 (remote) · tier3 0 (cwd) · interactive 0 · non-interactive 2 HARNESS SESSION KIND WHEN SIZE TIER PROJECT codex aaaa-bbbb non-interactive today 2KB t1 ~/.no-mistakes/worktrees/26c81f7411 claude 11111111-222 non-interactive today 2KB t1 ~/.no-mistakes/worktrees/26c81f7411 STATE DIRECTORY MODE: 700 ~/.no-mistakes/worktrees/26c81f74111f/01M1GP6BEEPGHNQ6Y3EEG6GAC9/.test-user-scope-e2e/home/xdg/backpass/user PROJECT .backpass DIRECTORIES CREATED: none ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
✅ **intent** - passed ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
🔧 **Review** - 4 issues found → auto-fixed (7) ✅ - 🚨 `src/subprocess.js:121` - The intent explicitly says: "no hard containment" and "Do not add a write allowlist, deny-default sandbox, or further OS containment machinery." This branch adds sandbox-exec/bubblewrap launch policy and wires it into user synthesis. It also withholds grounding paths when containment is unavailable. Revert this pipeline-added containment machinery and retain instruction-based edit scope only. - 🚨 `src/analyze.js:249` - Fresh cached evidence updates only `interaction`, leaving the newly significant `project`, `projectRoot`, `cwd`, and association fields stale. For example, analyze a Codex session while its checkout is absent, then restore that checkout with project memory covering the gap: discovery finds the live root, but fold receives the cached null `projectRoot` and incorrectly counts the covered gap. Refresh the non-judgment transcript metadata from the current descriptor whenever cached evidence is reused. - 🚨 `src/scope.js:65` - Live sessions use each git worktree path as `project`, while deleted sessions use a normalized remote. Two worktrees of one repository therefore count as two projects at `fold.js:343`, incorrectly satisfying `minGapProjects=2` and independently evading the per-project sample cap. Establish a stable repository identity at the user-association boundary, using normalized live remotes when available and a path fallback only when no repository identity exists. - 🚨 `src/state.js:55` - The required criterion says user state is mode 0700, but `ensure()` creates it with the process default mode and silently continues when chmod fails. A filesystem or permission state that rejects chmod therefore leaves evidence, prompts, proposals, and apply surfaces under a potentially broader directory mode. Create with 0700 and fail clearly if the existing directory cannot be secured rather than treating the requirement as best effort. 🔧 Fix: Refresh cached associations and unify worktree project identity 2 errors still open: - 🚨 `src/state.js:55` - Intent requires user state to be mode 0700, but the directory is initially created with the process default mode and chmod failures are silently ignored. It can therefore remain broadly readable while holding evidence, prompts, proposals, and apply surfaces. Create it with mode 0700 and fail clearly if an existing directory cannot be secured. - 🚨 `src/scope.js:72` - The worktree-identity fix still uses each toplevel path when a repository has no remote. Two worktrees of the same local repository therefore receive different project keys, can independently evade maxTranscriptsPerProject, and can incorrectly satisfy minGapProjects=2. At the association boundary, use the shared git-common-dir identity before falling back to the worktree path. 🔧 Fix: Unify local worktrees by shared Git identity 3 errors still open: - 🚨 `src/subprocess.js:106` - The authoritative intent says "no hard containment" and explicitly forbids "a write allowlist, deny-default sandbox, or further OS containment machinery." This change adds sandbox-exec/bubblewrap probing and launch policies at lines 106-174, then conditionally withholds grounding paths in synthesis. Revert this pipeline-added machinery to the smallest instruction-based edit-scope implementation required by the intent. - 🚨 `src/state.js:55` - Intent requires user state to be mode 0700, but ensure() creates it with the process default mode and silently ignores chmod failure. The directory can therefore remain broadly accessible while holding evidence, prompts, proposals, and apply surfaces. Create it with mode 0700 and fail clearly if an existing directory cannot be secured. - 🚨 `src/apply/writer.js:581` - With CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/custom/claude, discovery and synthesis correctly use /custom/claude/skills, but applying an extraction still calls ensureSkillsLayout(repo.root), which creates ~/.claude/skills rather than /custom/claude/skills. The new skill lands in ~/.agents/skills and remains invisible to relocated Claude. Pass the configured Claude skills location through the apply layout boundary and create or validate its link to the canonical directory. 🔧 Fix: Link relocated Claude skills during user apply 4 issues (3 errors, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `src/state.js:55` - The required user-state mode is not enforced. `ensure()` creates the directory with the process default mode and silently ignores `chmod` failure, so evidence, prompts, proposals, and apply surfaces can remain accessible beyond mode 0700. Create with mode 0700 and fail clearly when an existing directory cannot be secured. - 🚨 `src/repo.js:145` - Live repositories use the lexicographically first of every configured remote, while deleted Codex sessions use their single recorded `git.repository_url`. In a fork checkout with `origin=user/fork` and `upstream=org/repo`, live and deleted sessions from the same repository can receive different project keys, bypass the per-project cap, and incorrectly satisfy `minGapProjects=2`. Establish one identity compatible with the recorded remote at this association boundary, such as preferring the repository's authoritative origin before other remotes. - 🚨 `src/skills.js:75` - Skill resolution always injects `.claude/skills`, even when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` relocates Claude and `extraDirs` contains the actual directory. An old default skill can therefore affect budgets, be reported as covering a gap, or be edited even though the active Claude installation cannot load it. User scope should resolve exactly its configured harness skill roots rather than unconditionally adding the default Claude root. - ⚠️ `src/apply/writer.js:291` - User apply assumes `skillsDirs[1]` is Claude's directory, but validation and documentation expose `skillsDirs` as a general path list with no positional contract. Reordering or prepending a custom directory can make apply create a symlink at the wrong user path while leaving relocated Claude disconnected. Persist or otherwise carry the semantic Claude skills target instead of inferring it from list position; adding that explicit persisted contract needs authorization. 🔧 Fix: Enforce user state, project identity, and skill roots 2 issues (1 error, 1 warning) still open: - 🚨 `src/apply/writer.js:53` - The required named symlink refusal checks only whether the resolved file is writable. If the source file is mode 0644 but its containing store directory is not writable, this check passes, then atomicReplace cannot create its temporary sibling and returns a generic write error instead of the required message. Check writability needed by the actual replacement operation, including the resolved target's parent directory, before applying. - ⚠️ `src/fold.js:386` - With minGapProjects=3 and an eligible gap observed in two projects, projectSpecificNote selects the first project and reports `seen in <project> only`, incorrectly hiding the second project. Report the actual project count or list rather than claiming a single-project observation. 🔧 Fix: Detect read-only symlink stores and report project counts 1 error still open: - 🚨 `src/subprocess.js:43` - Authoritative intent says: "no hard containment; edit scope is instruction-based" and "Do not add a write allowlist, deny-default sandbox, or further OS containment machinery." This hunk routes synthesis subprocesses through the new sandbox-exec/bubblewrap policy in `readOnlyLaunch`, with `src/synthesize.js:450-574` probing and supplying grounding roots. Revert this prior fixer machinery and retain the required instruction-based edit scope. 🔧 Fix: Remove forbidden synthesis OS containment 3 issues (1 error, 2 warnings) still open: - 🚨 `src/workspace.js:102` - Skill membership is checked with hard-coded "/" separators. On Windows, an external CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CODEX_HOME produces logical paths such as `C:\cfg\skills\db\SKILL.md`, which do not start with `C:\cfg\skills/`. Changes to relocated existing skills are therefore silently classified as stray and omitted from proposals. Use path-relative component checks or normalize both paths before comparison. - ⚠️ `src/config.js:371` - `init --scope user` persists the currently derived memoryFiles and skillsDirs. After initializing under defaults, running with CODEX_HOME or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocated still uses the stored default memory and skill paths, while discovery follows the new environment. This can analyze relocated sessions against inactive memory. Keep environment-derived defaults implicit in the generated user block so explicit user configuration can still override them. - ⚠️ `src/proposal.js:517` - The minGapProjects proposal gate runs whenever the config contains the field, regardless of scope, although folding enables it only for user scope and the CLI documents it as user-only. A project config or `backpass --min-gap-projects 2` admits a one-project gap during folding and then repeatedly rejects its addition during synthesis. Gate project counts only when `scope.kind === "user"`, or reject the flag in project scope. 🔧 Fix: Fix Windows skill paths and scope-specific defaults ✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `node --test test/scope.test.js test/user-discovery.test.js test/fold.test.js test/user-apply.test.js test/sample.test.js test/config.test.js test/skills.test.js test/workspace.test.js test/proposal.test.js` - `node --test test/memory-resolution.test.js test/gap-ledger.test.js test/synthesize.test.js` - `node --test test/adapters.test.js test/association.test.js test/repo.test.js test/self-session.test.js test/sibling-clone-discovery.test.js` - Created isolated Claude and Codex fixture stores pointing to two live git projects, then ran `node bin/backpass.js scan --scope user --since all --harness claude,codex` with isolated `HOME` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. - Verified the CLI reported two transcripts across two projects, created user state with mode 0700, and created no project `.backpass` directories. - Removed the temporary `.test-user-scope-e2e` fixture and confirmed the worktree remained clean.
