title: feat: index direct task and steering instructions
body:
## Intent

Backpass indexes only project memory files as instruction sources, yet in measured sessions nearly half of the instructions that governed agent behaviour came from the initial task message or later user steering, which Backpass shows only as undifferentiated transcript evidence. This change makes direct task and steering instructions addressable as instruction sources with stable IDs and source, turn, authority, and lifetime metadata, referencing transcript text already sent rather than duplicating it, while keeping quoted transcripts, tool results, and assistant restatements as evidence rather than authority.

## What Changed

- Index direct user instructions as `TASK-1` and `STEER-<turn>` sources with authority and lifetime metadata, referencing existing trace text without duplication.
- Exclude fenced blocks, blockquotes, assistant messages, and tool results from instruction authority; flag truncated turns and unstable IDs from partial transcripts.
- Accept directive citations in analysis while keeping memory scores separate and preserving recurring gaps. Invalidate older analysis caches and add documentation and regression coverage.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The changes preserve the approved provenance boundaries and cache invalidation, with no new material defects found across the affected flows.

## Testing

Focused executable tests and isolated real CLI/model runs passed all eight scenarios. Setup lock, permission and adapter issues were resolved. CLI transcripts, generated prompts and persisted outputs were captured; fixtures were removed. No rendered UI changed, so screenshots were unnecessary.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 8 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Analyze and append a session: task and steering retain IDs, authority, turn references and lifetimes without duplicating instruction text. | ✅ pass | live | Generated instruction indexes: basic and basic after append |
| Analyze quoted, pasted, assistant and tool instructions: only authoritative user envelopes receive IDs, including adversarial list-marker and mixed-tab fences. | ✅ pass | live | Generated instruction indexes: authority, backtick and tilde; Real model directive citations |
| Analyze oversized messages: clamping preserves envelope extraction and warns when instruction text requires the raw transcript. | ✅ pass | live | Generated instruction indexes: clamped and clamp-fence |
| Analyze a capped trace: omitted turns are marked elided rather than falsely referenced as visible. | ✅ pass | live | Generated instruction indexes: elided |
| Analyze a log exceeding 64 MiB: discard task authority and persist retained steering IDs as partial and unstable. | ✅ pass | live | Persisted partial-transcript metadata |
| Complete model-backed analysis: retain TASK-1 and STEER-3 citations with quoted evidence, while storing directive metadata without envelope text. | ✅ pass | live | Real model directive citations |
| Rerun analysis: reuse version 10 evidence and reanalyze version 9 evidence. | ✅ pass | live | Version 10 cache reuse; Version 9 cache invalidation |
| Generate a proposal: exclude directive citations from memory-instruction rows, retain gap sightings and withhold uncorroborated singleton edits. | ✅ pass | live | Aggregated evidence; Generated proposal |

title: Support nested AGENTS.md in monorepos (train per-directory memory files from the sessions that worked there)
body:
## Problem

In a monorepo, agent memory is layered: a root `AGENTS.md` plus nested ones such as `apps/api/AGENTS.md` or `apps/mobile/AGENTS.md`, which harnesses load only when the session works under that directory. Those nested files carry most of the app-specific guidance, and they drift the same way the root file does.

Today backpass trains exactly one file per repo. `memoryFiles` is a fallback list: `resolveMemoryFiles` (src/memory.js) takes the first existing entry as `primary`, and every other entry is reported as `separate` and never updated, with a warning asking to consolidate. That is the right behavior for the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md pair, but it means listing nested files in `memoryFiles` does not train them.

## Workarounds and why they fall short

- `--target <file>` or `--memory-file apps/api/AGENTS.md` trains one nested file per run, but the loss signal is still every session in the repo. Lessons from frontend or root-level work become candidate edits for the backend file, so the gradient is noisy and the human gate at `apply` has to reject more.
- Training only the root file pushes app-specific lessons into the always-loaded root, which is exactly the token tax nested files exist to avoid.

## Proposal

1. Treat nested memory files as additional weights, not fallbacks. For example, a `nestedMemoryFiles` list, or auto-discovery of `**/AGENTS.md` below the root while keeping the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md pointer logic per directory.
2. Attribute each transcript to the directories it actually worked in, using file paths from its tool calls (reads, edits, cwd). Feed a nested file only the evidence from sessions that touched its subtree. Root keeps cross-cutting evidence.
3. Route each proposed edit to the most specific file that owns the evidence. Something general across several apps goes to root; something confined to `apps/api` goes to `apps/api/AGENTS.md`.
4. Apply a budget per file, with an optional smaller default for nested files, since a session in `apps/api` loads root plus nested.
5. Keep one proposal and one `apply` review surface covering every file, with each edit labeled by its target file.

The existing rules carry over unchanged: two-session verbatim evidence, the token budget, and `apply` as the only writer.

## Context

Observed on a pnpm/turbo monorepo with a root AGENTS.md and about five per-app AGENTS.md files (each with a CLAUDE.md symlink). backpass 0.1.28.

title: feat: train named nested memory files in monorepos

Context needed to read the ask: the PR implements upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/158, "Support nested AGENTS.md in monorepos (train per-directory memory files from the sessions that worked there)".
The issue: in a monorepo, memory is layered (root AGENTS.md plus nested ones such as apps/api/AGENTS.md that harnesses load only when working under that directory). backpass trains one file per repo: `resolveMemoryFiles` (src/memory.js) takes the first existing `memoryFiles` entry as primary and reports every other as `separate` (never updated, with a consolidate warning), correct for the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pair but it means nested files are never trained. `--target`/`--memory-file` can name one nested file, but the evidence is still every session in the repo, so the gradient is noisy and root-only training pushes app-specific lessons into the always-loaded root. The issue proposes: nested memory files as additional weights (e.g. a `nestedMemoryFiles` list), keeping the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointer logic per directory; attributing each transcript to the directories it worked in via tool-call file paths and cwd, feeding a nested file only evidence from sessions that touched its subtree while root keeps cross-cutting evidence; routing each proposed edit to the most specific file owning the evidence; a per-file budget with an optional smaller default for nested files; one proposal and one `apply` review surface covering every file, each edit labeled by target file; two-session verbatim evidence, the token budget, and `apply` as the only writer unchanged.
The maintainer's triage comment on the issue (labeled `ready-for-pr`) sets the acceptance conditions: nested files must stay human-named weights (config list or explicit CLI name), never silent always-on `**/AGENTS.md` auto-discovery that widens writes without naming scope; evidence must be scoped per subtree and association via tool paths/cwd must stay deterministic, with anything best-effort opt-in (accuracy over coverage); keep two-session verbatim evidence, `apply` as the only writer, and per-file budget; today's "consolidate separate files" warning is the wrong diagnosis for intentional nested weights, so a fix should name the nested surface clearly; the contract class is `opt-in` if unconfigured runs keep today's single-primary behavior exactly; it is not a `restore` (single-primary plus separate warning stays intentional for the AGENTS/CLAUDE pair).

## What Changed
- Add opt-in `nestedMemoryFiles` with deterministic, subtree-scoped session attribution and routing of new instructions to the most specific named file.
- Analyze and synthesize nested files separately, with per-file budgets, while combining their edits into one proposal and apply review.
- Show nested-file status and budgets in the CLI and apply UI; preserve single-primary behavior when no nested files are configured.

🚨 High: The nested evidence-selection rule conflicts with the stated touched-subtree criterion, and two routing paths can silently select the wrong training surface.

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- **Shared cross-pass gap identity between root and nested ledgers.** Each trained file is analyzed in its own pass with its own gap ledger. Exact session-and-quote matching keeps the common case of a cross-cutting lesson out of nested passes, but two distinct lessons citing the same quote can be conflated, and a root-owned lesson can still be proposed for both the root and a nested file when the passes quote it differently. A gap identity shared across ledgers is the follow-up.
- **Per-hunk evidence for edits that add instructions for several scopes.** Routing judges an edit's additions by the combined evidence behind the edit, so a single edit adding one API-only and one web-only instruction is treated as cross-cutting. Per-hunk evidence, or requiring independently evidenced addition edits, is the follow-up.

title: Question: should a project pass treat instructions already in the user-level file as covered?
body:
## Summary

A question about intended behavior, not a bug report.

I run the project pass over several repos and the user-scope pass over `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` on the same schedule. I want cross-project rules to live once, at user level, and repo files to hold only what is specific to that repo. Reading the source, the two scopes are aware of each other in one direction only, and I would like to understand whether that is the intended discipline.

What I see in 0.1.28:

- User scope defers to project memory. `clusterGapObservations` in `src/fold.js` takes `checkProjectCoverage`, and `isProjectCoveredSighting` drops a sighting from the session and project counts when the session's own project memory file already covers it. `src/commands/propose.js` sets `checkProjectCoverage` only when the scope is `user`.
- Project scope has no equivalent check against the user-level file. Analysis and synthesis for a repo compare against that repo's memory file only.

So if a repo proposal is accepted first, the user pass stops counting those sessions and the rule tends to stay at repo level. And a repo pass can propose an instruction that the user-level file already carries, which would then be paid twice in always-loaded tokens.

## Questions

1. Is the one-directional check deliberate? VISION says learned knowledge belongs with the repo it was learned in, and that project and user evidence stay isolated so neither launders the other's corroboration. I read the project-coverage check in user scope as consistent with that. I want to confirm that the absence of the reverse check is a choice and not an omission.
2. Is the intended review discipline for someone who runs both scopes "review and apply user scope first, then reject repo edits that repeat it"? If so, I am happy with that answer and would only suggest a sentence in the README under user scope.
3. Would read-only awareness of the user-level file in a project pass, reporting a sighting as already covered rather than proposing it, be in scope? The README already describes that shape for shared skill search paths: recognized as existing, never written. It would not widen writes or lower the two-session bar. I ask rather than propose because I may be missing a reason it conflicts with evidence isolation.

## Environment

backpass 0.1.28, macOS 15, Node 22. Project scope in four repos and user scope, run sequentially from one script.

body:
## Demo ![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/backpass/rejections/demo.gif) [Full-resolution MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/backpass/rejections/demo.mp4) ## Intent Make backpass remember a rejected proposal decision (add, rewrite, or remove) by its measured gap and instruction identities, so the same decision re-proposed in different wording stays suppressed until new session evidence arrives; extract/move stay keyed by hunk only. Let the browser apply surface optionally record a rejection reason, without adding a prompt to terminal review. ## What Changed - Rejected add/rewrite/remove edits now also save their measured `gapIds` and `instructionIds` (`src/state.js`). `isRejected` suppresses a later edit with the same kind and file when either set overlaps, until the new edit has strictly more sessions behind it. Extract/move still match on the hunk key only. `buildProposal` gets `gapIds` only from exact evidence-quote matches that point to a single gap cluster, and `instructionIds` from the content hashes of the instruction units the hunks touch (`src/proposal.js`). Fold and the gap ledger now carry stable ledger ids, aliases included, through to gap clusters (`src/fold.js`, `src/gap-ledger.js`). - The browser apply surface (`templates/apply.html`) shows optional reason chips on a rejected edit (`wrong-evidence`, `already-covered`, `too-narrow`, `too-broad`, `disagree`) and adds the choice to the decision vector as `eN=rejected:`. `src/apply/lavish.js` parses it, keeps only known tokens and drops unknown ones without losing the reject. The reason passes through `cmdApply` and `applyDecisions` into the rejection entry and shows up in `--json` output as `rejectReasons`. `--no-ui` records rejections without asking for a reason. - The synthesis prompt's rejection list now shows each entry's remembered ids and reason (`renderRejections` in `src/synthesize.js`). README and AGENTS.md describe the rejection identity rules, and new tests cover proposal, fold, gap-ledger, apply-surface and synthesize. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change matches the stated intent and fixes all three round-1 findings: rejections are keyed on content hashes of instruction units instead of positional aliases, absorbed ledger aliases are included in the gap identity, and the test that matched template source text was replaced with behavioral parse/poll tests. Extract and move still match only on their hunk key, reject reasons are optional and never revive an edit, and terminal review gets no new prompt. ## Testing I ran the five changed test files (all pass) and an end-to-end script in a headless browser, using the real apply.html template and the real apply writer. title: feat(proposal): gate annotate quotes against the fold catalog and show quote context
Sessions recorded with a Windows cwd match every repo at tier 1 when backpass runs on Linux/WSL
body:
On Linux, a transcript whose `cwd` is a Windows path (e.g. `C:\work\my-repo`) is associated with **every** repo you scan, at tier 1 ("cwd is inside worktree …").

**Cause.** `associate()` in `src/discovery/association.js` resolves candidates with `realpathOrResolve()`. On Linux `C:\work\my-repo` is not absolute, so `realpathSync` throws and `path.resolve()` makes it `<process.cwd()>/C:\work\my-repo`. Backpass runs from inside the repo, so that path is under the repo's own worktree, and `isUnder()` returns true. The same happens for Codex rollouts whose `session_meta.cwd` is a Windows path.

**Repro (0.1.28, current `main`):**
1. On WSL, set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/mnt/c/Users/<you>/.claude` (or `CODEX_HOME` to the Windows Codex home) so the Windows store is collected.
2. Run `backpass scan --json` in two unrelated repos.
3. Both list the same Windows transcripts as `tier: 1, confidence: "nested"`. In our case 180 Windows sessions matched each of four repos, though they belonged to one.

**Expected.** A Windows-shaped path (`/^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]/` or UNC) should not go through POSIX `path.resolve`. Either skip tiers 1/1.5 for it, or map it with `path.win32` (optionally translating `C:\` → `/mnt/c/` under WSL) before comparing. Tier 2 (recorded remote) already attributes Codex rollouts correctly, so skipping would only lose Claude sessions from deleted Windows paths.

**Related.** Tier 3's `path.basename()` also never matches these paths, because the whole backslash path is one POSIX segment. So `worktreeGlobs` is the only way to attribute Windows Claude sessions today.

title: Analysis pass dies on one oversized transcript and does not persist partial work
body:
Running the analysis pass on a repo that contains one very large session transcript kills the pass at the same point every time, and the completed work is not persisted, so every retry repeats and re-bills it.

## Environment

- backpass 0.1.28, macOS, opencode harness, provider `opencode-go`, `jobs=4`.

## Symptom

The pass reports `analyzing 100 transcript(s)` and dies between 70 and 80, across four runs and two models (`glm-5.3`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) at both `effort=low` and `effort=max`. Three failure signatures seen:

1. `acpx opencode session prompt timed out after 300s`
2. `acpx opencode session prompt failed (exit 5): [acpx] tokens: input=1091 output=84 cache_read=53632 total=55062`
3. `Insufficient account funds`, a provider balance issue, resolved by a top up, not the cause.

## Evidence pointing at one transcript

In `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, one session holds 15,957 rows in `part`. The next largest holds 1,153. It is also the most recent session, so every recency-weighted sample of 100 includes it, and the token line shows roughly 54k tokens read for that single prompt before the session dies.

## Two asks

1. Skip a transcript above a size threshold with a note in the summary, instead of letting it crash the whole pass.
2. Persist each completed per-transcript analysis as it finishes. A failing run currently banks nothing, so the first 70 are re-analyzed and re-billed on every retry.

## Related observation

`self` detection marked 8 sessions, the children of the session that launched the scan, but not the parent session, so launching backpass from inside the oversized session does not exclude it. An `--exclude-session` flag or an ignore list would work as a workaround.

## Reproduction

`backpass scan --json` reports 271 scanned and 231 matched on this machine. A plain `backpass` then dies as above.

title: fix(acpx): retry timed-out adapter verification instead of aborting the run
body:
## Intent

Fix a run-killing misclassification in src/acpx.js verifyHarnessInvocation. Observed on a loaded macOS host (load average ~30, 6 parallel analysis jobs): one 'acpx config show --format json' call exceeded its 10s budget, run() returned code null / timedOut, and the function threw a UserError ('cannot verify acpx adapter configuration for codex: exit null' / 'upgrade acpx or omit the model and effort override'). analyze.js rethrows UserError, so the analysis pool's Promise.all rejected at 23/100 transcripts and the run ended without a proposal, with advice that cannot help (acpx 0.19.3 was current). Per this repo's own invariant that result.timedOut is handled before generic exits, a timeout now retries once with 3x the budget and, if it still times out, raises a timed-out AcpxError: the analysis stage records that transcript as failed and a later run retries it. Deliberate choices: the budget is an injectable verifyTimeoutMs option on openSession/execOneShot (default unchanged at 10s) so tests do not wait on real timeouts; non-timeout failures and the replaced-adapter refusal are unchanged; no caching of the verification was added. Two tests in test/harness-invoke.test.js drive a fake acpx whose config show hangs always / once. Full suite 740/740 locally.

## What Changed
- `verifyHarnessInvocation` (`src/acpx.js`) now treats a timed-out `acpx config show` separately from other failures. It retries once with 3× the budget. If the retry also times out, it throws a timed-out `AcpxError` tagged `stage: "verify"` instead of a run-ending `UserError`, so the analysis stage records only that transcript as failed. `openSession` and `execOneShot` take a new `verifyTimeoutMs` option (default still 10s). Non-timeout failures and the replaced-adapter refusal behave as before.
- `AgentResolver.withFallthrough` (`src/agents.js`) now lets a timed-out `AcpxError` from a pinned agent propagate unchanged, where before it was wrapped as a pinned-agent failure.
- `src/cli.js` moves top-level error printing into a new exported `reportError`. For a timed-out `AcpxError` it prints a retry hint: one wording when the adapter check timed out and another for a timed-out harness call, which also suggests raising `timeoutSeconds`. New tests cover this: a fake acpx whose `config show` hangs every time or only once (`test/harness-invoke.test.js`), the pinned-timeout case (`test/agents.test.js`) and the CLI hints (`test/cli-errors.test.js`). The branch also strips trailing whitespace from `README.md`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small and bounded. A verify timeout is retried once at three times the budget and then raised as a timed-out AcpxError, which classifyAcpxFailure leaves unclassified, so it propagates unchanged. Analysis (analyze.js:411) records it as a failed transcript and consolidation (consolidate.js:93) continues past it, while synthesis now reports it through the CLI branch with a hint that fits the timeout kind. Non-timeout and replaced-adapter paths are unchanged. The tests exercise real fake-acpx hang/retry behaviour, the pinned passthrough, and both CLI hint variants.

## Testing

I ran the four targeted test files (71/71 pass). I then drove the real backpass CLI end to end in a throwaway repo and HOME, with a scriptable fake acpx on PATH, and ran the same setup against the base commit. On base, one timed-out config show kills the run with the misleading upgrade advice. On the fix, the check is retried at 10s and then 30s, the transcript is recorded as failed, the run exits 0, and the next run analyzes it. Non-timeout failures still stop the run with the same error, and a synthesis timeout prints a clean hint with no stack trace. All six live scenarios pass. The prompt/exec timeout hint was covered only by a unit test and is marked untested for live validation. Transcripts are saved in the evidence directory and the temporary setup has been removed.

Because the remedy changes pinned-failure semantics, this needs the author's decision.
- ℹ️ `src/agents.js:523` - Side effect of the round-1 fix, which was the user's own prescribed change: the `!err.timedOut` exemption in withFallthrough covers every role, not only analysis. A pinned synthesis prompt that times out (or a pinned synthesis `config show` that times out twice) used to surface as a UserError ('pinned synthesis agent X failed unexpectedly (...timed out...)') with a retry hint. It now reaches cli.js:324 as a raw AcpxError and prints `err.stack` with no hint. Auto-picked synthesis timeouts already behaved this way, and the user explicitly asked for 'pinned and auto-picked agents alike', so this is recorded as a known trade-off, not a defect. The analysis path (analyze.js:411) and consolidation (consolidate.js:93) now fail soft as the intent requires.

🔧 Fix applied.
1 warning still open:

- ⚠️ `src/cli.js:334` - The round-2 fix added a timed-out-AcpxError branch to reportError. It always prints 'or raise timeoutSeconds in the backpass config'. One error that reaches this branch is the new verify timeout from verifyHarnessInvocation (src/acpx.js:357). That can happen when a synthesis agent's `acpx config show` times out at 10s and then at 30s. Those budgets come from VERIFY_CONFIG_TIMEOUT_MS / verifyTimeoutMs and ignore config.timeoutSeconds. Synthesis also clamps its own timeout to max(config.timeoutSeconds, 900) (src/synthesize.js:644), so raising timeoutSeconds below 900 changes nothing there either. This brings back the problem the intent names ('advice that cannot help') for this path. 'rerun to retry' is still correct. The hint wording came from the user's round-2 instruction ('for example: ...'), so check with the user before changing it. The narrowest remedy is to drop the timeoutSeconds clause, or print it only when the error is not the config-show verify timeout.

🔧 Fix applied.

title: ci: add restricted workflow_dispatch path to republish npm 0.1.29
body: GitHub release `backpass-v0.1.29` already exists, but npm never received `0.1.29` because the original publish failed on `format:check`. The tag was retargeted to `f13cc56` (the 0.1.29 release plus the README trailing-space fix). Captain sanctioned republishing `backpass@0.1.29` only. This PR adds a one-off recovery path to `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` so we can republish that existing tag via trusted publishing / provenance, without bumping the version and without creating a new release-please release. ## Behavior - Normal `push` to `main` is unchanged, except the existing `release-please` job now has `if: github.event_name == 'push'` so a dispatch cannot create a release. - `workflow_dispatch` inputs: `tag_name` (required) and `version` (required). - New `npm-republish` job runs only on `workflow_dispatch`. - Recovery is hard-allowlisted to `tag_name == backpass-v0.1.29` and `version == 0.1.29`, must be dispatched from `main`, checks out `refs/tags/${tag_name}`, and asserts `package.json` version matches the input. Anything else fails loud. - Then the same gate + publish sequence as today: pnpm/node 24 with registry-url, frozen install, lint, format:check, typecheck, test, `npm publish --access public --provenance`. - `permissions` still include `id-token: write`. No product code, README, or package version changes. ## After merge Do not merge this PR as part of this agent run. After it lands on `main`, dispatch **release-please** from `main` with: - `tag_name`: `backpass-v0.1.29` - `version`: `0.1.29`

title: fix: prevent false session matches from Windows paths on POSIX
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #164 upstream: a session a harness recorded on Windows (C:\work\repo, \\server\share\repo, //server/share/repo) must never be resolved against the POSIX process cwd, which made it a tier-1 match for whichever repo ran backpass. Refuse such paths wherever a recorded path is resolved (association tiers 1, 1.5 and 3, user-scope project keys, nested-file attribution) while a recorded git remote still associates the session at tier 2, and leave Windows behavior unchanged. Keep WSL path translation out of this change; it follows separately.

## What Changed
- Exclude recorded Windows drive and UNC paths from POSIX association tiers 1, 1.5, and 3 while preserving tier-2 matches through recorded git remotes.
- Keep foreign user-scope cwd keys in their original spelling and exclude foreign paths and workdirs from nested-file attribution, invalidating cached attribution results.
- Add regression coverage and document path handling, preserving native Windows behavior without introducing WSL path translation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small and consistent: one shared helper refuses foreign Windows paths at every place the intent lists, tier 2 via a recorded remote still works, Windows hosts are unaffected, and behavioral regression tests cover it.

## Testing

Focused regression tests and isolated CLI scans and analyses passed, with base-commit comparisons demonstrating the original misassociations and incorrect nested attribution. CLI transcripts and persisted attribution artifacts were captured; setup issues were corrected and disposable data removed. Native Windows validation was unavailable.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scan Windows cwd and gitRoot recordings without falsely associating them to the current POSIX repository | ✅ pass | live | comparison.json, project-scan.json, other-project-scan.json |
| Associate foreign-path sessions by their recorded git remote, including strict mode | ✅ pass | live | project-scan.json, project-strict.json |
| Scan user scope from different checkouts without rewriting foreign project keys | ✅ pass | live | user-scan.json, user-other-scan.json, user-strict.json |
| Analyze nested memory without attributing foreign tool paths or workdirs to local files | ✅ pass | live | nested-analyze.json, named-nested-attribution.json, base-nested-analyze.json |
| Reanalyze after upgrading with stale nested attribution cached | ✅ pass | live | nested-cache-refresh.json, nested-refreshed-attribution.json |
| Continue associating native POSIX local, sibling, and deleted paths | ✅ pass | live | project-scan.json, project-strict.json |
| Run native Windows scans with unchanged Windows path behavior | ⏸️ untested | no | The platform-parameterized Windows helper test passed, but this Linux host has no Wine, QEMU, or Docker on PATH and no supplied Windows image or disposable Windows endpoint. A workspace-local Windows… |

<details>
<summary>Evidence: Validation report and reproduction instructions</summary>

```text
# Foreign-path live CLI validation

## Environment and isolation

The product ran on Linux with Node v24.21.0 against disposable Git repositories and Codex/Grok transcript stores inside the assigned worktree.
HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, CODEX_HOME, TMPDIR, and Git configuration were isolated.
No model outputs were mocked: analyze used short sessions that the real product skips before making model calls, while still computing and persisting nested attribution.
An initial analyze attempt used automatic agent selection and failed because the disposable home had no credentials; rerunning with the supported --no-auto-agent flag avoided probing and completed without model calls.
A driver assertion initially assumed readable attribution keys; it was corrected to use transcriptIdentity to look up the actual persisted hashed keys.
These were setup issues, not product failures.

## Results

| Recorded cwd | Base association | Target association without remote | Target with matching recorded remote |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `C:\work\repo` | Tier 1 | Excluded | Tier 2 |
| `C:/work/repo` | Tier 1.5 through a deliberately planted POSIX symlink | Excluded | Tier 2 |
| `\\server\share\repo` | Tier 1 | Excluded | Tier 2 |
| `//server/share/repo` | Tier 3 | Excluded | Tier 2 |

The scan used a permissive `**` worktree glob and exercised both cwd and Grok git_root_dir metadata.
Strict mode retained recorded-remote matches and rejected foreign paths without remotes.
An unrelated checkout did not collect the foreign Codex sessions.
Native POSIX local, sibling, dead-path, and legal colon-containing relative paths retained their expected behavior.

User-scope scans from two different working directories preserved each foreign cwd verbatim as its tier-3 project key, even when a same-spelled local directory existed inside a known checkout.
Recorded remotes still produced normalized tier-2 user project keys, and strict mode excluded the cwd-only sessions.

Nested analysis selected 2 legitimate local sessions after the fix, versus 9 sessions at the base commit.
Foreign tool paths, relative paths with foreign workdirs, foreign cwd-relative paths, and a foreign apply_patch filename contributed no local attribution.
A deliberately poisoned version-3 attribution cache was rebuilt as version 4 and again selected only the 2 legitimate sessions.

The focused association, scope, and nested test files also passed.
The Windows platform-parameterized helper test passed, but this is not native Windows end-to-end evidence.
The host is Linux and has no wine, qemu-system-x86_64, or docker executable on PATH, no supplied Windows runtime/image, and no disposable Windows endpoint credentials.
A Windows Node executable alone cannot run on this Linux kernel.
Native Windows verification needs a Windows runner with Node and Git, or an authorized disposable Windows VM image/runtime.

## Artifacts

- `comparison.json`: before/after product associations, user keys, nested corpus sizes, and exact successful CLI commands.
- `project-scan.json`, `project-strict.json`, `other-project-scan.json`: CLI stdout/stderr and invocation records.
- `user-scan.json`, `user-other-scan.json`, `user-strict.json`: user-scope CLI invocation records.
- `nested-analyze.json`, `nested-cache-refresh.json`: CLI nested-analysis output.
- `nested-attribution.json`, `nested-refreshed-attribution.json`: persisted product attribution state.
- `named-nested-attribution.json`: persisted attribution paths joined to scan session names for readability.
- `base-project-scan.json`, `base-user-scan.json`, `base-nested-analyze.json`: base-commit CLI regression reproduction.
- `targeted-tests.log`: supplemental focused regression tests.
- `drive-foreign-paths.mjs`: disposable setup, real CLI driver, and observable-output assertions.

This change has no rendered UI surface; CLI output and persisted state are the product evidence.
All disposable worktree data was removed after validation.

## Reproduction

From the assigned worktree, create `.foreign-path-validation/base` and `.foreign-path-validation/tmp`, then extract the base runtime with `git archive ddf8a7b06a9d191ee696d2ae9a10683c8b1ca872 src bin package.json | tar -x -C .foreign-path-validation/base`.
Run `node ~/.no-mistakes/evidence/01M3P92ZGR96EVQDPW9SJR4TYP/drive-foreign-paths.mjs` once against a clean disposable directory.
Remove `.foreign-path-validation` afterward.
```

title: fix(discovery): exclude backpass's own OpenCode sessions safely
body:
## Intent

Make backpass never analyze its own OpenCode sessions, and never drop a genuine one. acpx drives opencode (on both default ladders), so backpass analysis and synthesis calls land in the opencode SQLite store under the repo cwd; the file-head self check cannot see them and instead reads the database head, where one backpass prompt marks every session in the store as self. Mark self sessions from the store (first user text opens with the sentinel), never read a SQLite database as a transcript head, and do not list the empty sessions each agent probe leaves behind.

## What Changed
- Detect OpenCode self sessions from the first user text in SQLite and exclude their descendants locally and remotely, even when ancestors fall outside `--since`.
- Skip transcript-head reads for SQLite stores and omit message-less OpenCode probe sessions while retaining genuine conversations, including attachment-only prompts.
- Document the filtering behavior and add regression coverage for shared stores, malformed rows, ancestry, CLI scans, and remote probes.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is limited to OpenCode self-session detection and the SQLite head-read bypass. Both earlier fix rounds are verified correct, the logic fails soft on corrupt rows, and behavioral tests cover the local and remote paths.

## Testing

Focused self-session and probe tests passed, followed by six live scenarios using isolated CLI scans and locally executed shipped probes. Captured product outputs confirm self exclusion, genuine-session retention, and the attachment fix. Disposable data was removed; no source changes were needed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Exclude self sessions whose prompts lie beyond the database-head window | ✅ pass | live | round2-product-transcripts.txt: round2-self-beyond-head |
| Retain an image-only conversation while omitting unused agent probes | ✅ pass | live | round2-attachments-and-probes-scan.txt; round2-attachments-and-probes-fetch.frames |
| Retain genuine conversations that mention or later quote the sentinel | ✅ pass | live | round2-product-transcripts.txt: round2-genuine-sentinel-mentions |
| Exclude self descendants across the date cutoff without losing genuine descendants | ✅ pass | live | round2-product-transcripts.txt: round2-ancestry-and-cutoff |
| Scan a store containing malformed message and part records | ✅ pass | live | round2-product-transcripts.txt: round2-malformed-store-rows |

In SQLite, `json_extract` on text that is not valid JSON throws `malformed JSON` instead of returning NULL. I checked this with node:sqlite: the error comes through a correlated scalar subquery too. So a single corrupt `message.data` or `part.data` row in any session inside the cutoff window, including a session belonging to a different repo, makes `discover()` throw. `discoverTranscripts` then catches the error, logs `opencode: transcript store unreadable ... - harness skipped` and drops every genuine opencode session. Fix: guard both calls so a bad row only drops itself, for example `CASE WHEN json_valid(m.data) THEN json_extract(m.data, '$.role') END = 'user'` and the same for `pt.data`. Use CASE rather than a separate `json_valid(...) AND` term, because SQLite does not guarantee the order in which WHERE terms are evaluated.

title: fix: map Windows-recorded session paths safely under WSL
body:
## Intent

Follow up on PR #175 (read Windows-recorded session paths where WSL mounts them) to resolve Greptile's latest review finding: WSL path mapping must keep working under a custom WSL 2 kernel whose release string does not name Microsoft, without going back to trusting an inherited WSL_DISTRO_NAME on a non-WSL Linux machine. WSL is recognized by a kernel release naming Microsoft or WSL, or by WSL's drive-root mounts of Windows drives.

## What Changed
- Map Windows drive paths through WSL drive-root mounts and same-distro UNC paths to local paths for session association, user-scope project keys, and nested-file attribution.
- Recognize WSL through Microsoft/WSL kernel names or Windows drive-root mounts, supporting custom kernels without trusting `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` alone; keep unmappable paths out of path-based association while preserving recorded-remote matching.
- Preserve Windows path semantics for relative tool paths and workdirs, retain usable absolute paths with unmappable workdirs, and invalidate stale attribution caches; document the behavior and add regression coverage.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change meets the stated goal: WSL is recognized by a kernel release naming Microsoft or WSL, or by drive-root drvfs/9p mounts of Windows drives, and an inherited `WSL_DISTRO_NAME` alone is never trusted; the fix round's filesystem-type filter is correct and backed by tests that check behavior.

## Testing

All 60 focused tests and 24 CLI checks passed after correcting a native-host fixture assumption about its existing drive mount. Native WSL was exercised directly; alternate kernel releases and mount tables were supplied through a process-local OS-input shim to the unchanged CLI, not by booting alternate kernels. CLI JSON transcripts and a reproducible driver were preserved, the pre-fix regression was demonstrated, and disposable files were removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 6 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Scan Windows UNC sessions on native WSL and associate the matching distro | ✅ pass | live | wsl-cli-transcript.log: native-wsl and native-wsl-strict |
| Scan Windows paths with a custom kernel release and WSL drive-root mounts | ✅ pass | live | wsl-cli-transcript.log: custom-kernel-drive-root, custom-kernel-wsl1-drvfs, their strict variants, and before-fix-custom-kernel |
| Recognize Microsoft-only and WSL-only kernel names without drive mounts | ✅ pass | live | wsl-cli-transcript.log: microsoft-kernel-no-drives and wsl-only-kernel-no-drives, including strict variants |
| Reject an inherited WSL_DISTRO_NAME on ordinary Linux | ✅ pass | live | wsl-cli-transcript.log: inherited-distro-ordinary-linux and inherited-distro-ordinary-linux-strict |
| Reject unrelated drive-named mounts and subdirectory mounts as proof of WSL | ✅ pass | live | wsl-cli-transcript.log: unrelated-fuse-drive, unrelated-9p-drive, subdirectory-bind, and subdirectory-source, including strict variants |
| Preserve user-scope project identity and strict filtering across mapped and unmapped Windows paths | ✅ pass | live | wsl-cli-transcript.log: user-custom-kernel and user-inherited-distro, including strict variants |

title: fix(discovery): read OpenCode 2 stores and exclude backpass sessions
body:
## Intent

Stacked on #174 (backpass own OpenCode sessions). OpenCode 2 no longer writes the session, message and part tables; its store keeps sessions in session_v2 and the whole history as one typed row per message in session_message, so on an OpenCode 2 store the opencode adapter failed with no such table: session and every session was skipped. Read both layouts from one database: list session_v2 dated by its newest message (session_v2.time_updated does not move), read a session found in both layouts from session_v2 after an in-place upgrade, report a store with neither table as drifted, and map each 2.x message type deliberately (user and assistant turns, tool calls in order with text output or error, background subagent and shell completions as the result of the call that started them, user shell commands and skills as calls; instruction files, continue notices, system notices and compaction summaries never become turns). Apply the same self-session, delegated-descendant and empty-session rules as 1.x. Pin both layouts with golden fixtures built from the real 2.0.18 and 1.18.32 DDL.

## What Changed
- Read OpenCode 1.x and 2.x layouts together, prefer upgraded sessions in `session_v2`, use newest-message activity for discovery, and report unrecognized stores.
- Normalize 2.x turns and ordered tool calls, attach background completions to their originating calls, and omit injected notices and compaction summaries.
- Exclude backpass sessions, delegated descendants, and empty probes from local and remote discovery while retaining attachment-only conversations; document the behavior and add golden fixtures based on OpenCode 1.18.32 and 2.0.18 schemas.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is limited to one read-only discovery adapter and meets every intent requirement: both layouts, dating by newest message, v2 preferred for upgraded sessions, drift reporting, deliberate message-type mapping, the same self, descendant and empty-session rules, and golden fixtures; the only findings are an unrequired fallback and minor cleanups.

## Testing

Focused OpenCode tests and all seven live scenarios passed after correcting a disposable database-builder setup error; baseline reproduction, CLI transcripts, and fetched protocol payloads were saved, and temporary data was removed. No graphical UI changed, so evidence is CLI/protocol output rather than screenshots.

title: fix: recognize acpx exit code 3 as a timeout
body:
## Intent

Found on a real backpass run with a pinned OpenCode analysis agent: acpx 0.19 ends a model turn at its --timeout budget itself and exits with its documented TIMEOUT code 3, with only a zero-token accounting line on stderr. backpass named a timeout only from its own outer kill (result.timedOut), which never fires once acpx has exited, so one long prompt surfaced as a pinned agent failing unexpectedly and aborted the whole run. Name acpx exit 3 a timeout wherever result.timedOut is checked (exec, session prompt, session create, probe), so a long analysis fails only that transcript for a retry, as the design already intends, and the ladder never falls through because a prompt ran long.

## What Changed
- Treat acpx exit code 3 as a timeout across one-shot execution, session prompts, session creation, probes, and session setup, keeping model-turn timeouts out of agent fallthrough.
- Distinguish acpx-reported timeouts from backpass's outer timeout, preserving useful error details while filtering accounting noise.
- Add regression coverage for timeout exits and pinned-agent setup behavior, and document transcript-level retry semantics and legacy blank-output timeout handling.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is small and well-bounded: it treats acpx's documented timeout exit (3) the same way as backpass's existing outer-kill timeout at every model-call boundary, and behavior tests drive a fake acpx process through each path.

## Testing

Reproduced the baseline abort, passed focused timeout and resolver tests, and validated all scenarios through the real CLI and acpx using disposable ACP endpoints; saved CLI transcripts and state evidence, then removed the test environment. No graphical surface changed, so evidence is terminal output rather than screenshots.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product

| Effortful session analysis treats an acpx prompt timeout as a retryable transcript failure | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: session-prompt-timeout and session-prompt-retry. |
| An auto-selected model is not replaced when its prompt runs long | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: auto-ladder-prompt-timeout; Model selection preserved after timeout. |
| Session creation timeout reports timeout rather than unsupported sessions | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: session-create-timeout. |
| Session effort setup timeout remains retryable rather than aborting pinned analysis | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: session-effort-timeout. |
| Synthesis write-mode timeout gives retry guidance and preserves completed analysis | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: synthesis-prerequisite-analysis and synthesis-write-mode-timeout. |
| Timed-out availability probes do not poison subsequent agent selection | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: probe-timeout and probe-recovery; Probe timeouts leave no negative cache. |
| An ordinary protocol error remains a non-timeout pinned-agent failure | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: non-timeout-error. |

The same helper is used at src/acpx.js:156 (session-create UserError message), src/acpx.js:467 (probe detail), src/acpx.js:541 (exec) and src/acpx.js:734 (session prompt). Fix: in `timeoutMessage`, keep `acpx ${agent} <exec|session prompt|session create|probe>` in the exit-3 wording, for example by passing the agent and call label. Pick the detail line from stderr with the `[acpx]` accounting and noise lines filtered out (`stripAcpxNoise`-style), and omit it when nothing else remains. Update the two tests to assert that.

🔧 Fix applied.
4 issues (3 warnings, 1 info) still open:

- ⚠️ `src/acpx.js:628` - When acpx exits 3 on its own internal timeout, backpass's error message reports backpass's budget, not the time acpx actually waited. In `openSession`, `endedAtTimeout(created)` raises `sessionCreateTimeoutError({ timeoutMs: createTimeoutMs })`, which says "did not create a session within 180s". But `sessions new` gets no `--timeout` flag, so an exit 3 there comes from acpx's own adapter timeouts. Installed acpx 0.19 has two: `CLAUDE_ACP_SESSION_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS` = 60s, overridable by `ACPX_CLAUDE_ACP_SESSION_CREATE_TIMEOUT_MS`, and `GEMINI_ACP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` = 15s. Concrete path: a slow Claude adapter makes acpx exit 3 after 60s, and the user reads "within 180s". The hint also implies backpass's cold-start budget was exhausted, and raising it cannot help. The same wrong number appears at: src/acpx.js:456 (probe detail "probe timed out after ${createTimeoutMs}s" when acpx hit its 15s Gemini startup timeout under a 20s probe budget); src/acpx.js:532 and src/acpx.js:722 ("exec/session prompt timed out after ${timeoutSeconds}s" when the exit 3 came from an adapter startup or create timeout inside the turn, not the `--timeout` budget). Classification is correct; only the reported duration and cause are wrong. Fix at `endedAtTimeout`'s callers: when `!result.timedOut && result.code === ACPX_EXIT_TIMEOUT`, say acpx ended the call at its own timeout (exit 3) and append `firstLine(result.stderr)` when it is present, instead of quoting backpass's budget.
- ⚠️ `src/acpx.js:137` - This problem was introduced by the round-1 fix. For acpx exit 3, `timeoutMessage` throws away the backpass-built message and returns a generic `acpx ended the call at its own timeout (exit 3)`. It then appends `firstLine(result.stderr)` as the cause. In the exact scenario from the intent, the only stderr line is acpx's accounting line. The user therefore sees `acpx ended the call at its own timeout (exit 3): [acpx] tokens: input=0 output=0 total=0`. That shows a zero-token usage record as the timeout cause, and it no longer names the agent or the call. Before this change, the message read, for example, `acpx opencode exec timed out after 600s`. Now the analyze warning (src/analyze.js:414) shows only the transcript's harness, not the analysis agent. The consolidate warning (src/consolidate.js:94) and the synthesis error printed by `reportError` (src/cli.js:332) do not say which agent or stage timed out at all. The new tests encode this noisy output as the expected result (test/acpx-exec-timeout.test.js:152, test/acpx-session-create-timeout.test.js:112), so they cannot catch it. The same helper is used at src/acpx.js:156 (session-create UserError message), src/acpx.js:467 (probe detail), src/acpx.js:541 (exec) and src/acpx.js:734 (session prompt). Fix: in `timeoutMessage`, keep `acpx ${agent} <exec|session prompt|session create|probe>` in the exit-3 wording, for example by passing the agent and call label. Pick the detail line from stderr with the `[acpx]` accounting and noise lines filtered out (`stripAcpxNoise`-style), and omit it when nothing else remains. Update the two tests to assert that.
- ⚠️ `src/acpx.js:698` - The fix missed two sites that still check only `result.timedOut`: the session `set` call here and `set-mode` at src/acpx.js:681. The intent says to name acpx exit 3 a timeout "wherever result.timedOut is checked".

`acpx <agent> -s <name> set <key> <value>` goes through acpx `setSessionConfigOption`. When no queue owner is running, that call reconnects and starts the adapter. In acpx 0.19, `GEMINI_ACP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT` and `CLAUDE_ACP_SESSION_CREATE_TIMEOUT` both map to `EXIT_CODES.TIMEOUT` = 3, so this call can exit 3.

Here is the concrete path:
- `runModelCall` runs with a pinned agent and an effort override, which calls `sessionPrompt`, then `openSession`.
- `set` exits 3.
- The `AcpxError` is built from the raw result, so `timedOut` is false.
- `withFallthrough` skips the timeout rethrow and builds `pinnedFailureError` (a `UserError`).
- analyze rethrows `UserError`, and the whole run aborts as "failed unexpectedly".

That is the failure the intent set out to remove. It is still reachable here, whereas an outer kill at the same step already gives `timedOut: true` and fails only that transcript. The set-mode path at :681 has the same gap when `sessionModeRequired` is set.

Fix: at both sites, use `endedAtTimeout(...)` to choose the detail and pass `{ ...set, timedOut: endedAtTimeout(set) }` (and the same for `setMode`) to `AcpxError`. That matches the exec and session-prompt paths.
- ℹ️ `src/acpx.js:137` - The round-2 fix introduced this. `timeoutMessage` runs `stripAcpxNoise` on stderr, which drops every line starting with `[acpx]`, not just the accounting line.

exec and session prompt run with `--format quiet`. In that format, acpx's quiet formatter writes the only timeout diagnostic as `[acpx] error: TIMEOUT GEMINI_ACP_STARTUP_TIMEOUT ...` (see `onError` in acpx `output-*.js`). So when acpx hits an adapter startup timeout inside a turn, the filter removes exactly the line that tells it apart from a `--timeout` budget stop. The message then reads only `acpx <agent> exec ended at its own timeout (exit 3)`, which is the ambiguity the round-1 finding wanted cleared up.

The new tests (test/acpx-exec-timeout.test.js:151-157, test/acpx-session-create-timeout.test.js:110-117) feed plain `adapter startup timed out` lines, a shape acpx never writes in quiet mode, so they cannot catch this.

Fix: filter only acpx's accounting and status lines (for example `[acpx] tokens:`), keep `[acpx] error:` lines, and add a test case that uses the real `[acpx] error: TIMEOUT ...` shape.

🔧 Fix applied.
✅ Re-checked - no issues remain.

title: fix: isolate SQLite session raw transcripts and reclaim expired files
feat(discovery): associate sessions by structured work paths
body:
## Intent

Follow-up on #179 (tier 2.5, work paths): the work tier keys its path cache by a hash of a SQLite session events (a SQLite row can change without its timestamp moving), but it also wrote that hash into the transcript contentSignature, which evidence and nested-attribution keys are built from. Evidence identity then depended on which tier associated a session, and every tier-2.5 session existing evidence went stale on upgrade, re-running all analysis for unchanged content. Keep the hash for the work-path cache only and leave the transcript content signature to its adapter, like every other tier.

## What Changed
- Add local tier-2.5 association for sessions started outside checkouts when most checkout-bound tool paths belong to this repo, including strict-mode support and CLI/TUI reporting.
- Share path resolution with nested-memory attribution, map supported Windows paths under WSL, and exclude unmappable Windows paths from path-based association.
- Cache work paths with content and resolver-version checks, keeping SQLite event hashes confined to the work-path cache and preserving adapter-provided transcript signatures for evidence and nested attribution.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The final change is a one-line fix that meets the stated intent exactly: the content hash now keys only the work-path cache, and the transcript's content signature comes from its adapter. I found no new defects in it or in the parts of the branch it touches.

## Testing

Reproduced the pre-fix signature regression, passed the focused regression on the target, and verified three scenarios through the real CLI. Captured CLI responses and persisted evidence/cache state; all target checks passed and disposable worktree data was removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product

| Analyze a work-tier session with existing root and nested evidence without reanalysis | ✅ pass | live | 06-fixed-cached-analysis.json and 07-persisted-cache-contracts.json |
| Change SQLite tool-call paths without advancing timestamps and refresh repository association | ✅ pass | live | CLI transcript and 11-cache-invalidation.json |

title: fix: stop scheduling analysis after a fatal worker error
body:
## Intent

Found on a real backpass run: an error that fails the run (a pinned agent failing in a way nothing can classify) propagated from one analysis worker and stopped only that worker. The run reported the failure at once while the other workers kept taking transcripts and starting model calls in the background for over an hour, and the process exited only when the whole queue was done. Stop handing out transcripts after the first fatal worker error, let calls already in flight finish and keep their evidence, and rethrow the first error once every worker has stopped, so nothing is still running when it surfaces. Per-transcript failures keep their existing fail-soft behavior.

## What Changed
- Stop assigning transcripts after the first fatal analysis worker error, wait for all workers to stop, then rethrow that first error.
- Preserve successful evidence from calls already in flight and retain fail-soft handling of per-transcript failures; document these behaviors in the README.
- Add a CLI regression test with two workers and five sessions that verifies a fatal failure prevents further model calls.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This is a small, well-bounded change to one private helper with a single caller. It meets every stated requirement: no new work is handed out after a fatal error, calls in flight finish and keep their evidence, the first error is rethrown after every worker has stopped, and per-transcript failures still fail soft. The new test runs the real CLI end to end.

## Testing

Reproduced the bug before the fix, then verified queue shutdown, in-flight evidence preservation, first-error ordering, serial execution, and fail-soft retries through the real CLI. The focused regression passed after correcting an isolated CommonJS/ESM fixture setup issue. CLI transcripts, process timelines, and persisted evidence were captured; all disposable fixtures were removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fatal analysis stops queued work and reports only after active work is saved | ✅ pass | live | baseline-fatal.txt and fatal-drain.txt |
| Retry after a fatal run reuses the completed sibling's evidence | ✅ pass | live | retry-cache.txt |
| A later fatal worker cannot replace the first error | ✅ pass | live | competing-fatal.txt |
| Single-worker analysis stops immediately after its fatal transcript | ✅ pass | live | serial-fatal.txt |
| Malformed output and timeout failures remain per-transcript and retryable | ✅ pass | live | per-transcript-soft.txt and per-transcript-retry.txt |

title: feat(discovery): support additional OpenCode stores and 2.x transcripts
body:
## Intent

Stacked on #174 and #176. Let a person point backpass at more OpenCode stores than the default one, for example a consistent copy of the store the Windows OpenCode desktop app keeps, read from WSL, whose sessions did the work in this distro checkouts. It must be a personal config list (discovery.opencodeStores: OpenCode data directories or database files), not OpenCode relocation variables in the environment: acpx passes backpass environment to the OpenCode it runs for analysis, which must keep its own store and login. Like discovery.hosts, a repository .backpassrc.json that sets it is refused by name and user scope inherits the top-level list; entries are absolute (~/ expanded). Each session is read from the store that listed it; a store named twice or a session copied into two stores is read once from the first, so a copy never counts twice; a configured store that is missing or unreadable is named in a warning and skipped while the default store keeps its harness-level failure. Remote hosts are unaffected.

## What Changed
- Add personal-only `discovery.opencodeStores` for absolute data-directory or database paths, with user-scope inheritance, first-store deduplication, source-specific reads, and warnings for unavailable configured stores without relocating the analysis harness or changing SSH store selection.
- Read OpenCode 2.x transcripts alongside 1.x stores, prefer upgraded sessions, track message activity, and normalize tool calls and background results while excluding injected notices.
- Exclude backpass-originated OpenCode sessions and their descendants even when ancestors fall outside the discovery window, omit empty probes, and avoid treating SQLite databases as individual transcript files.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This is an additive, fail-soft change to discovery that matches every constraint in the stated intent, and the only finding is a pair of unneeded tests of the test helpers.

## Testing

Focused tests and isolated CLI, shipped-probe, and live PTY scenarios passed after resolving disposable-driver setup issues; evidence includes CLI transcripts, normalized session contents, probe responses, environment checks, and rendered terminal HTML, with all temporary worktree data removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Add personal OpenCode stores without relocating the default store | ✅ pass | live | CLI scenario transcripts; Normalized session contents from their originating stores; Unchanged OpenCode relocation environment |
| Deduplicate store aliases and copied sessions, keeping the first source | ✅ pass | live | CLI scenario transcripts: 02-duplicate-stores and 03-first-configured-store-wins |
| Reject repository-supplied stores and invalid personal paths | ✅ pass | live | CLI scenario transcripts: 05-invalid-config-* and 06-repo-refusal-* |
| Inherit the top-level store list in user scope | ✅ pass | live | CLI scenario transcripts: 04-user-scope |
| Skip bad configured stores while preserving default-store failure behavior | ✅ pass | live | Named configured-store warnings with successful discovery; Default-store harness failure; CLI scenario transcripts: 10-missing-default-store |
| Read legacy, current, resumed, and migrated OpenCode sessions correctly | ✅ pass | live | Normalized session contents from their originating stores; Live self-session and recency boundaries; Upgraded store retains v2 session identity |
| Exclude self descendants without dropping genuine or malformed conversations | ✅ pass | live | Live self-session and recency boundaries; live-self-boundaries.mjs CLI and shipped-probe execution |
| Keep shipped remote discovery independent of the local configured-store list | ✅ pass | live | Shipped probe discovers only its default store; Shipped probe fetch response |
| Show the accurate SQLite store label in the live terminal | ✅ pass | live | Live terminal frame showing sqlite store |

title: feat: support explicit per-edit decisions in backpass apply
body:
## Intent

Let backpass apply take per-edit decisions without a browser or a terminal, so a person who explicitly chooses to let a trusted script decide for their own repo (for example a nightly job that applies edits passing a rules check) can apply accepted edits and record rejections with reasons. backpass apply --decisions takes the vector the review surface sends (e1=accepted e2=rejected:too-narrow), is repeatable, and is strict: every supplied vector must name at least one edit, every token must name one edit of the proposal, a verdict, and at most one known reject reason, no edit may be decided twice across flags, and any violation writes nothing. Unnamed edits stay undecided. It is never a default (VISION.md: looser review is an explicit opt-in), and every existing apply gate still runs. This follow-up closes Greptile's finding that a blank vector next to a valid one was dropped.

## What Changed
- Add repeatable `backpass apply --decisions` vectors to accept edits and record rejections with optional known reasons without a browser or terminal, leaving unnamed edits undecided and retaining existing apply gates.
- Validate all vectors before writing, rejecting blank vectors, malformed tokens, unknown edits, duplicate decisions across flags, and invalid reasons; disallow combining with `--no-ui` or using on other commands.
- Document the opt-in scripted workflow and add CLI regression coverage for partial decisions, rejection reasons, repeated flags, and invalid inputs that must write nothing.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: This adds an opt-in, strictly validated input path that fails before anything is written and reuses the existing applyDecisions gates unchanged; I traced it against every intent constraint and found no defect.

## Testing

Focused CLI regressions and isolated live checks passed for decision persistence, strict validation, dry-run, explicit opt-in, and apply safety gates. The blank-vector failure was reproduced before the fix and refused afterward. CLI transcripts and persisted-state snapshots were captured; all disposable worktree data was removed. No screenshots were needed for this noninteractive CLI change.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 11 of 11 scenarios driven live against the product

| Record rejection-only decisions with optional known reasons | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: reject-only-*. |
| Refuse blank flags alongside valid decisions | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: blank-before-valid, empty-after-valid, blank-between-valid-and-reject, and before-fix-blank-flag-wrote-edit. |
| Reject malformed, unknown, and duplicate decisions atomically | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: earlier-typo through extra-token. |
| Preview explicit decisions without persisting changes | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: dry-run-mixed-keeps-all-state. |
| Require explicit opt-in and reject conflicting command usage | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: default-needs-review-surface, terminal-fallback-needs-human, no-ui-conflict, and wrong-subcommand. |
| Refuse decisions against stale memory or another stale target | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: stale-memory-refuses-rejection-too and stale-non-memory-target. |
| Preserve composition and skill-write safeguards | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: composition-failure, skill-collision, and changed-skills-directory. |
| Enforce budget limits on accepted decisions | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: accepted-subset-budget-cap and over-budget-must-shrink. |
| Preserve proposal scope, target, and eligibility gates | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: target-mismatch, scope-mismatch, failed-proposal-gates, and already-applied-proposal. |

title: fix: retry blank model turns once before falling through
body:
## Intent

Keep PR #183's explanation of blank model turns accurate. The blank turns that stopped a pinned OpenCode run turned out to be turns that spent their whole 32,000-token output budget on reasoning (finish length, no text), not provider hiccups; how far a turn reasons varies between attempts, which is why a single retry recovered one analysis call. Update the comments and README wording only; the retry-once behaviour is unchanged.

## What Changed
- Retry blank model output once per candidate per call, including pinned agents, before falling back or stopping the run; timeouts remain excluded from retries.
- Clarify README and code comments that blank turns can exhaust their output budget on reasoning, whose length varies between attempts, rather than necessarily indicating provider failures.
- Add regression coverage for recovery without demotion, pinned-agent retries, and fallback after repeated blank output.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: Since the last round only wording changed in comments, README and a test message, and it matches the intent; the retry logic is small, unchanged, and traced as correct.

## Testing

The targeted tests and seven isolated CLI scenarios passed, with CLI output, boundary-call logs, and persisted state captured as evidence. The explanation follow-up preserves retry behavior. Upstream blank responses were scripted; actual model reasoning was not exercised. No screenshots were needed for this CLI-only validation, and all disposable worktree data was removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 7 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Analyze two transcripts with pinned OpenCode: each initial blank retries once and succeeds | ✅ pass | live | pinned-single-blank-per-call.json |
| Analyze with automatic selection: a single blank does not poison the candidate cache | ✅ pass | live | auto-single-blank-retains-candidate.json |
| Run pinned OpenCode against repeated blanks: stop after exactly one retry | ✅ pass | live | pinned-second-blank-stops.json |
| Run automatic selection against repeated blanks: demote and give the next candidate its own retry | ✅ pass | live | auto-second-blank-falls-through.json |

title: Synthesis fails after analysis is complete when the adapter's bundled harness is too old for the model
body:
## What happened

backpass v0.1.29 with acpx 0.13.1, Linux. The analysis step used `claude-sonnet-5-5` and completed all 50 transcripts. Then the synthesis step used `claude-opus-5-5`, failed on its first prompt, and the run stopped:

```
error AcpxError: acpx claude session prompt failed (exit 1): [acpx] error: RUNTIME QUEUE_RUNTIME_PROMPT_FAILED Internal error: API Error: 400 Claude Code 2.1.215 does not support this model; version 2.1.280 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.
    at Object.prompt (.../backpass/src/acpx.js:683:13)
    ...
    at async AgentResolver.withFallthrough (.../backpass/src/agents.js:518:16)
    at async synthesizeProposal (.../backpass/src/synthesize.js:689:22)
```

The synthesis ladder had a second rung (`gpt-5.6-sol` on pi/opencode/codex), but backpass did not try it.

## Root cause (upstream, outside backpass)

acpx pins `@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp`. On Linux, acpx does not set `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE`, so the adapter runs the Claude Code copy that its `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` includes. It does not run the user's installed `claude`.

| acpx | adapter range | agent SDK | bundled Claude Code |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.13.1 | `^0.60.0` | 0.3.215 | 2.1.215 |
| 0.19.3 (latest) | `^0.76.0` | 0.3.257 | 2.1.257 |

Opus 5.5 needs 2.1.280 or newer. The acpx fix is open: openclaw/acpx#831 and #832.

## Gaps in backpass

1. **The probe cannot find this failure.** `probeSession` (`src/acpx.js`) creates a session and reads `availableModels`, but it sends no prompt. The adapter lists the model, so the probe passes. The failure occurs only when the first real prompt goes to the provider.
2. **This failure is not classified.** `classifyAcpxFailure` has no pattern for `does not support this model`. It returns `null`, so `withFallthrough` throws the error again and does not demote the candidate.
3. **The cache keeps a wrong positive verdict.** After the run, `.backpass/agent-probe-cache.json` still has `claude|claude-opus-5-5` with verdict `ok`, so the next run fails in the same way. (If gap 2 is fixed, `demote()` writes the negative verdict.)
4. **Each role is probed only when its step starts.** `resolve("synthesis")` runs at `synthesize.js:654`, after the analysis step. A problem with the synthesis model shows only after the analysis tokens are used. Saved evidence makes a rerun less expensive, but the first run still fails at the last step.

## Suggested fixes

- Gaps 2 and 3: classify `does not support this model` as `model-unavailable`. PR to follow.
- Gap 4: resolve all roles before the analysis step starts, so that probe failures show first.
- Gap 1 (for discussion): an optional check that sends a one-token prompt to each role's pick at startup. It costs a few tokens. It would find provider-side rejections that a model list cannot show.

## Workaround

Set the adapter to use the installed CLI:

```
CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE=$HOME/.local/bin/claude npx backpass
```

Delete the stale `claude|claude-opus-5-5` entry from `.backpass/agent-probe-cache.json` if necessary.

title: fix(agents): treat "does not support this model" as model-unavailable
body:
## What Changed - `classifyAcpxFailure` (`src/acpx.js`) now classifies a provider error containing `does not support this model` as `model-unavailable`, the same verdict as `did not advertise that model`. This error appears when an adapter lists a model that its bundled harness is too old to call, so the first prompt gets rejected. The header comment explains that the probe can't catch this case because it sends no prompt. - The `model-unavailable` verdict label in `src/agents.js` changes from "model not advertised" to "model not available", since it now also covers models that are listed but can't be called. The module header comment uses the new label too. - Added a test in `test/agents.test.js` for a real Claude Code `API Error: 400 ... does not support this model; version ... or newer is required` stderr line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This is a one-regex widening of classifyAcpxFailure, so a harness-too-old prompt rejection is now classified "model-unavailable" and follows the existing withFallthrough/demote path. That rejection comes on the first prompt, before any real work, so the rule against switching models mid-work still holds. The negative cache TTL (30 min) applies as for other verdicts, the pinned and exhausted error paths just pick up the neutral "model not available" label, and the new test runs the real classifier on a real stderr sample. ## Testing I built a disposable git repo, a HOME holding one Pi session transcript, and fake acpx/claude/codex binaries under /tmp, then ran the real backpass CLI against them five times. The current build falls through from the too-old claude harness to codex and analyzes the transcript. The base build reproduces the bug: it marks the transcript failed and does not fall through. The pinned and exhausted-ladder errors show the new "model not available" label. An unrelated 400 error does not trigger fall-through. The targeted classification unit test also passes.
