title: Push a root rule down into a nested memory file when only that subtree uses it
body:
## Problem

With `nestedMemoryFiles` set (#159), a new rule goes to the lowest file that fits (`owningFile`, `src/nested.js`). An existing root rule stays in the root, even when every session where it mattered worked under one nested directory. That rule loads in every session, but only one subtree uses it.

The root pass cannot move it down today:

- An edit changes one file (`src/proposal.js`: "an edit changes one file").
- A `move` must stay in the same memory file (`src/proposal.js`: `kind "move" must be change(s) to <file> only`).
- An `extract` must write to a skill file (`src/proposal.js`, `isSkillFilePath` check).

So the root pass can keep the rule, extract it to a skill, or remove it with harm evidence. None of these fits a rule that is correct but used in only one directory.

## Proposal

Allow a push-down edit: remove text from the root file and add it verbatim to one named nested file, as one edit.

- Keep the text one-for-one, as `move` does now.
- Allow it only when measured evidence shows the rule is local:
  - `owningFile` places every session where the rule mattered (`entry.sessions`, `src/fold.js`) under the target file's directory;
  - there are at least `minGapEvidence` such sessions.
- Check the target file's budget (`nestedBudget`) and the root budget at propose and at apply.
- Show it in apply as one decision that names both files. Remember a rejection like any other edit.
- Keep the gate in `buildProposal`, with no text classifier.
- The root synthesis pass needs the nested file as an allowed destination. Today nested files have their own staging copies and passes.

## Risks to check before building

1. **Harness loading.** A nested file helps only if the harness loads it in the sessions that need the rule. Codex may load `AGENTS.md` files only on the path from the repo root to the session cwd; this needs checking against current Codex docs. If true, a Codex session started at the root that edits `apps/api/` would lose a pushed-down rule. Claude Code loads a nested `CLAUDE.md` only when it reads files in that directory. The attribution in `src/nested.js` assumes the nested file loaded when all work paths are under its directory. Push-down depends on that assumption more than additions do, because it takes the rule out of the root.
2. **Small samples.** "Mattered only in `apps/api` sessions" can be chance on a small sample. Two sessions can be enough to add a rule at the subtree level, but maybe not enough to take it away from every other session. The floor may need to be higher than `minGapEvidence`, or be a share of placed sessions.
3. **VISION fit.** `extract` and `move` are exempt from the session floor because they keep the text. Push-down keeps the text but narrows who sees it, so for sessions outside the subtree it is close to a removal. The gate above treats it that way.

## Out of scope

Pull-up (merging the same rule from sibling nested files into the root). `src/overlap.js` already reports cross-file duplicates, and the saving is small.

Context: backpass 0.1.30 (d1e7550).

title: apply gates against the current config budget, not the cap the proposal was made under
body:
## Problem

`backpass apply` checks the accepted edits against the budget in the **current** config, not against the cap the proposal was made under.

- Root file: `capTokens: config.budgetTokens` (`src/apply/writer.js`).
- Nested files: `config.nestedBudgetTokens ?? config.budgetTokens` (same file).

The proposal already records its cap in `proposal.budget.capTokens` (and `nested[].budget.capTokens`). When the run and the apply see different budgets, apply judges the edits against a cap the proposal never saw, and nothing says so.

`cmdApply` already refuses a scope mismatch with a clear message (`this proposal is <scope> scope; run backpass apply --scope <scope>`). A budget mismatch gets no such check.

## Repro

Found by reading the source; not run end to end.

1. `.backpassrc.json` has `"budgetTokens": 10000`. A second file, `docs/RULES.md`, is about 25k tokens.
2. `backpass --memory-file docs/RULES.md --budget 30000`. The proposal has `budget.capTokens: 30000`. The file is under that cap, so the proposal can carry additions.
3. `backpass apply --memory-file docs/RULES.md` (no `--budget`).
4. Apply uses the 10000 cap. The file is now "already over budget", so the shrink gate refuses every accepted subset that adds tokens.

The reverse also happens: a proposal made under a small cap can be applied under a larger one, so the zero-sum rule is skipped.

## Expected

One of:

- apply gates at the proposal's own `budget.capTokens`; or
- apply refuses and names both numbers, for example: `this proposal was made under a 30,000-token budget; the current config says 10,000. Re-run apply with --budget 30000, or propose again.`

VISION: "a display that quietly compares two different measurements is a defect".

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: Evidence cache keeps one record per transcript, so alternating --memory-file targets re-analyzes every transcript
body:
## Problem

The evidence cache holds one record per transcript: `State.evidencePath` writes `evidence/<transcript identity>.json` (`src/state.js`). The freshness key includes the memory hash (`evidenceKey`), but the path does not.

So when a user trains two root files in turn with `--memory-file` (or `--target`):

1. The run for file A writes evidence for every sampled transcript.
2. The run for file B overwrites those records.
3. The next run for A finds no fresh evidence and analyzes every transcript again, even though A did not change.

`proposal.json` is also one file, so A's proposal must be applied before B runs.

This is not #34. In #34 the memory file changed, and re-analysis is correct. Here nothing changed: the cache can only hold one surface at a time.

## Who hits it

Anyone who trains more than one root-level file with `--memory-file`, which is the workaround #111 mentions. It is also the only way to give files different caps today (#190). The cost is one analysis call per sampled transcript, at every switch.

## Proposal

Give each named target file its own state directory, the way nested files already do (`nestedStateDir` in `src/nested.js`: `.backpass/nested/<file>-<hash>/`). That means its own `evidence/`, `proposal.json` and gap ledger, with rejections shared. A default run keeps `.backpass/` as it is today.

A smaller alternative: key the evidence path on identity + memory hash, and prune records whose hash matches no configured file.

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: Per-file budget for nested memory files
body:
## Problem

`nestedBudgetTokens` is one number for every file in `nestedMemoryFiles`: `nestedBudget()` in `src/nested.js` at propose time, and `config.nestedBudgetTokens ?? config.budgetTokens` in `src/apply/writer.js` at apply time.

Nested files often differ in size by 5-10x. One cap cannot fit all of them:

- If the cap fits the large file, the small files get a cap far above their size, so the zero-sum gate never starts for them.
- If the cap fits the small files, the large file starts over budget, and every run for it is a shrink run.

#158 asked for "a budget per file". #159 shipped one shared value.

## Proposal

Accept a per-file cap, and keep the current shape valid:

```json
{
  "nestedMemoryFiles": [
    "apps/web/AGENTS.md",
    { "path": "apps/api/AGENTS.md", "budgetTokens": 8000 }
  ],
  "nestedBudgetTokens": 2000
}
```

A string entry uses `nestedBudgetTokens` (then `budgetTokens`), as it does today. Propose and apply read the cap from the same place (compare the apply budget issue, #188).

An alternative shape: `nestedBudgetTokens` as a map, `{ "<path>": N }`.

## Workaround today

One run per file: `--memory-file <file> --budget <N>`. This loses nested attribution, and it re-analyzes every transcript at each switch (#189).

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: Nested memory files: show when a file cannot collect evidence under the all-paths attribution rule
body:
## Problem

A nested file trains only on sessions whose **every** in-repo work path is under its directory (`workedPaths` and `workedUnder`, `src/nested.js`). Reads count as work paths.

In a repo where most sessions cross directories, a nested file never reaches `minGapEvidence` sessions, and nothing tells the user. The file is listed as configured, runs finish, and it gets no edits. The user cannot tell "no gaps" apart from "no evidence can reach this file".

## Measured

One repo, Claude Code sessions, last 30 days, `minUserTurns: 2`: 78 sessions. I replayed the attribution offline over the transcripts (structured tool-call paths, repo-relative, worktree prefixes removed):

| attribution rule | most sessions for any one top-level subdirectory | subdirectories with 2 or more sessions |
|---|---|---|
| current: every path under the directory, reads included | 2 | 2 |
| same, but reads of root-level files ignored | 3 | 6 |
| only edit/write paths counted | 3 | 4 |

So in this repo a looser rule helps only a little. The main gap is that the user does not see the count. (Here the root memory file tells agents to read a root-level map file first, so one read makes many sessions cross-cutting.)

## Proposal

1. `backpass status` and the run summary print, for each nested file, the number of sampled sessions attributed to it, with a warning below `minGapEvidence`. For example: `apps/api/AGENTS.md: 1 of 78 sessions worked only under apps/api/, below minGapEvidence (2); this file cannot receive edits.`
2. Optional and opt-in, still deterministic: do not count reads of the configured memory files themselves (the root file and named ancestors) as work paths. The agent reads them as instructions, not as work. In the table above, the effect of this is at most the "reads of root-level files ignored" row.

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: Thematic breaks (---) are parsed as instructions and reported as cross-surface overlaps
body:
## Problem

A line that is only a thematic break (`---`) is parsed as an instruction unit (`parseMemoryUnits`, `src/memory.js`). It then:

- adds to the "N instructions" count in `status`;
- gets an id in the instruction index given to analysis;
- shows as a cross-surface overlap with similarity 1.00 against any skill whose body also has a `---` line.

## Repro

`AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
# Guide

Run the linter before you commit.

---

## Tests

Run the unit tests with `make test`.

---

Keep commits small.
```

`.agents/skills/demo/SKILL.md`:

```markdown
---
name: demo
description: Use when releasing.
---

# Release

Tag the commit, then push the tag.

---

Write the changelog entry.
```

`backpass status`:

```
BUDGET (always-loaded)
  AGENTS.md + skill descriptions [....] 36 / 5,000 tok · 5 instructions

CROSS-SURFACE (report-only)
  AG-002 restates demo body · 1 tok · similarity 1.00 · body loads on trigger; weigh placement
  AG-004 restates demo body · 1 tok · similarity 1.00 · body loads on trigger; weigh placement
```

The units are `AG-001` "Run the linter...", `AG-002` `---`, `AG-003` "Run the unit tests...", `AG-004` `---`, `AG-005` "Keep commits small." There are 3 instructions, not 5, and there is no overlap. In a real file with several section breaks, most of the overlap report was these lines.

## Expected

A thematic-break-only line (`---`, `***`, `___`) is not an instruction unit. It is not counted, not given an id, and not reported as an overlap.

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: Failed analysis keeps no trace of the reply ("analysis returned no parseable JSON") and is retried every run
body:
## Problem

When `extractJson(result.text)` finds nothing, analysis throws `analysis returned no parseable JSON` (`src/analyze.js`). The evidence record then keeps only `status: "failed"` and that error string. The reply is dropped.

A failed record is never fresh (`isEvidenceFresh` needs `status === "ok"`), so the transcript is analyzed again on every run, with no limit.

## Measured

In one repo, 27 of 211 evidence records failed this way (13%). Analysis agent: claude, Sonnet, auto-picked, effort medium, `jobs: 10`. The failures do not track transcript size: median 0.62 MB for failed records against 0.79 MB for ok records.

From the record alone, the user cannot tell the cause: an empty turn, prose instead of JSON, JSON cut off at a length limit, or a fence the extractor does not accept. Each run pays for the same failures again.

## Proposal

1. On this failure, save in the evidence record, after redaction: the reply length in characters, the first and last ~300 characters, and the harness stop reason if acpx gives one.
2. Show a short class in `status`: `empty`, `prose`, `truncated` or `unparsed`.
3. Optional: after N failures of the same transcript at the same key, skip it and say so, instead of retrying it forever.

VISION: "Failure is loud and named."

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: Claude Code per-project auto memory (MEMORY.md) is always loaded but invisible to project scope
body:
## Problem

Claude Code keeps a per-project auto memory in `~/.claude/projects/<munged-cwd>/memory/`. Its index, `MEMORY.md`, is loaded into every session for that project, next to `CLAUDE.md`. In one repo it is about 22 KB (~5.5k tokens), about the same size as the root memory file.

Project scope cannot see it:

- `--memory-file ~/.claude/projects/<munged-cwd>/memory/MEMORY.md` is refused: `resolves outside the project root; project scope cannot access it` (`resolveMemoryPath`, `src/memory.js`).
- The budget bar leaves it out, so the always-loaded surface is under-counted. This is the same class of problem as #111.
- Analysis is not shown those lines, so a gap that the auto memory already covers can still be proposed for the root file.

## Workaround that works today

User scope, with the file named and the sessions filtered to the one project:

```sh
backpass --scope user \
  --memory-file ~/.claude/projects/<munged-cwd>/memory/MEMORY.md \
  --budget 9000 --project '~/<repo>' --project '~/<repo>/**'
```

`status` measures it correctly, and the project globs pick only that repo's sessions. Limits:

- the evidence goes to user-scope state, not the project's;
- the user-scope skill descriptions are billed, not the project's;
- synthesis may add rule text to a file whose format is one pointer line per memory (the topic files hold the content).

## Proposal (any of these)

1. Report-only: count the project's auto memory `MEMORY.md` in the project budget bar as its own line, the way the `CLAUDE.md pointer` line is shown.
2. Show its text to analysis as "also loaded", as nested runs already do for the root file (`renderAlsoLoaded`), so covered gaps are not proposed again.
3. Opt-in: allow naming it as a project-scope target with its own budget, and keep the index format (one line per entry).

backpass 0.1.30 (main `d1e7550`).

title: fix(state): skip unverifiable POSIX mode check for Windows user-profile state dirs
body:
## Intent Fix issue #115: on native Windows every --scope user command fails at startup with 'could not secure state directory ... as mode 700 (got 666)'. State.ensure() chmods the user state dir to 0o700 and reads the mode back, but Windows has no POSIX mode bits (chmod only toggles the read-only attribute; stat always reports 0o666), so the read-back can never pass. POSIX behavior stays exactly as before (chmod + read-back + throw). On win32 the read-back is skipped when the state dir resolves inside the user profile (os.homedir(), compared case-insensitively), because there its privacy comes from the NTFS ACL inherited from the profile (verified with icacls on a real machine: only SYSTEM, Administrators and the user). Operator decision from an earlier review round: when the dir resolves OUTSIDE the profile on win32 (e.g. XDG_CONFIG_HOME redirected to a synced or network folder), do not throw; proceed and emit one warning naming the directory saying its privacy cannot be verified there. test/state-mode.test.js simulates Windows' stat and pins: accepted on win32 in-profile with no warning, accepted with the warning when redirected outside the profile, still refused off win32. Scope is intentionally minimal; other Windows test-suite failures (issue #148: POSIX-only fixtures, symlinks, extensionless fake binaries) are out of scope. Verified end to end on Windows 11 / Node 26.7: backpass scan, status, analyze and propose all run in user scope with the fix. Earlier runs failed only for infrastructure reasons (Test agent schema-output errors, then an account session usage limit), not code findings. ## What Changed - `State.ensure()` in `src/state.js` skips the POSIX mode read-back check on `win32`, since Windows has no mode bits (`chmod` only toggles read-only, `stat` always reports `0o666`), which previously made the check fail unconditionally there; title: --target <memory file> discards whole-surface evidence when another memory file exists (memory-set hash narrows)
body:
## Problem

The README says a targeted run keeps the whole surface's analysis: "Analysis, evidence, and state are those of the whole surface; only staging and the proposal gate narrow." That breaks as soon as the resolved memory set holds more than one file.

`src/cli.js:301` narrows the configured list for a memory target:

```js
config.memoryFiles = config.target.kind === "memory" ? [config.target.path] : scope.memoryFiles;
```

`memorySetHash()` (`src/memory.js`) hashes every resolved file (`path:hash`), and the evidence key includes that hash (`evidenceKey`, `src/state.js`). So an untargeted run and a targeted run over the same root file compute different hashes, and `foldForRun` (`src/commands/propose.js`) keeps no evidence (`e.memoryHash === memoryHash` fails for every record).

## Repro (user scope, backpass 0.1.30 @ `d1e7550`)

Setup: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` exists, `~/.agents/AGENTS.md` does not, and `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` exists (so it resolves as a *separate* memory file with the usual warning).

1. `backpass analyze --scope user --max-transcripts 12 ...` → `11 ok` evidence records, all with one memory hash.
2. `backpass propose --scope user --max-transcripts 12 --target .claude/CLAUDE.md ...` → `error no loss calculated yet: nothing to run gradient descent on`. `status` shows `evidence 11 ok` but `gradients 0 session(s)`.

The transcripts were unchanged on disk (the same `mtimeMs:bytes` as the stored keys), so freshness is not the cause. Only the memory hash differs. Re-running `analyze` with the same `--target` recomputes every record under the narrowed hash, and `propose --target` then works.

This matters most in user scope: `--target` is the practical way to avoid #75 (whole skill trees staged), so users hit this right after a normal `backpass` or `analyze` run.

## Not #189

#189 is about alternating between two *different* targets, where one evidence record per transcript gets overwritten. Here the target is the same root file the untargeted run already analyzed, and nothing was overwritten. The key just never matches.

## Possible fixes

- Keep hashing the full resolved set for a memory target: narrow only the write and staging surface, not `memoryFiles` as used for `memorySetHash`. That matches the README.
- Or exclude *separate* (never-optimized) files from `memorySetHash`, since they are not judged against at all.

title: Feature: add `backpass update` command to check and upgrade to the latest version
body:
### Summary
Currently, `backpass` is primarily distributed and installed as a global npm CLI package (`npm install -g backpass`) or run via `npx backpass`. However, it lacks a built-in command to check for updates or self-upgrade to the latest published npm release.

### Motivation
In active development and fast-iterating agent workflows, keeping `backpass` up to date ensures the latest bug fixes, model ladders, and parser improvements are picked up promptly. Companion ecosystem CLIs (such as `chrome-devtools-axi`) provide built-in `update` and `update --check` commands for frictionless maintenance.

### Proposed Behavior
Add a `backpass update` subcommand:
- `backpass update --check`: Query the npm registry (e.g. `npm view backpass version` or registry API) to check if a newer version is published compared to the running CLI version, outputting whether an upgrade is available.
- `backpass update`: Upgrade `backpass` to the latest release:
  - If installed globally via npm/pnpm: run the package manager upgrade or execute the global upgrade command (`npm install -g backpass@latest`).
  - If executed in a git checkout / development mode: cleanly fetch and fast-forward the default branch.
  - If permissions prevent in-place upgrade: display the exact copy-paste command required to upgrade.

### Alternatives Considered
Users currently have to remember to manually run `npm install -g backpass@latest` or `npm update -g backpass`. Having a first-class `backpass update` command directly within the CLI significantly improves operator ergonomics.

title: Synthesis abort blames the harness when a concurrent process edits a watched file
body:
## What happens

`assertRepoUntouched` (src/synthesize.js) fingerprints the repo's memory and skill files before synthesis and aborts the whole run if any of them changes. It reports the change as "synthesis changed X in the repository directly instead of the staging copy".

In a repo with other writers (a shared agent workspace where other agent sessions and cron jobs edit files), an unrelated process can edit a watched skill file during the long synthesis step. Backpass then blames the synthesis harness, and the finished analysis produces no proposal.

## Repro

1. Run `backpass` in a repo where `skills/foo/SKILL.md` is watched.
2. While the synthesis step runs, edit `skills/foo/SKILL.md` from another shell.
3. The run aborts with `synthesis changed skills/foo/SKILL.md in the repository directly instead of the staging copy ... a harness that edits outside its cwd cannot be trusted with the synthesis role`.

Seen on 0.1.28, and the check is unchanged on current main. The file was actually changed by a concurrent editor in another session, and the harness never touched it.

## Suggestion

- Say what was observed ("X changed during synthesis") instead of asserting the harness caused it, and mention concurrent editors as a possible cause.
- Optionally compare the changed file against the staging copy's version. If the repo content does not match what the harness wrote to staging, it is very likely a concurrent writer.

Workaround we use: run backpass from a detached git worktree snapshot so nothing else writes there.

title: One non-unique hunk anchor discards the whole synthesis proposal
body:
## What happens

A synthesis proposal is rejected in full when one hunk's `find` text is not unique in its target skill file (`"find" text appears 2 times in skills/<x>/SKILL.md; must be unique`, src/proposal.js). After the re-prompts are spent (`synthesis could not produce a valid proposal after 2 re-prompt(s)`), the run ends with nothing, and all the other valid edits are lost. In our run, 19 edits were proposed from 114 analyzed sessions, and two non-unique anchors in skill bodies discarded all of them.

Seen on 0.1.28 with codex/gpt-6-astra (xhigh) as the synthesis model. The anchors were short repeated lines in long SKILL.md files, such as a bullet that appears twice.

## Suggestion

- Tell the re-prompt the line numbers of each occurrence, and ask for a longer anchor with surrounding context.
- If an edit is still ambiguous after the re-prompts, drop only that edit, record why, and keep the rest of the proposal instead of failing the run.

The saved `proposal.json` made manual recovery possible, which was great. It would be even better if the valid edits went through automatically.

- Added `src/discovery/adapters/openclaw.js`, a new local-only, SQLite-backed harness adapter that reads an online backup snapshot (`openclaw backup sqlite create`, or `BACKPASS_OPENCLAW_DB`) rather than the live database, covers live branches plus deleted/reset archives (zstd-aware), assigns order-independent generation identity from each session's anchor, strips injected context/system scaffolding, excludes probe/eval/test namespaces and self-sentinel sessions, and removes its private temp snapshot via a new `cleanup` hook invoked from `src/cli.js`.

title: Analysis prompt lists a symlinked skill once per harness root (user scope)
Parallel `sessions new` helpers can abandon Claude's OAuth refresh lock, and the whole run dies in 15 s
body:
## What happens

When the Claude OAuth token happens to be due for a refresh at the moment backpass starts, the run fails in about 15 seconds before analysing anything:

```
· analyzing 54 transcript(s) with claude (claude-sonnet-5) effort=medium at jobs=4
error pinned analysis agent claude (claude-sonnet-5) failed unexpectedly (acpx claude session prompt failed (exit 1): [acpx] error: RUNTIME QUEUE_RUNTIME_PROMPT_FAILED Internal error: Failed to refresh OAuth token: another Claude Code process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh. This is usually transient; retry in a minute, and if it persists close other Claude Code processes or sign in again)
  check the claude/acpx failure above and retry; or pin a different harness: backpass --analysis-agent <agent>
```

Nothing else was using Claude Code on the machine at that hour. The same command had passed on the three previous nights, when the token was still valid at start time.

## Minimal way to see it

1. Sign in to Claude Code in a dedicated config dir and let the access token get close to expiry, or wait for a night where it expires right before the run.
2. Run `backpass --scope user` with the default `--jobs 4` and the analysis agent pinned to claude.
3. All four parallel analysis sessions fail with the message above. A `.oauth_refresh.lock` directory is left behind in that config dir (`$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.oauth_refresh.lock`), empty, with no live process owning it, and the credentials file has not been rewritten.

## Observed timing (one run, 2026-10-02, local time)

- 03:50:01 backpass starts.
- 03:50:02.97 the `.oauth_refresh.lock` directory is created. Its mtime stays at 03:50:03.00, so it was never touched again.
- 03:50:03.30 to 03:50:03.36 the four analysis sessions are created in acpx.
- 03:50:06.9 to 03:50:07.1 the four Claude agent processes start.
- 03:50:16.1 to 03:50:16.5 all four close with the refresh error, three times each in their stream logs.
- 03:50:16 backpass exits 1.

The lock's own rules, read from the Claude binary the adapter ships: it is considered stale after 60 s, and its owner touches it every 5 s while alive (`stale:60000,update:5000`). The lock was created and never updated, so whatever owned it was gone within 5 s. The sessions gave up after roughly 9 s, well before the 60 s takeover.

## Likely cause (inferred, not observed directly)

backpass opens every analysis call with a separate, short-lived `acpx claude sessions new` process before the prompt itself (`src/acpx.js`, the `run([... "sessions", "new", "--name", sessionName])` call; same code on current main). With `--jobs 4` four of these run at once. If the token is due, the first helper to start begins the refresh and takes the lock, then exits as soon as the session is registered, before the refresh completes. The lock is left with no owner, the credentials file is never rewritten, and the four real sessions that follow all see "another process is refreshing it or exited mid-refresh" until they give up.

The timing fits: the lock appears 0.33 s before the first session record, after backpass started, and no other Claude process ran in that config dir between 03:49 and 03:51. I could not log the helper's own exit, so I cannot prove which process held the lock.

## Suggested fix

Before fanning out, do one Claude call alone and wait for it to finish, so that a due refresh runs to completion in a single process. A prompt-less probe would do, as long as the process lives through the refresh rather than exiting right after `sessions new` returns. Retrying after a minute, as the message suggests, would start the same short-lived helpers and could abandon the lock again.

The workaround I use: one small Claude call under the same config dir just before `backpass`, which rewrites the credentials and clears the lock. With that in place the next run passed on all 54 transcripts.

## Versions

- backpass 0.1.29
- acpx 0.18.0
- @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp 0.76.0
- node v22.22.0
- Linux

I ran backpass nightly for a week up to 2026-10-05 and once more on 2026-10-07. It is not in regular use here at the moment, so this is offered in case it helps rather than as something I am blocked on.

title: fix(analyze): list each skill file once in analysis index
body:
Fixes #202

User scope loads three skill roots (`.agents/skills`, `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills`). A library skill symlinked into all three became three entries, and `renderSkillIndexForAnalysis` printed each one. `src/analyze.js` sends that index with every transcript, so the analysis model read the same skill several times.

`renderSkillIndexForAnalysis` now dedupes by the skill file's realpath, the same identity `loadedCopies` uses (shared helper `skillFileIdentity`). Entries whose realpath can't be resolved are kept. Distinct files that share a name and description are not merged.

`loadedCopies` and `skillDescriptionTokens` are unchanged, so budget accounting still bills every loaded copy. `analyze.js` passes `repo.root` so relative skill paths resolve against the repo, not the cwd.

Tests: a symlinked library skill reached through all three user roots appears once (fails without the fix); two distinct files with the same name and description both appear. `npm test` 859/859.

https://claude.ai/code/session_013cT8qWEkSqJRG6tm8AuKWc

title: fix: keep incompletely attributed instructions in root memory
body:
## What Changed
- Route new instructions to the root memory file when any supporting quote lacks session attribution, rather than assigning them to a nested file using only identifiable sessions.
- Add regression coverage for rejecting nested placement, accepting root placement, and preserving nested routing when attribution is complete.
- Document the root fallback for incomplete attribution.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bounded routing change restores root ownership when attribution is incomplete while preserving existing evidence floors, fully attributed routing, and write-scope safeguards.

## Testing

Targeted regressions, base-commit reproduction, production API smoke checks, and nine real CLI scenarios passed. CLI runs used isolated cached evidence and a scripted external synthesis harness—not live model calls. Product transcripts and persisted-file evidence were retained; disposable setups were removed.

title: fix(discovery): associate sessions in repos with separate git directories
body:
## What Changed - `listWorktrees` in `src/repo.js` now always includes the resolved repo root. It also drops the `worktree` entry that matches `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`. With `git init --separate-git-dir`, git reports that external git dir as the main worktree even though it isn't a checkout. Before this change, sessions run in the actual checkout (or a directory nested under it) were not associated with the repo. - If `--git-common-dir` can't be resolved, every reported entry is kept. Outside a Git repository, the function still falls back to the normalized root, and duplicate paths are removed. - Adds tests in `test/repo.test.js` for three cases: a separate-git-dir checkout, where sessions at the root and in a nested directory get tier-1 association and pass strict mode while an unrelated directory does not match; an ordinary repo with a linked worktree, with no duplicate paths; and a directory that isn't a Git repository. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is small and contained in listWorktrees. Filtering out the common dir only removes entries that are not checkouts: a separate git dir, or a bare repo's main entry. Always including the resolved root is safe at every call site, since they all pass a git toplevel or a directory that contains `.git`. Real-git tests cover the separate-dir, linked-worktree, and non-repo cases. ## Testing I ran the targeted repo tests, all passing. I confirmed the new separate-git-dir regression test fails on the base code and passes with the fix. Then I ran the real `backpass scan --strict` CLI against a temp repo made with `git init --separate-git-dir` and a fake Claude session: the base code matched 0 sessions, because git reports the external git dir as the worktree, while the fixed code matched the session as tier-1 exact ("cwd is worktree <checkout>"). The before/after CLI transcript is saved as evidence. There is no UI surface, so no screenshot applies.
Evidence: backpass scan before/after in a separate-git-dir repo $ git worktree list --porcelain worktree <tmp>/proj-gitdir ## base: backpass scan --strict local claude SCANNED 1 MATCHED 0 0 transcript(s) associated with this repo · tier1 0 (exact) ## fix: backpass scan --strict local claude SCANNED 1 MATCHED 1 1 transcript(s) associated with this repo · tier1 1 (exact) local claude 11111111-222 interactive today 2KB t1 cwd is worktree <tmp>/proj ```text ## Setup: git init --separate-git-dir $ cat proj/.git gitdir: /proj-gitdir $ git worktree list --porcelain worktree /proj-gitdir HEAD 59c45ae10001eeae24f9f52d54e96410610c2dff branch refs/heads/main ## base: backpass scan --strict --since all (HOME=fake, cwd=checkout) proj · 1 worktree(s) · since all HOST HARNESS SCANNED MATCHED SELF CACHED NOTE local claude 1 0 0 0 0 transcript(s) associated with this repo · tier1 0 (exact) · tier1.5 0 (sibling clone) · tier2 0 (remote) · tier3 0 (best-effort) · interactive 0 · non-interactive 0 HOST HARNESS SESSION KIND WHEN SIZE TIER HOW ## fix: backpass scan --strict --since all (HOME=fake, cwd=checkout) proj · 1 worktree(s) · since all HOST HARNESS SCANNED MATCHED SELF CACHED NOTE local claude 1 1 0 1 1 transcript(s) associated with this repo · tier1 1 (exact) · tier1.5 0 (sibling clone) · tier2 0 (remote) · tier3 0 (best-effort) · interactive 1 · non-interactive 0 HOST HARNESS SESSION KIND WHEN SIZE TIER HOW local claude 11111111-222 interactive today 2KB t1 cwd is worktree /proj ```
## Pipeline Updates from [git push no-mistakes](https://github.com/kunchenguid/no-mistakes)
⏭️ **intent** - skipped ✅ No issues found.
✅ **Rebase** - passed ✅ No issues found.
⚠️ **Review** - 1 info - ℹ️ `src/repo.js:67` - This fixes the main case but leaves a gap. With `--separate-git-dir`, `git worktree list` reports the external git dir as the main entry, so when backpass runs from a linked worktree of that repo, listWorktrees now returns only the linked worktree and the real main checkout is still missing. Verified with git 2.50.1: from `lt`, the porcelain output lists `meta` (dropped as commonDir) and `lt`. `co` never appears. Before this change `co` was also missing (`meta` was listed in its place), so this is not a regression. Sessions in the main checkout are associated only if the sibling-clone scan finds `co` through a shared remote. Git keeps no pointer from the git dir back to the checkout, so the only fix would be extra discovery machinery, which is outside this change's scope.
✅ **Test** - passed ✅ No issues found. - `node --test test/repo.test.js` (all 14 pass, including the 3 new listWorktrees and separate-git-dir tests) - Regression check: put the base `src/repo.js` back temporarily and ran `node --test --test-name-pattern="separate git" test/repo.test.js`. It fails as expected: listWorktrees returned the external git dir instead of the checkout. Restored the fixed file afterwards. - End-to-end: built a temp repo with `git init --separate-git-dir` and a fake HOME holding a Claude session whose cwd is the checkout, then ran `HOME=<fake> node bin/backpass.js scan --strict --since all --harness claude --host none` from the checkout against both the base and fixed `src/repo.js` - Deleted the temp repo, fake HOME and copied files; the worktree is clean (`git status --short` shows nothing)
✅ **Document** - passed ✅ No issues found.

title: feat(status): show each nested memory file's sampled-session reach
body:
## Intent

Implement part (1) of issue #191: a nested memory file trains only on sessions whose every in-repo work path is under its directory, so in repos with cross-cutting sessions it may never reach minGapEvidence, and nothing told the user. Now backpass status and the run summary show, per nested file, how many sampled sessions were attributed to it, with a warning below minGapEvidence. The user (issue author, Pantoria) asked to implement their own ready-for-pr backpass issues, each in its own worktree and PR. Follow AGENTS.md invariants and VISION.md. No live model calls were made while implementing.
Scope decision: only part (1) (maintainer: restore, can ship alone). Part (2), the opt-in to ignore reads of configured memory files as work paths, is explicitly out of scope and left for a follow-up; commit says Refs #191, not Fixes. Design: counts come only from deterministic workedUnder attribution in nestedCorpora (src/commands/analyze.js), persisted to .backpass/nested/reach.json at attribution time so status stays read-only and cheap (no discovery/sampling); unmeasured files show 'not yet measured'. Proposal nested entries gain sampledSessions/minGapEvidence/belowMinGapEvidence; status --json gains nestedAttribution. Strictly report-only per the 'Presentation never gates' invariant - a test asserts the root edit is still proposed when a nested file is below the floor. Wording deliberately says 'no add, rewrite, or remove edit can reach this file' instead of the issue's 'cannot receive edits', because extract/move edits are exempt from the evidence floor. Accepted: status shows the count/floor saved at the last attribution, timestamped, not a fresh measurement.

## What Changed

- Each time sessions are attributed to nested memory files (`nestedCorpora` in `src/commands/analyze.js`), backpass now saves to `.backpass/nested/reach.json` how many sampled sessions each nested file can learn from, meaning sessions whose every in-repo work path is under that file's directory. The save has a timestamp and records the `minGapEvidence` floor and whether the file is below it. New helpers in `src/nested.js` build, write, read and format this record (`nestedReach`, `writeNestedReach`, `readNestedReach`, `nestedReachWarning`).
- `backpass status` gains a "NESTED EVIDENCE REACH" section. It shows the count and floor saved at the last attribution, or `not yet measured` if no attribution has run, and warns when a file is below `minGapEvidence`, at which point no add, rewrite, or remove edit can reach it. `status --json` now includes a `nestedAttribution` object. `status` reads only the saved file and does no discovery or sampling.
- In proposals, each `nested` entry now carries `sampledSessions`, `minGapEvidence` and `belowMinGapEvidence`. The run summary prints "N of M sampled session(s) worked only under dir/" and the same below-floor warning. All of this is report-only and never gates a run. README documents it, and tests cover the status output and the warning, including a check that the root edit is still proposed when a nested file is below the floor.

Refs #191. This covers part (1) only; the opt-in to ignore reads of memory files is left for a follow-up.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change only reports data: counts come from the existing deterministic workedUnder attribution and are saved to .backpass/nested/reach.json. That file sits beside the per-file state directories without clashing, since the raw-file cleanup only walks subdirectories. Nothing reads the count back to gate a run, and a test checks the root edit is still proposed when a nested file is below the floor, which matches every stated constraint in the intent.

## Testing

I drove the real CLI end to end in four disposable monorepo setups: below the floor, at the floor, `analyze` only, and no nested config. In every setup only the model was stubbed. The run summary and status showed "1 of 3 sampled session(s) worked only under apps/api/" with the warning "below minGapEvidence (2); no add, rewrite, or remove edit can reach this file". At the floor ("2 of 4") there was no warning. The root edit was still proposed below the floor, so the count stays report-only. Before any run, status shows "not yet measured". Status does not change reach.json. A corrupt reach.json makes status warn and fall back to "not yet measured" without failing. With no nested config there is no reach section and no `nestedAttribution` key. The two targeted test files also pass. Every scenario passed, so the verdict is go.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before any run, backpass status lists the nested file as 'not yet measured' and writes no reach.json | ✅ pass | live | sparse.txt: 'apps/api/AGENTS.md: not yet measured - run `backpass` or `backpass analyze`'; 'reach.json exists after status: false' |
| A full backpass run where the nested file gets 1 of 3 sessions prints the count and the below-minGapEvidence warning in the run summary | ✅ pass | live | sparse.txt run summary; proposal.nested[0] has sampledSessions 3, minGapEvidence 2, belowMinGapEvidence true |
| Report-only: the root edit earned by the web sessions is still proposed while the nested file is below the floor | ✅ pass | live | sparse.txt: proposal edit files = [["e1","add","AGENTS.md"]] |
| After the run, backpass status shows the timestamped reach section with the warning, and status --json carries nestedAttribution | ✅ pass | live | sparse.txt: 'NESTED EVIDENCE REACH (sampled sessions at the last attribution, 2026-10-15 16:49; report-only)' plus the JSON nestedAttribution block |
| status reads the saved count without rewriting reach.json | ✅ pass | live | sparse.txt: 'reach.json unchanged by status: true' |
| At the floor (2 of 4 sessions), the count is shown with no warning in both the run summary and status | ✅ pass | live | floor.txt |
| backpass analyze alone records the count, and status then shows it | ✅ pass | live | analyze.txt: 'reach.json exists after analyze: true'; status shows '1 of 2' with the warning |
| Adversarial: a corrupt or malformed reach.json does not make status fail; it falls back to 'not yet measured' | ✅ pass | live | sparse.txt: both corrupt-file status runs exit 0 and show 'not yet measured' |
| A repo without nested memory files shows no reach section, no nestedAttribution key, and writes no reach.json | ✅ pass | live | plain.txt: 'status --json has nestedAttribution key: false', 'reach.json exists: false' |

title: fix(apply): refuse a proposal made under a different budget
body:
## Intent Fix issue #188: backpass apply gated accepted edits against the CURRENT config budget (config.budgetTokens / nestedBudgetTokens) instead of the cap the proposal was made under (proposal.budget.capTokens, nested[].budget.capTokens), silently comparing two different measurements. The user (issue author, Pantoria) asked to implement their own ready-for-pr backpass issues, each in its own worktree and PR. Follow AGENTS.md invariants and VISION.md. No live model calls were made while implementing. Deliberate decision: apply REFUSES on a mismatch (loud and named, consistent with the existing scope-mismatch refusal) rather than silently gating at the proposal's cap, because silently overriding the user's current config/--budget would also be a quiet swap. The refusal names the file and both numbers and gives the remedy (re-run apply with --budget N, or nestedBudgetTokens N for nested files, or propose again). Only files that accepted edits land in are checked, so a nested-only apply is not blocked by the root. cmdApply refuses before the review UI; src/apply/writer.js repeats the check as owner of all write gates. Proposals with no recorded cap fall back to the current config as before. The writer's nested gate now uses the shared nestedBudget(config) helper from src/nested.js (a parallel PR #190 extends that helper for per-file caps). Existing tests that relied on the bug (proposal built at one cap, applied at another) were updated to build the proposal at the cap they apply under; this is intentional. Message wording differs slightly from the issue example because root and nested can mismatch separately. ## What Changed - `backpass apply` now checks that the budget a proposal was made under (`budget.capTokens` for the root, `nested[].budget.capTokens` for nested files) still matches the current config. If they differ, `cmdApply` stops with a `UserError` before the review starts. The error names the file and both token counts, and tells you how to fix it: re-run apply with `--budget N` or `nestedBudgetTokens` set to N, or propose again. Only files that receive accepted edits are checked, so a nested-only apply isn't blocked by a root mismatch. A proposal with no recorded cap still uses the current config, as before. - `applyDecisions` in `src/apply/writer.js` runs the same check (`budgetMismatches`) before it reads or writes anything, and records each mismatch as a failure. The nested budget gate now uses the shared `nestedBudget(config)` helper from `src/nested.js` instead of computing the value inline. - The README apply and nested-budget sections now describe the refusal. In `test/apply-cli.test.js`, `test/nested.test.js` and `test/proposal.test.js`, tests that built a proposal at one budget and applied it at another now build it at the budget they apply under. New tests cover the refusal. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: This is a small, well-tested refusal gate that matches the stated intent and can only block an apply, never cause a wrong write; the one finding is an edge case in the hint text. ## Testing The three targeted test files passed. I then drove the real `backpass apply` CLI in throwaway git repos holding real proposals (no model calls) through 13 root and nested scenarios, including a side-by-side run against the base commit that reproduces the issue #188 bug. Every scenario driven live behaved as the intent requires, and the transcripts are saved in the evidence directory. The writer-level repeat check can't be reached through the CLI, so it is marked untested live and is covered by unit tests only. This is a CLI-only change with no visual UI, so the evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots. - Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 10 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Proposal made at 30,000 tokens, config says 10,000: apply refuses with exit 1, names AGENTS.md and both numbers, suggests `--budget 30000`, and leaves AGENTS.md and the rejection file untouched | ✅ pass | live | root-budget-mismatch.txt (S1) | | Same mismatch through the review paths (`--no-open` and `--no-ui`): refuses before any review UI opens | ✅ pass | live | root-budget-mismatch.txt (S2, S2b) | | Following the suggested fix, `--budget 30000`, writes the edit and checks it against 30,000 | ✅ pass | live | root-budget-mismatch.txt (S3) | | Bug reproduction: the base commit silently writes a proposal made at 30 under a 5,000 config and gives a misleading over-budget failure for one made at 5000 under 20; the fixed build refuses both and… | ✅ pass | live | root-budget-before-after.txt (S4, S5) | | Matching budgets (10,000 and 10,000) still apply normally | ✅ pass | live | root-budget-before-after.txt (S6) | | A proposal with no recorded budget falls back to the current config and applies | ✅ pass | live | root-budget-before-after.txt (S7) | | Nested file made at 200, nestedBudgetTokens 300: refuses, names apps/api/AGENTS.md, suggests `nestedBudgetTokens set to 200`, and writes nothing | ✅ pass | live | nested-budget-mismatch.txt (N1) | | Nested-only apply is not blocked when the root budget (1) differs from the root's recorded budget, because the root has no accepted edits | ✅ pass | live | nested-budget-mismatch.txt (N2) | | nestedBudgetTokens unset: the nested mismatch suggests `--budget 200`, and following it writes the nested file | ✅ pass | live | nested-budget-mismatch.txt (N3, N4) | | The writer repeats the check on its own, even when the earlier `cmdApply` check is bypassed (nested file in both directions, plus only checking files that accepted edits land in) | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload did not establish a live result. applyDecisions is reached from the CLI only after cmdApply's own check has already refused, so the writer's separate check can't be driven through th… |

title: feat(config): allow a per-file budget on nested memory file entries
body:
## Intent Implement issue #190: per-file budget for nested memory files. nestedBudgetTokens was one shared cap for every nestedMemoryFiles entry, which cannot fit files differing 5-10x in size. The user (issue author, Pantoria) asked to implement their own ready-for-pr backpass issues, each in its own worktree and PR. Follow AGENTS.md invariants and VISION.md. No live model calls were made while implementing. Design, following the maintainer's stated preference for object entries over a path map: nestedMemoryFiles accepts plain strings (unchanged behavior: nestedBudgetTokens then budgetTokens) or { "path", "budgetTokens" } objects. Entries are normalized once at config load (splitNestedMemoryFiles in src/config.js) into a plain path list plus a derived nestedBudgetTokensByPath, so downstream string consumers are untouched; the derived key is always recomputed and ignored if set by hand. Propose and apply both read the cap through ONE helper, nestedBudget(config, relative) in src/nested.js (maintainer requirement, see #188); the apply change is deliberately a one-line call-site swap so the parallel #188 PR rebases cleanly. Malformed entries fail with named config errors (maintainer requirement). Deliberate choices: unknown keys in an entry are rejected (so a typo like 'budget' can't silently train under the wrong cap) even though other config objects are lenient; per-file budgetTokens must be a positive integer as the issue specified. --budget behavior is unchanged. contract-class opt-in: existing configs behave identically. ## What Changed - `nestedMemoryFiles` entries can now be `{ "path", "budgetTokens" }` objects as well as plain path strings. At config load, `splitNestedMemoryFiles` (`src/config.js`) turns them into a plain path list plus a derived `nestedBudgetTokensByPath`. `applyNestedMemoryConfig` then re-keys those caps to normalized paths. Any `nestedBudgetTokensByPath` set by hand is overwritten. Malformed entries fail with named config errors: a non-object, a missing or empty `path`, an unknown key, or a `budgetTokens` that isn't a positive integer. - `nestedBudget(config, relative)` (`src/nested.js`) now takes the file path. It returns the entry's own cap if it has one, otherwise `nestedBudgetTokens`, otherwise `budgetTokens`. Propose (`nestedContext`), `run` and `status` budget displays, and the apply gate in `src/apply/writer.js` all read the cap through this one helper. title: fix(analyze): keep a trace of unparseable replies and stop retrying them forever
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #193: when analysis output had no parseable JSON, the evidence record kept only status failed plus the error string, dropping the reply, and the transcript was re-analyzed every run forever. The user (issue author, Pantoria) asked to implement their own ready-for-pr backpass issues, each in its own worktree and PR. Follow AGENTS.md invariants and VISION.md. No live model calls were made while implementing.
Implemented all three proposal parts. (1) Failed records keep reply {class, chars, head, tail}: the whole reply is passed through the existing redact() before cutting 300-char head/tail (so a secret can't be split at a snippet edge); chars is measured by backpass from the raw reply. No harness stop reason is stored because acpx runs --format quiet and exposes none - deliberately not invented (never trust/invent model numbers). (2) A deterministic class empty/prose/truncated/unparsed (rules documented in classifyUnparsedReply) shows in status and in the error text. empty is unreachable today because assertNonEmptyOutput fires first, kept for completeness (open PR #183 may change that path). (3) Skip-after-N, which the maintainer allowed only if named in status and the last trace kept: MAX_UNPARSED_REPLIES = 3 constant (deliberately no config option), counted per failureKey = evidence key + answering agent/model/effort + analysis prompt hash, so any change resets; only unparseable replies count (timeouts/exec failures reset and always retry so a flaky provider can't make backpass give up); --force re-analyzes. Skips are named in a run warning, summary suffix, summary.gaveUp in --json, and status text/JSON. Skipped records stay failed, so never count as evidence. No ANALYSIS_INDEX_VERSION bump: only failure records change, not what analysis accepts; legacy failed records still load.

## What Changed
- When an analysis reply has no parseable JSON, the failed evidence record now stores `reply: {class, chars, head, tail}`. The whole reply goes through `redact()` before the 300-char head and tail are cut, and `chars` is measured from the raw reply. `classifyUnparsedReply` decides the class (`empty`, `prose`, `truncated` or `unparsed`) from the reply text alone, and the class also appears in the error text.
- A transcript stops being retried after `MAX_UNPARSED_REPLIES` (3) unparseable replies in a row with the same failure key. The key covers evidence key, answering agent, model, effort and analysis prompt hash. Timeouts and exec failures reset the count. Changing any part of the key, or passing `--force`, analyzes the transcript again. Skipped records stay `failed`, so they never count as evidence. The skip is reported in a run warning, as a `skipped after 3 failures` suffix on the analyze/run/bootstrap evidence summary lines, and as `summary.gaveUp` in `--json`.
- `backpass status` now reads the root evidence store and the store of each trained nested memory file. Shared `layerNestedWeights` logic in `src/nested.js` gives status and analyze the same nested-file hashes. Status shows reply classes, give-ups and a MEMORY column for failed transcripts (only when nested files are configured), and `--json` `evidence` gains a per-file `files` array. README and `--force` help text are updated, and `test/analyze-failure-trace.test.js` adds end-to-end coverage.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change only touches failed-record bookkeeping and status reporting; given-up records stay `failed` and never count as evidence. Analyze and status now compute the root and nested hashes with the same shared helper, and the user decisions from the earlier fix rounds (a current-surface check for give-ups, nested evidence stores in status) are implemented correctly.

## Testing

Ran the targeted end-to-end test file, which runs the real CLI with a fake acpx (all 9 pass). Then drove backpass by hand in a throwaway repo and HOME. A secret placed across the snippet edge is redacted before the cut and never stored. A truncated JSON reply is classed `truncated` and a prose reply `prose`, each with a character count backpass measures itself. After 3 prose replies the next run makes no model call and names the skip in the warning, the summary, and status text and JSON. --force calls the model again, and a timeout resets the count. One informational note: an acpx exit 1 with a pinned agent aborts the whole run, as it did before this change. That writes no record, so the streak is neither reset nor counted. It is not a regression. No UI surface, so no screenshots.

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Secret straddling the 300-char head boundary is redacted before cutting and never persisted | ✅ pass | live | cli-transcript.txt: head ends 'API_KEY=[redac', grep for the secret finds 0 matches, prints 'secret not present in record' |
| After 3 unparseable replies in a row the next analyze makes no model call and names the skip in the warning and the summary | ✅ pass | live | cli-transcript.txt: model calls stay at 3; '1 skipped after 3 failures' and a warn line |
| status text and --json report the give-up (NEXT RUN column, gaveUp count, per-file evidence entries); the skipped record stays failed and is not counted as evidence | ✅ pass | live | cli-transcript.txt status output; evidence {ok:0, failed:1, gaveUp:1, files:[...]} |
| --force re-analyzes a given-up transcript | ✅ pass | live | cli-transcript.txt: model calls go from 3 to 4 with --force |
| A changed analysis model or memory surface resets the streak; status shows 'retry' once the memory surface changes | ✅ pass | live | test/analyze-failure-trace.test.js 'after 3 unparseable replies...' and 'status names a give-up only while the memory surface...' (real CLI with fake acpx) |
| A nested memory file's give-up appears in status (MEMORY column, per-file JSON) while the root analysis succeeds | ✅ pass | live | test 'status reads a nested memory file's own evidence store and names its give-up' |
| Adversarial: a timeout resets the streak and keeps no reply trace, so a flaky provider cannot cause a give-up | ✅ pass | live | test 'a timeout resets the streak and keeps no reply trace' |
| Old-format failed record without trace fields still shows in status and is retried | ✅ pass | live | test 'status still lists an older failed record without the trace fields' |

title: fix(memory): stop treating thematic breaks as instruction units
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #192: a thematic-break-only line (---, ***, ___) was parsed as an instruction unit by parseMemoryUnits (src/memory.js), inflating the status instruction count, getting an AG id in the analysis index, and showing as a similarity-1.00 cross-surface overlap against skills that also contain ---. The user (issue author, Pantoria) asked to implement their own ready-for-pr backpass issues, each in its own worktree and PR. Follow AGENTS.md invariants and VISION.md. No live model calls were made while implementing.
Change: CommonMark thematic breaks outside fences (3+ of the same -/*/_ char, optional internal spaces/tabs, up to 3 leading spaces) are not units and flush the current unit. Maintainer cautions honored: '- item' list items stay units, and --- inside fenced blocks stays content. Deliberate decision: a dash-only line directly under a plain paragraph is a setext H2 underline as in CommonMark, so the paragraph becomes the section name like a ## heading (neither is a unit); under a list item, quote, or fence it is an ordinary break; *** and ___ never underline. ANALYSIS_INDEX_VERSION bumped 3->4 deliberately, per the AGENTS.md rule, because analysis evidence stores positional AG ids validated by sanitizeEvidence and the cache key (memory content hash) would not change when only the parser does - so cached evidence on files containing --- would otherwise cite shifted ids. Rejection instructionIds are content hashes and stay valid. Out of scope: === setext and 1-2 dash underlines.

## What Changed
- `parseMemoryUnits` (`src/memory.js`) uses a new exported `THEMATIC_BREAK` pattern (CommonMark: 3 or more of the same `-`, `*` or `_`, optional internal spaces or tabs, up to 3 leading spaces). A break line outside a fence is no longer an instruction unit and ends the current unit. A dash-only line directly under a plain paragraph is now read as a setext H2 underline, so that paragraph becomes the section heading. Under a list item, a quote, or a fenced line it stays an ordinary break, and `***` / `___` never act as underlines. `- item` list items still count as units, and `---` inside fences stays content.

- `ANALYSIS_INDEX_VERSION` goes from 3 to 4 (`src/state.js`). Cached analysis evidence uses positional AG ids, and those ids shift for files that contain `---`, so old cache entries are invalidated. Covered by the new `test/memory-units.test.js` plus new cases in `test/status.test.js` and `test/workspace.test.js`.

title: fix(state): keep a named root memory file's evidence and proposal in its own state dir
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #189: the evidence cache held one record per transcript (evidence/<identity>.json) and one proposal.json, so alternating --memory-file / --target between different root memory files (A, then B, then A) overwrote evidence and re-analyzed every transcript though nothing changed, and B's run wiped A's pending proposal. The user (issue author, Pantoria) asked to implement their own ready-for-pr backpass issues, each in its own worktree and PR. Follow AGENTS.md invariants and VISION.md. No live model calls were made while implementing.
Deliberate decisions: per-target state directory (mirroring nestedStateDir) rather than keying the evidence path on identity+hash, because only that also fixes the single proposal.json. Runs whose resolved primary root file differs from the default run's file keep evidence/, evidence-summary.json, proposal.json, prompts/, synthesis/, raw/, apply/ under <state root>/targets/<file>-<sha8>/; --memory-file X and --target X share one dir. A default run (and --memory-file/--target naming the default file, and skill --target) keeps .backpass/ exactly as today - the maintainer required that. Rejections, gap ledger, scan cache, and probe cache stay shared via the root State (maintainer asked rejections be shared; the ledger is already scoped by memoryPath). User scope target dirs live under the user state root with mode 0700, never in the repo. apply/status/analyze with --memory-file X read X's state; bare apply and status list pending target proposals with the exact command. AGENTS.md got a one-clause update under 'Scopes and targets' to record the new layout. Known, accepted limitations: one-time re-analysis on upgrade for users who already used non-default --memory-file (no migration); skill --target still shares the default proposal.json (out of scope). Maintainer wants a test that fails if the per-surface path is removed (A,B,A with no re-analysis of A) - included in test/target-state.test.js - and live evidence of a real A,B,A --memory-file run showing reuse.

## What Changed

- A run that names a root memory file other than the default one (`--memory-file X` or a memory `--target X`) now keeps its evidence, evidence summary, proposal, prompts, synthesis staging, raw, and apply surface under `<state root>/targets/<file>-<sha8>/` (`surfaceState` in `src/target.js`, `targetStateDir` in `src/state.js`). Training A, then B, then A no longer re-analyzes unchanged transcripts or overwrites the other file's pending proposal. Default runs, runs that name the default file, and skill targets still use `.backpass/` exactly as before. User-scope target dirs sit under the user state root with mode 0700.
- Target states share the scope root's scan cache, rejections, gap ledger, and probe cache. Raw-file reclamation and the host-cache prune now run against the scope root (`state.scopeRoot`), so they also cover `targets/`.
- `apply`, `status`, `propose`, `analyze`, and full-run hints now show the exact command for the state being read, e.g. `backpass apply --memory-file X` (with `--scope user` when needed). Bare `apply` and `status` also list pending target proposals that are unapplied and passed their gates. README and AGENTS.md describe the new layout, and `test/target-state.test.js` covers it, including an A, B, A run where A's evidence is reused without re-analysis.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The fix round fully addresses both earlier findings: every apply/status hint is now built from the state being read, so a target state gives `--memory-file <file>`, and bare apply also lists waiting target proposals when the default proposal is already applied or failed its gates. I traced the default, target, skill-target and user-scope cases and found no wrong output or behavior change for default runs.

## Testing

Ran the real CLI in throwaway repos with an isolated HOME and a stand-in acpx/pi harness, so no real model was called. Covered: the A,B,A `--memory-file` runs, compared with the same runs on the base commit; the default layout; `--target` and `--memory-file` sharing one state; the status and apply hints; review-2's bare-apply listing; the fixed synthesis-failure hint in both the propose and full-run paths; and user-scope permissions. Every live-driven scenario passed. The targeted regression test file was also run, but it is not a live run, so its scenario is recorded as untested. The gate-failed and bootstrap-applied states for review-2 were seeded by editing the disposable proposal.json, because the stand-in harness can't produce them reliably. This is a CLI-only change, so the evidence is CLI transcripts rather than screenshots.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 10 of 11 scenarios driven live against the product

title: fix(acpx): classify adapter-rejected models as model-unavailable
body:
## Intent Goal: a backpass user whose pinned Claude model is turned down by the Claude ACP adapter gets a true, actionable error instead of "its acpx adapter does not support sessions - upgrade acpx or omit the effort override". That message was false: sessions worked and acpx was current. The block was found in a real run on Windows with acpx 0.19.6 and claude-agent-acp 0.81.2. The Claude Code CLI on PATH was an older build whose advertised model list did not include the pinned id claude-haiku-5-5. The adapter refused --model after session/new ("Failed session/set_config_option for model ...: Invalid value for config option model"), acpx exited 1, and classifyAcpxFailure did not recognize that line, so openSession marked the failure as unsupported and sessionPrompt printed the misleading upgrade advice. Decisions: - Keep the change scoped to the classifier, mirroring #185, which made "does not support this model" a model-unavailable verdict. The new regex also matches "session/set_config_option for model" and "session/set_model for model". A pinned pass now reports "model not available" with the adapter's advertised list in the detail; an auto-picked pass falls through the ladder. Ruled out here on purpose: - changing which unclassified create failures count as unsupported. That is the #91 class (EPERM), with its own maintainer contract and a behavior change for the pi/grok exec fallback, so it stays a separate issue; - an explicit effort-off switch (#70, its own PR). - One regression test, the incident's own repro: a model-rejected mode in the existing fake acpx (test/acpx-session-create-timeout.test.js) asserts openSession and sessionPrompt throw an AcpxError that is not unsupported, reads "session create failed", and classifies as model-unavailable. No other tests are wanted. - Running tests: the fake-acpx tests are POSIX shebang scripts that cannot spawn on native Windows (ENOENT for every test in that file, pre-existing ones included), so run them under WSL or Linux with Node 22.5+. Measured before submitting: the full suite under WSL with Node 22 passed 950/950; eslint, prettier --check and tsc --noEmit are clean. - Real run with the old CLI (backpass analyze --scope user --limit 1, pinned claude-haiku-5-5): - before: "error claude cannot apply invocation-scoped effort=medium because its acpx adapter does not support sessions / upgrade acpx or omit the effort override"; - after: "error pinned analysis agent claude (claude-haiku-5-5) model not available (acpx claude session create failed: [acpx] warning: requested model "claude-haiku-5-5" was not in the Claude ACP advertised model list (default, opus, fable, sonnet, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, ...); forwarding it to Claude Code so the adapter can accept or reject it.)". With a current CLI the same pin works end to end. - Docs: no user-facing docs describe this error text, so none should need changes; do not add a CHANGELOG entry (release-please owns it). ## What Changed - In `src/acpx.js`, `classifyAcpxFailure` now matches acpx's `session/set_config_option for model` and `session/set_model for model` rejections as `model-unavailable`. Both extend the existing "did not advertise that model" and "does not support this model" cases, which move into a shared `MODEL_REJECTED` regex. Previously this failure was unclassified, so `openSession` treated it as "unsupported" and `sessionPrompt` printed the false "its acpx adapter does not support sessions - upgrade acpx or omit the effort override" advice. A pinned pass now reports "model not available" with the adapter's advertised model list, and an auto-picked pass falls through to the next candidate. - In `test/acpx-session-create-timeout.test.js`, added a model-rejected mode to the fake acpx, plus one regression test. It asserts that `openSession` and `sessionPrompt` throw an `AcpxError` that is not marked unsupported, whose message reads "session create failed", and that `classifyAcpxFailure` returns `model-unavailable`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: A single regex in the classifier gains an alternative so a create-time model rejection takes the existing model-unavailable path; the change is scoped to the stated intent, adds one behavioral regression test, and I found no wrong-result path (effort is set after create via a different config key, so the new pattern cannot misclassify it). ## Testing The fake-acpx test file can't spawn on native Windows, so I ran it under WSL with Node 22. The new regression test fails on the pre-fix `src/acpx.js` and passes on the fixed one, and the other nine tests pass, including the case where an adapter really rejects sessions and still reports unsupported. Fixed, it printed "pinned analysis agent claude (claude-haiku-5-5) model not available (acpx claude session create failed: ... advertised model list ...)" plus the "pin a different harness" hint. In the fixed run the advertised-list warning appears but the "Failed session/set_config_option" line does not, so the detail is shorter than the author's quoted output, though it still shows the list. The classifier check shows the new pattern is narrow: it matches model rejections only, and a set_config_option failure for another option, the unknown-command-sessions error and EPERM all stay unclassified. title: fix(workspace): keep VCS internals and binary files out of the staging copy
body:
## Intent The operator reported "backpass is blocked" and asked for an upstream fix PR. A user-scope run (`backpass --scope user`: analysis, then synthesis) could not finish. Synthesis died while preparing the staging workspace with "FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory" (exit 134, after 479 s). prepareWorkspace walked, read and copied every file under every skill directory in a skills tree of about 1.7 GB. Several of those skills are their own git checkouts, with full .git object stores and pack files, and some ship compiled tool binaries (.exe). None of that is text an edit can apply to. Goal: unblock the run with the narrow fix that the #75 triage points to. Content that is not the memory surface stays out of the staging copy, and nothing is hidden: 1. Version-control internals (.git, .hg, .svn) under a skill directory are never walked, copied or read. Each one is named in `unstageable` with the reason READ_ONLY_VCS, so the existing contract holds: anything not staged is named and read-only, never silently dropped. 2. Binary files are not copied. The test is git's own (xdiff buffer_is_binary): a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes. Each binary file is named in `unstageable` with READ_ONLY_BINARY. A file that cannot be opened is not classified; the copy's existing error handling deals with it as before. 3. Deliberately out of scope: no size cap, no ignore-list setting, no special case for node_modules. Text files there are still staged as before. No CHANGELOG.md or release-manifest edits, because release-please owns them. The README gets one sentence saying VCS internals and binary files stay out of the copy and are read-only. 4. One test was added, because this failed for real. It stages a skill with its own .git pack and a NUL-bearing bin/tool.exe. It asserts that both stay out of the copy, that both are named in `unstageable` with their reasons, and that measureWorkspace reports no changes. The real run of this branch, on the same store: `backpass --scope user --limit 3 --jobs 1` completed analysis and synthesis end to end, exit 0 in 631 s. The proposal was "0 edit(s) from 3 session(s)": the evidence did not clear the thresholds, which is correct for that store. The staging copy held 24,596 text files (305 MB), with no VCS directories, no .exe files and no file containing a NUL byte. Before the fix, the same command died with the out-of-memory abort above. Environment note for the test step: this host is Windows without Developer Mode. The existing workspace tests whose fixtures call fs.symlink fail in fixture setup with "EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink", before any code under test runs. That is a host privilege limit, independent of this change, and upstream CI on Linux runs those tests. ## What Changed - `walkFiles` in `src/workspace.js` no longer descends into `.git`, `.hg` or `.svn` under a skill directory. Each one is named in `unstageable` with the new `READ_ONLY_VCS` reason. `prepareWorkspace` also skips binary files, which it detects with git's own test (a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes), and names each in `unstageable` with the new `READ_ONLY_BINARY` reason. A file that cannot be opened is not classified and goes through the copy's existing error handling. There is no size cap, ignore-list setting or `node_modules` special case, so text files are staged as before. - Together these stop user-scope synthesis from walking, reading and copying a skills tree with nested git checkouts and compiled `.exe` tools, which ran out of heap and aborted staging (#75). - `README.md` gains one sentence saying VCS internals and binary files stay out of the staging copy and are read-only. `test/workspace.test.js` adds one test: a skill with its own `.git` pack and a NUL-bearing `bin/tool.exe` keeps both out of the copy, names both in `unstageable` with their reasons, and `measureWorkspace` reports no changes. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small, additive filter in staging (prune .git/.hg/.svn, skip files with a NUL in the first 8000 bytes). Both kinds of skipped entry are named in `unstageable`, and it matches the stated intent with no extra components. Tracing it through `measureWorkspace`, the read-only skill index and the repo fingerprint found no wrong-result path. The skipped entries never enter `originals`, so they cannot be measured as deleted. The one new test drives the real `prepareWorkspace` and `measureWorkspace`. ## Testing I ran the new regression test, which passes. I also drove the real `prepareWorkspace` and `measureWorkspace` on a disposable repo with realistic and adversarial skill content, on both the target and the base commit. On the target, `.git`, `.hg` and `.svn` are pruned and named `READ_ONLY_VCS`, and binaries are named `READ_ONLY_BINARY`. A NUL at byte 7999 is classified binary and a NUL at byte 8000 is not. The empty file, UTF-8 file and node_modules text file are still staged, and `measureWorkspace` reports no changes. The base commit staged all 29 nested `.git` files, the .exe and the binaries, and named nothing in `unstageable`. The full `test/workspace.test.js` run has 13 failures: 11 are the documented symlink EPERM and the other 2 also fail identically on the base commit. I did not run the full `backpass --scope user` end to end: it needs an agent and a 1.7 GB store, so the author's own 631 s run stands unverified here. - Live validation: ✅ go - 6 of 7 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Skill with its own real git checkout (gc'd pack): the .git is never copied and is named READ_ONLY_VCS; the working files are still staged | ✅ pass | live | drive-target.txt: `.agents/skills/vendored/.git <- is version-control internals, not skill content`; SKILL.md and f0..f19.txt staged. drive-base.txt: 29 files from `.git` (pack, idx, hooks) were stage… | | .hg, .svn and a submodule-style .git file are also pruned and named | ✅ pass | live | drive-target.txt lists .hg, .svn and sub/.git as READ_ONLY_VCS; sub/readme.txt is still staged. | | A 3 MB .exe with a NUL byte is not copied and is named READ_ONLY_BINARY | ✅ pass | live | drive-target.txt: `bin/tool.exe <- is a binary file...`; absent from STAGED. drive-base.txt staged it. | | Binary test boundary is git's: a NUL at byte 7999 is binary, a NUL at byte 8000 is not | ✅ pass | live | drive-target.txt: nul7999.bin unstageable as binary; nul8000.txt staged. | | Out-of-scope behaviour is unchanged: node_modules text, an empty file and a UTF-8 file are still staged, and no size cap applies | ✅ pass | live | drive-target.txt STAGED includes node_modules/pkg/index.js, edge/empty.txt and edge/utf8.md. | | Files left out are never measured as deleted (measureWorkspace reports no changes), and the regression test passes | ✅ pass | live | drive-target.txt: `measure changes: []`; `node --test --test-name-pattern="object store and compiled tools" test/workspace.test.js` passes (1/1). | | Full `backpass --scope user` run on the author's 1.7 GB store completes without heap OOM | ⏸️ untested | no | It needs the operator's real skills store and a live ACP agent (acpx plus model credentials) and would read real user data, which is off-limits here. The staging stage that caused the OOM was driven l… |
