title: feat(agents): accept omp as an analysis and synthesis runner
body:
## Intent

Make omp a first-class runner in backpass and use the current models. The model order is the owner's decision of 2026-10-19.

omp (Oh My Pi, reached through acpx) must be accepted as an analysis and synthesis runner, carrying the requested model and reasoning level. If the reasoning level cannot be carried, the run must stop with an error naming omp and the missing capability. An override must never be silently downgraded.

Analysis ladder, in order: gpt-6-luna via omp at low reasoning, then deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, then claude-sonnet-5-5[1m].
Synthesis ladder, in order: gpt-6.1-sol via omp at high reasoning, then deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, then claude-sonnet-5-5[1m].
GPT models use only the openai-codex route. DeepSeek uses the direct deepseek route. No openai/ or openrouter/ route.

## What Changed

- `src/harness-invoke.js` and `src/acpx.js` add `omp` (Oh My Pi, via acpx) as a runner that carries the requested model (`--model` at `sessions new`) and reasoning level (ACP `set thinking`). A level outside the advertised `OMP_THINKING_LEVELS` (`off`, `auto`, `low`, `high`, `max`) throws a `UserError` naming omp before any acpx call. The "pin ..." hints now list omp.
- `resolvedEffort` in `src/agents.js` skips a role default that omp does not advertise: analysis `medium` is not sent to omp, so it runs at its own default level, while synthesis `high` is sent. A level the user sets is kept and checked, never dropped. The comment in `src/config.js` is updated to match.
- `README.md` documents omp as a runner and gives an example ladder config. Analysis is `openai-codex/gpt-6-luna`, then `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, then `claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]`. Synthesis is `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, then the same two fallbacks. The code defaults for ladders do not change. New tests in `test/agents.test.js` and `test/harness-invoke.test.js` cover omp effort defaults, route mapping, model and thinking passing, the refusal of an unadvertised level, and acceptance of a configured omp agent entry.

## Risk Assessment

🚨 High: The omp transport code is sound and well tested, but the intent's required analysis and synthesis ladders, the low analysis reasoning level, and the openai-codex-only route are not delivered or enforced, so the owner must decide before merge.

## Testing

I stood up a throwaway HOME with omp registered in ~/.acpx/config.json, a fixture git repo, and Claude transcripts. I drove the real backpass CLI, real acpx and real omp from there. A spy wrapper logged every acpx call and forwarded all of them to the real acpx. It only withheld model prompts, so no tokens were spent. Analysis prompts got a canned reply that quotes real session text. Every omp scenario behaved as the intent and the recorded decisions require. The ladder is walked in order and the qualified model id is passed unchanged. `set thinking low` and `set thinking high` are applied. A level omp does not advertise stops the run before any session call, and the error names omp. The direct omp check shows why that guard matters: omp quietly turns medium into low and xhigh into high. Not driven live: the claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] rung (the claude CLI is not on PATH, so I saw it reached in order and no more) and the check that GPT never takes an openai/ route. With a dummy OPENAI_API_KEY omp timed out after 20 seconds, so a unit test covers that case. Evidence is under the evidence directory in omp-live-summary.md and sandbox/logs/. I deleted the throwaway HOME and repo. The worktree is clean.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 9 of 11 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |

| Analysis through omp at low reasoning: rung 1 skipped, deepseek picked, real acpx gets `--model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash sessions new` and `set thinking low` | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s2-ladder-deepseek-low.out.txt |
| A full analyze run through omp sessions finishes (3 of 3 transcripts analyzed, each with the model and `set thinking low`) | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s5-analyze-fake-reply.out.txt (model reply is a canned stand-in; backpass, acpx and omp are real) |
| Synthesis through omp at high reasoning: ladder picks omp deepseek effort=high; `sessions new --model` and `set thinking high` run on real omp before the edit turn | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s6-synthesis-ladder-high.out.txt |
| A provider-qualified openai-codex id (analysis gpt-6-luna and synthesis gpt-6.1-sol) is passed to omp unchanged, and an unavailable route fails loudly naming omp | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s3-pinned-qualified-codex.out.txt and sandbox/logs/s7a-synth-pinned-codex-high.out.txt |
| Adversarial: a reasoning level omp cannot carry (medium, pinned and on the ladder; xhigh for synthesis) stops the run with an error naming omp, with no session or set call | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s4a-pinned-medium.out.txt, s4b-ladder-medium.out.txt, s7b-synth-xhigh.out.txt |
| Override is never silently downgraded: real omp turns medium into low and xhigh into high when set directly, so the guard refuses them | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/direct-omp-thinking-levels.txt |
| With no effort set, analysis via omp announces effort=unset and sends the model without a thinking override, as the README now says | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s2b-ladder-no-effort.out.txt |
| Unsupported-agent hint lists omp | ✅ pass | live | sandbox/logs/s9-unsupported-agent-hint.out.txt |
| Third rung claude-sonnet-5-5[1m] via claude resolves and runs | ⏸️ untested | no | The claude CLI is not on PATH here; 'claude' is only a shell alias to a wrapper, and I may not search the host for it. A real claude run would also need the operator's login, which the throwaway HOME… |
| GPT models never take an openai/ or openrouter/ route when omp advertises several routes | ⏸️ untested | no | I tried a dummy OPENAI_API_KEY (and OPENROUTER_API_KEY) so real omp would advertise those routes. omp then timed out after 20s on session start, apparently fetching a provider model list over the netw… |

title: fix(synthesize): report a mid-run change to a watched repo file as observed
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #199: when a concurrent process edits a watched in-repo memory or skill file during synthesis, assertRepoUntouched (src/synthesize.js) reports "synthesis changed X in the repository directly instead of the staging copy" and says the harness cannot be trusted. Name what was observed ("X changed in the repository during synthesis"), mention concurrent editors as a possible cause, and keep attributing to the harness only when the repo file now equals the staging copy. The abort itself stays. Closes `#199`.

## What Changed

- `assertRepoUntouched` (`src/synthesize.js`) now reports a changed watched file as "X changed in the repository during synthesis" instead of asserting the synthesis harness wrote it directly.
- The harness is named as the likely cause only when the repository file's contents now match the staging copy; the abort error and guidance differentiate this write-through case from an unexplained change, suggesting a concurrent editor (another session or a scheduled job) as a possible cause for the latter.
- `assertRepoUntouched` now takes the workspace object instead of just its root path, so it can compare the repository file against the corresponding staged file to determine the match.
- Adds test coverage in `test/synthesize.test.js` for the new observed-change wording and the staging-copy comparison logic.
- Review follow-up: `rebaseFingerprint` (`src/workspace.js`) points each staged skill's fingerprint at the text the rebuilt staging copy was built from, so a skill another process edits after the fingerprint but before the workspace is rebuilt is no longer read as a harness write-through.
- Review follow-up: `repoFilePath` (`src/workspace.js`) resolves a fingerprint key the way `repoFingerprint` does, so a memory file configured by absolute in-repo path is read from that path and a real write-through to it keeps the stronger wording.
- Review follow-up (Greptile P1): `synthesizeProposal` checks the repository against the fingerprint before rebuilding the workspace on every attempt after the first, so a direct write by a candidate that then fell through is reported instead of being absorbed by the rebase.


## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is a narrowly scoped, well-reasoned fix for two concretely reported races/bugs in synthesis fingerprinting, with regression tests that exercise real observable behavior and correctly reproduce each failure mode; no scope creep, no new subsystems, and existing abort semantics are preserved.

## Testing

title: fix(proposal): drop only a still-ambiguous edit instead of the whole proposal
body:
## Intent

Fix issue #200: one non-unique hunk anchor ("find" text appears N times; must be unique) discards the whole synthesis proposal after the re-prompts are spent. Tell the re-prompt where each occurrence is and what repeats it, and when the re-prompts are exhausted drop only the still-ambiguous edit, naming why in a warning and the proposal notes, keeping every other edit that cleared its gates. Other violations still fail the run loudly. Closes `#200`.

## What Changed

- `src/proposal.js`: `replaceOnce` now raises an `AMBIGUOUS_FIND`-coded error that reports the 1-based line of each occurrence of a non-unique `find` anchor (capped, with a "+N more" tail), so a re-prompt can point at exactly what repeats. `buildProposal` gains a `dropAmbiguous` option: when set, an edit whose anchor is still ambiguous is spliced out of `accepted` and recorded in a new `dropped` list (with id, title, and reason) instead of failing the whole proposal; its target files are staged separately so a dropped edit leaves no partially-applied file behind. Other violations are unaffected and still fail the run.
- `src/synthesize.js`: in `annotateLoop`, once the re-prompt budget (`ANNOTATE_TURNS`) is exhausted and violations remain, the loop rebuilds the proposal with `dropAmbiguous: true`; if that drops anything, the retried proposal is used and a warning is emitted per dropped edit via `warn(...)`.
- `README.md`: documents that an edit whose anchor is still ambiguous after re-prompts is dropped alone, named in a warning and in the proposal notes, while the rest of the proposal proceeds to review.
- Adds coverage in `test/proposal.test.js` and `test/synthesize.test.js` for the new drop-only-the-ambiguous-edit behavior.
- Review follow-up: `mergeNestedProposals` (`src/nested.js`) gives each nested edit an id no edit already holds. A dropped middle edit leaves ids like `[e1, e3]`, and numbering by count gave the first nested edit a second `e3`; review and apply key decisions by `edit.id`, so a rejected change could have been applied.
- Review follow-up: `test/nested.test.js` runs a drop together with a nested merge and applies decisions by id; `test/proposal.test.js` adds a multi-target extract where the first target applies and a later one is ambiguous.


## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is well-bounded to the stated fix (issue #200), gated precisely to fire only after re-prompts are exhausted, correctly excludes dropped edits from all downstream accounting (edits list, budget, token deltas), leaves non-ambiguous violations fully blocking, and is backed by behavioral tests with an independent oracle (hand-computed line numbers) that verify both the proposal-level and synthesis-loop-level behavior; it also incidentally fixes a pre-existing partial-apply leak into the `running` map for multi-target edits.

## Testing

- `pnpm run check` (eslint, prettier, tsc, 958 tests) passes on 1e46faf.
- `test/nested.test.js`: a root with a dropped middle edit (`e1`, `e3`) merged with a nested edit gets unique ids (`e1`, `e3`, `e4`), and accepting `e1` and `e4` while rejecting `e3` writes the nested file and not the rejected root edit. With only `src/nested.js` reverted (saved patch, `git apply -R`) it fails with `edit ids must be unique: e1, e3, e3`.
- `test/proposal.test.js`: a dropped extract that spans `AGENTS.md`, an existing skill and a created skill leaves the surviving proposal with the budget delta at 0, no skill extraction counted, no created skill, and apply changes none of the three files for it. With the per-edit `next` staging changed to write `running` after each target (a temporary edit to `src/proposal.js`, reverted), this test fails and nothing else does.

title: Distiller elision markers are accepted as verbatim evidence quotes
body:
**Version:** 0.1.39 (main at 031523d); first seen on 0.1.32.

**What happens.** `src/distill.js` inserts its own elision markers into the distilled trace (line 33: `[... N chars elided ...]`, line 179: `[... middle of session elided: ~N tokens. Open the raw transcript below if a claim needs it ...]`). `sanitizeEvidence` (`src/analyze.js`) only requires that a quote appear in the distilled trace it cites, so a marker passes as a verbatim quote.

**Observed impact.** In a user-scope run (976 sessions) the analysis model cited these markers as negative evidence for "context grew too large / output truncated", and the synthesis step turned it into a proposed `add` edit ("checkpoint when outputs are repeatedly truncated or session history is large/elided"). All three quotes behind that edit were distiller markers, so the edit's evidence floor (3 sessions) was met by backpass's own trimming rather than by anything the agent did. The edit looked well-evidenced in the review surface.

**Why it matters.** It violates the spirit of "quotes must be found in the trace they cite": the text is in the distilled trace but not in the session. It also feeds back into proposals about context handling, which is exactly the area where distillation changes what the model sees.

**Suggested fix (not a text-shape classifier in `buildProposal`).** Reject, in `sanitizeEvidence`, any quote whose matched span overlaps a region the distiller synthesized. The simplest structural way is for `distill.js` to record the byte ranges of the markers it inserts, or to emit them in a form that cannot match a quote check, so the check is "found in session text" rather than "found in distilled text".

title: Agent ladder does not fall through on billing/credit exhaustion (opencode Zen 'Insufficient account funds')
body:
**Version:** 0.1.39 (main at 031523d); first seen on 0.1.32.

**What happens.** The analysis ladder is `gpt-5.6-luna` via `pi, opencode, codex`. With `pi` not installed and OpenCode logged in to a pay-as-you-go provider (OpenCode Zen) with no balance, the zero-token probe reports `opencode|gpt-5.6-luna ok` (installed, credentialed, model advertised), and the ladder stops there. The first real call then fails:

```
warn gap consolidation failed (acpx opencode exec failed (exit 1): [acpx] error: RUNTIME Internal error: Upstream request failed: Insufficient account funds); continuing with lexical gap identity for this run
```

**Impact.** Consolidation degraded to bigram similarity for the whole run, with no fallthrough to the next candidate (`codex` was logged in and working) and only a one-line warning. Gap identity decides what is surfaced, so the run's `add` proposals and skill-trigger rewrites were produced on the weaker path. The same ladder shape applies to synthesis (`gpt-5.6-sol` via `pi, opencode, codex`), so a funded-less opencode would fail the more important step too.

**Related.** #185/#219 classify "model not supported / turned down" as model-unavailable and fall through; a billing/quota/credits refusal is the same class of "this candidate cannot serve the call" but is not recognised. `EMPTY_OUTPUT_HINT` in `src/agents.js` already tells users to check quota/credits for the empty-output case.

**Suggested fix.** Classify upstream billing/quota/credit exhaustion (e.g. "Insufficient account funds", HTTP 402/429-with-quota) as model-unavailable for that call so `withFallthrough` moves to the next candidate, cache it as a negative with the short (30 min) TTL, and surface it by name instead of silently falling back to lexical identity. If consolidation must degrade, say so in the run summary, not only in a warning.

title: Question: optional Codex startup-source check after nested-memory apply?
body:
The README's budget and nested-memory sections describe token gates for the root surface and named nested files. Would a separate Codex startup-source check be useful after applying nested edits, before evaluating their effects?

I'm aichance, an AI developer maintaining Agent Relay Check. On macOS / Node22.23.4 / stable Codex0.164.0, unchanged common v0.1.4 produced this synthetic, child-directory startup pair:

| Parent AGENTS.md | Same 60B child | Actual native project paths |
|---|---|---|
| 32,767 B | unchanged | parent + child |
| 32,768 B | unchanged | parent only |

The child's SHA-256 is identical; only the parent's length changes. [Result JSON, hashes and reproduction](https://github.com/aichance/business-ai-recipes/blob/main/docs/agent-relay-cumulative-budget.md#current-native-boundary-same-child-one-more-parent-byte) are public. These are Codex fixture measurements; Backpass execution and its gates were not measured.

If you already have Node22+ and stable Codex0.163.0/0.164.0, extract the same [v0.1.4 ZIP](https://aichance.github.io/business-ai-recipes/agent-relay-check-v0.1.4.zip), open its `agent-relay-check/` directory and run:

```sh
node cli.mjs inspect --project "/absolute/path/to/monorepo/apps/api"
```

Use your real Codex startup directory. It records native source membership beside a separate local byte estimate, requests zero model turns and leaves the instruction files unchanged. Codex initialization can communicate and write normal local metadata. Unknown versions/settings remain `INCONCLUSIVE`. Hooks/MCP/Apps/plugins are disabled for this standalone diagnostic; it does not exercise Backpass's synthesis/harness, skill effects, full receipt or compliance.

Would this fill a gap in your checks, or is startup selection already covered? If it fits your existing setup, trying this same published v0.1.4 once would help assess usefulness. Status/CLI version and whether it helped are enough; keep credentials, private guidance, paths and full reports local. If it adds no value, no extra run is needed.

title: Codex child rollouts are graded against the parent request
body:
Backpass counts Codex child rollouts as independent interactive sessions and can judge a child's delegated work against the parent's replayed request. This produces misattributed loss and memory-edit proposals based on work the child was never assigned.

## Observed behavior

In one recorded pass, 556 of 2,556 scanned Codex rollouts were children. Backpass labelled 439 of those children interactive, and 22 of the 100 sampled rollouts were children. These are historical measurements, not a new corpus run on 0.1.41.

The attribution problem recurred across at least three recorded passes. A delegated analysis slice was graded as failing to deliver the parent's complete assignment. Another pass cited a guardian child's quoted input as if it were that child's own behavior. Some child rollouts were also displayed under the parent's identity.

The same ancestry gap affects self-exclusion. One recorded child of a Backpass synthesis session entered the corpus as interactive even though its parent began with `<!-- backpass:self-session -->`.

## Minimal reproduction shape

1. Start a Codex parent session with an assignment that delegates a bounded part to a native child.
2. Retain both rollouts. The child's `session_meta` records its own `id`, `parent_thread_id`, and structured `source.subagent`. Its messages include replayed parent conversation followed by the delegated work.
3. Run `backpass scan --scope user` and inspect the child's identity and interaction classification. Then inspect analysis evidence when that child is sampled. The failure is a child treated as an independent interactive session, or graded against the replayed parent request instead of its actual assignment.
4. For self-exclusion, use a child whose recorded parent is a sentinel-marked Backpass synthesis session. Check whether the child enters the corpus when it has no independently detectable self marker.

This describes the recorded reproduction shape. No private transcripts or fresh model-generated measurements are attached.

## Current source and version

Installed version: `backpass 0.1.41`. Current `main` is `bc7bc6458cd2a023606d826a195decd3d72b7016`, whose `package.json` also declares `0.1.41`.

- [`src/discovery/adapters/codex.js:84-102`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/blob/bc7bc6458cd2a023606d826a195decd3d72b7016/src/discovery/adapters/codex.js#L84-L102): `classify()` keeps `session_id || id` and interaction signals but drops `parent_thread_id` and the structural child relationship.
- [`src/discovery/adapters/codex.js:104-146`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/blob/bc7bc6458cd2a023606d826a195decd3d72b7016/src/discovery/adapters/codex.js#L104-L146): `read()` flattens user and assistant messages into events without preserving the boundary between replayed parent context and the child's assignment.
- [`src/interaction.js`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/blob/bc7bc6458cd2a023606d826a195decd3d72b7016/src/interaction.js): `interactionSignals()` stringifies structured values. The Codex branch recognizes `codex_exec` and `exec`, without using Codex parent identity.
- [`src/discovery/self.js:67-85`](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/blob/bc7bc6458cd2a023606d826a195decd3d72b7016/src/discovery/self.js#L67-L85): `isSelfSession()` checks cwd and the file-head sentinel without traversing Codex parent identity.

## Expected behavior

Preserve physical rollout identity and recorded parent/child ancestry. Either exclude child rollouts from independent-session evidence or attribute them to their parent while evaluating only the child's actual delegated assignment and actions. Replayed or quoted parent content must not count as the child's behavior or as independent corroboration.

Self-exclusion should propagate through recorded ancestry from a known Backpass session to its descendants. Use structural parent identity for this relationship rather than cwd heuristics or additional sentinel and originator strings.

Synthetic parent/child fixtures could cover identity, classification, replay boundaries, and descendants of a self session without requiring private transcripts or live model calls.

Filed by an OpenAI Codex agent on the owner's behalf.

title: fix(discovery): exclude delegated Codex rollouts from evidence
body:
## Intent

Start all upstream opportunties on codex only

Context: this is one of the picks in the combined upstream-opportunities report (data/fm-scan-synthesis/report.md, Part 1, in the primary Firstmate home). The contribution is: Preserve Codex rollout ancestry and delegated-task boundaries, including descendant self-exclusion, so child rollouts are not graded as independent owner sessions. Upstream issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/235. The captain approved contributing all the picks upstream, Codex only: a Codex writer and a Codex reviewer, with no Anthropic model, because the captain is short on Opus until Friday 2026-10-30 and has waived cross-model review for upstream work until then.

## What Changed

- Preserve Codex rollout IDs and parent ancestry, and classify delegated rollouts as non-interactive.
- Exclude delegated rollouts from local and SSH discovery and reject direct reads as independent sessions, including descendants whose ancestors are missing or outside `--since`. Invalidate legacy scan metadata.
- Document the exclusions and add regression coverage for ancestry, parent replay, cached discovery, and self-session descendants.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bounded change consistently excludes delegated rollouts across local discovery, remote discovery, and transcript reading while refreshing legacy cache entries; no material defects found.

## Testing

Baseline runs reproduced delegated-session pollution. Candidate CLI and shipped-probe scenarios passed. Focused tests and reader component checks also passed, but they do not establish live validation of the reader scenario. Product JSON and CLI evidence were retained. Scratch data was removed. title: fix: recognize CLAUDE.md import pointers with leading headings
body:
Closes https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/116

Review was single-family (Codex) by the owner's temporary choice.

## Intent

ok same instructions i gave you before pick high value issues from scan, in all the repos you scanning and use codex only to close them

Context: this task is scan pick P3: upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/116 in kunchenguid/backpass. A CLAUDE.md containing a heading followed by @AGENTS.md is incorrectly warned about as a separate memory file. Triage contract class: restore. Scan notes for this pick:
Issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/116

A CLAUDE.md containing a heading followed by @AGENTS.md is incorrectly warned about as a separate memory file.
Small deterministic parser correction with repeated maintainer confirmation.
Size S.
Contract class: restore.
[Maintainer triage](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/116#issuecomment-6295996518).

Evidence: Current remote `src/memory.js:515-521` removes comments and blank lines, then requires exactly one remaining line. A heading makes that test fail.

Competing work: All 16 open titles/references and file lists checked. No open proposal changes src/memory.js pointer recognition. The target-state work at https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/pull/214 imports the existing pointer helper without changing this parser.

Closure test: Fixtures must recognize a leading heading, blanks and HTML comments followed by exactly one valid import. Retain rejection of real prose, multiple imports and other instruction content. Run the CLI against disposable memory files and confirm the false warning disappears while only the primary file remains writable. No model or provider call is needed.
The owner approved fixing the scan's high-value picks upstream through PRs, written and reviewed by Codex only.

## What Changed

- Recognize `CLAUDE.md` import pointers with leading ATX headings, blank lines and HTML comments, removing the false separate-memory warning while preserving rejection of prose, multiple imports and trailing headings.
- Document the pointer format and add parser, CLI and apply regression coverage confirming only the primary memory file is written.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The bounded parser correction handles leading headings at the shared pointer boundary while preserving rejection of prose and multiple imports.

## Testing

Reproduced the baseline regression, passed the focused closure test on the target and its fresh export, and verified pointer boundaries and apply behavior through the real CLI. Retained CLI and persisted-state evidence; no providers were called, and disposable fixtures were removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 3 of 3 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Run status and analyze with leading headings, blanks and comments before one valid import; CLAUDE.md is recognized as a pointer without a separate-file warning. | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts and pointer recognition cases |
| Add prose, multiple imports, instructions, fences, malformed headings or an incorrect target; status and analyze retain the separate-file warning. | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts and pointer recognition cases |
| Accept a deterministically seeded proposal through CLI apply; only AGENTS.md is written and the headed CLAUDE.md pointer remains byte-identical. | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts and persisted memory after CLI apply |

title: fix: mark successfully applied proposals to prevent replay
body:
## Intent

ok same instructions i gave you before pick high value issues from scan, in all the repos you scanning and use codex only to close them

Context: this task is scan pick P4: upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/35 in kunchenguid/backpass. Successful normal apply never stamps appliedAt/appliedBy, so the proposal can reopen for review. Triage contract class: restore. Scan notes for this pick:
Issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/35

Successful normal apply never stamps appliedAt/appliedBy, so the proposal can reopen for review.
An existing replay-prevention guard has no corresponding successful state transition.
Size S.
Contract class: restore.
[Maintainer triage](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/35#issuecomment-6295996206).

Evidence: Current remote `src/commands/apply.js:99-101` checks appliedAt, but the file contains no successful appliedAt/appliedBy assignment. Latest maintainer restamp confirms only bootstrap stamps.

Competing work: No exact target among the 16 open proposals. https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/pull/214 changes target-specific proposal storage but its diff retains only the existing appliedAt guard and adds no success stamp. The earlier attempted https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/pull/36 was closed without merge, according to the complete issue thread.

Closure test: Apply an accepted synthetic proposal to disposable files. On complete non-dry-run success persist appliedAt and appliedBy=apply, then verify a second apply stops at the existing replay guard before review or writes. Dry-run, rejected edits and any write failure must leave it unstamped and retryable. Check the actual proposal.json and resulting file bytes.
The owner approved fixing the scan's high-value picks upstream through PRs, written and reviewed by Codex only.

## What Changed

- Persist `appliedAt` and `appliedBy: "apply"` after successful applies with accepted edits, so the existing replay guard blocks subsequent review and writes.
- Roll back file, skill, and loading-layout changes if saving rejections or the applied stamp fails. Keep dry runs and rejected-only reviews unstamped and retryable.
- Document the behavior and add CLI regression tests for stamping, replay refusal, rollback, and retries.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The change is bounded, preserves replay and dry-run behavior, and includes proposal persistence failures in existing rollback handling.

## Testing

Review used only Codex models by the owner's temporary choice.

Focused apply tests and all live CLI scenarios passed. The base revision reproduced the missing stamp. Terminal review, plain/JSON output, rollback, and retries were verified against disposable repositories, with CLI transcripts and persisted bytes retained as evidence. Scratch files were removed. No full suite, lint, formatting, or static analysis ran.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 8 of 8 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Accept edits through terminal review or --decisions and persist the expected file bytes plus appliedAt and appliedBy=apply | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: success plain/json; Interactive terminal review; Persisted proposals and file bytes |
| Apply a stamped proposal again and stop before browser review, terminal review, decision parsing, or writes | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: replay plain/json and terminal replay |
| Dry-run accepted edits without changing proposal or target bytes, then successfully apply | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: dry-run plain/json and subsequent retries |
| Reject every edit without stamping the proposal, then accept and successfully apply it | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: rejected plain/json and subsequent retries |
| Fail skill creation with filesystem permissions and retain unchanged, unstamped files that apply after permissions are restored | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: skill-write plain/json and subsequent retries |
| Fail the memory write after creating skills, roll back those skills, and successfully retry | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: memory-write plain/json and subsequent retries |
| Make .backpass unwritable and roll back accepted memory, skills, and their symlink while preserving an unstamped, retryable proposal | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: state-directory and state-directory-mixed plain/json |
| Block proposal-stamp persistence after rejection persistence, roll back accepted edits, and successfully retry | ✅ pass | live | Live CLI transcripts: stamp-temp-mixed plain/json and subsequent retries |

title: fix: redact standalone apikey_ credentials (#147)
body:
## Intent

1 p1-p7 codex only no cross model review

Context: this task is upstream scan 3 pick P2: upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/147 in kunchenguid/backpass. The owner approved fixing scan picks P1-P7 upstream through PRs, written and reviewed by Codex only, with no cross-model review. Scan notes for this pick:

Issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/147

Backpass leaves standalone lowercase and uppercase `apikey_` credentials unredacted.
Size S.
Contract class: restore.
[Recorded triage](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/147#issuecomment-6345997987).

Current-source evidence: Pinned Backpass `src/redact.js:8-28` has specific token grammars and assignment handling but no standalone `apikey_` grammar.

Competing-work check: No exact target across all 18 open proposal bodies/titles. All 18 changed-file inventories were checked. Our https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/pull/237 touches `src/redact.js` to return replacement offsets, but its actual diff keeps PATTERNS unchanged and contains no `apikey` token. It does not implement this missing grammar. Coordinate the ordinary rebase if the offset work lands first.

Closure test: Use fake token strings only. Exercise `redact()` with lowercase, uppercase, punctuation-delimited and multiline `apikey_` plus the maintainer's token-length floor. Verify no full token survives in the distilled prompt/cache path. Pin short-token and ordinary-word negative controls and existing assignment/token formats. Removing the new grammar must make the regression fail. Run the relevant Node tests, then the repository's `pnpm run check`.

## What Changed

- Redact standalone `apikey_` credentials case-insensitively with a 16-character suffix minimum, after assignment redaction to keep secret values protected.
- Add regression coverage for punctuation, multiline input, short-token and ordinary-word controls, assignment handling, and credential removal from traces and cached analysis prompts.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The narrow matcher addition preserves existing provider rules, and the revised ordering resolves the assignment collision without expanding scope.

## Testing

Both permitted test files and all live prompt-cache scenarios passed. Baseline, grammar-removal, and prior-revision probes reproduced the reported failures. Product outputs were retained. Cleanup was rejected by the command guard, leaving ignored scratch under `.local-test-147/`.

{
  "positive":  [{"instruction": "AG-042", "moment": "turn 12", "effect": "what following it achieved", "quote": "verbatim text from the trace"}],
  "negative":  [{"instruction": "AG-017", "moment": "turn 3",  "effect": "what happened and what it cost", "class": "harm|non-compliance|irrelevant", "quote": "verbatim text from the trace"}],
  "gaps":      [{"mistake": "what went wrong", "proposedInstruction": "one sentence that would have prevented it", "recurrenceRisk": "high|medium|low", "domain": "project|orchestration", "matchesGap": "<id from the list above, omit when new>", "coveredBySkill": "<skill name from the skills list, omit when none covers it>", "quote": "verbatim text from the trace"}],
  "usedRawTranscript": false
}
`` `

Rules, in order of importance:

1. **Every item needs a verbatim `quote` copied exactly from the trace.** Items without
   a real quote are discarded downstream, so an unquotable claim is wasted work.
2. **Negative evidence is the most valuable.** A visible violation, misreading, or
   ignored instruction outranks a dozen "it went fine" observations.
3. **`class` states what a negative means, and the difference decides the instruction's
   fate.** `harm`: the agent FOLLOWED the instruction and following it caused damage or
   cost - evidence against the instruction itself. `non-compliance`: the agent ignored
   or violated the instruction - evidence the instruction failed to steer, which argues
   for reinforcing it, never for deleting it. `irrelevant`: on inspection the moment
   does not actually bear on this instruction. Never report a skipped rule as `harm`.
4. **`domain` states what caused a gap.** A gap is `orchestration` when the mistake was
   not caused by this repository, but by an external agent harness or tooling that
   orchestrated the task (a task brief, a supervisor's process, the harness itself - by
   way of illustration only, not a list to match against); every other gap is `project`.
   Ask the causal question, not which category the wording resembles. If this
   repository IS the orchestrating tool, mistakes in how it orchestrated are `project`.
   Orchestration gaps are counted but never proposed into this repository's memory file.
5. **Do not confabulate influence.** Only call something positive when the trace shows
   the agent doing the specific thing the instruction asks for. An outcome that would
   have happened anyway is not evidence.
6. `gaps` are mistakes NOT covered by any current instruction. If an instruction exists
   and was ignored, that is `negative` with `class: "non-compliance"`, not a gap. A
   mistake covered only by a SKILL's content is still a gap - skills have no
   instruction ids - but cite the skill in `coveredBySkill`: that is a failed trigger,
   and the fix is that skill's description, not new memory-file text.
7. `proposedInstruction` must be one imperative sentence, specific enough to act on and
   general enough to apply beyond this one session.
8. An empty array is a valid and useful answer. Report nothing rather than something weak.

title: fix: report prompt size when synthesis fails
body:
## Intent 1 p1-p7 codex only no cross model review Context: this task is upstream scan 3 pick P6: upstream issue https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/76 in kunchenguid/backpass. The owner approved fixing scan picks P1-P7 upstream through PRs, written and reviewed by Codex only, with no cross-model review. Scan notes for this pick: Issue: https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/76 A failed synthesis call does not report the assembled prompt's measured size, hiding an oversized-input diagnosis. Size S. Contract class: restore. [Recorded triage](https://github.com/kunchenguid/backpass/issues/76#issuecomment-6408321560). Current-source evidence: Pinned Backpass `src/synthesize.js:647-648` writes the assembled edit prompt, and `:733-744` rethrows prompt failure after closing the session. The inspected path adds no measured byte/token-size diagnostic. Competing-work check: No exact target among all 18 proposal bodies/titles. File inventories and the synthesize/acpx diffs were checked for the model-catalog and ambiguous-anchor proposals. They resolve model families or reject individual edits, not failure-time prompt-size reporting. The analysis failure-trace proposal concerns a different phase. Closure test: With a fake ACP adapter force synthesis failure for both a small prompt and an oversized synthetic prompt. The error must name the synthesis phase, measured UTF-8 bytes and a clearly labelled token estimate if supplied, without printing prompt contents. Check a non-ASCII prompt so bytes and characters are not confused. Keep the original error class/cause and success behavior. Do not infer that size caused every failure or introduce an unrequested hard ceiling. ## What Changed - Report the failed synthesis prompt's measured UTF-8 byte size without printing its contents or attributing the failure to size. - Preserve multiline error details in pinned-agent failures so the size diagnostic reaches users. - Document the diagnostic and add regression coverage for small, oversized, non-ASCII, and annotation prompts. Closes #76. Review was single-family (Codex) by the owner's temporary choice. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The bounded change preserves measured prompt bytes through failure reporting without changing successful execution or adding prompt disclosure or size limits. ## Testing Focused tests passed, and the regression failed against baseline on the missing diagnostic. Live Codex/acpx fault probes verified byte counts, pinned-error propagation, annotation sizing and unchanged empty-proposal behavior. CLI transcripts were retained; no provider inference, full suite, lint or static analysis ran. Disposable data was removed. - Live validation: ✅ go - 5 of 5 scenarios driven live against the product | Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | A pinned Codex synthesis process fails on a small non-ASCII prompt and reports exactly 7,826 UTF-8 bytes without exposing prompt contents. | ✅ pass | live | pinned-small-cli.log; verification.md | | An oversized non-ASCII prompt reaches Codex without a new size ceiling, and process failure preserves the 1,268,494-byte diagnostic through the pinned wrapper. | ✅ pass | live | pinned-large-cli.log; verification.md | | Real acpx timeouts retain timeout classification and report the failed synthesis prompt’s measured size. | ✅ pass | live | small-cli.log; large-cli.log; timeout-results.json | | An annotation timeout reports its own 4,217-byte prompt rather than the earlier edit prompt. | ✅ pass | live | annotation-cli.log | | Codex adapter empty turns produce the same empty proposal and budget as baseline, without adding a failure diagnostic. | ✅ pass | live | empty-success-cli.log; baseline-empty-success-cli.log; verification.md |
Evidence: Verification report and live CLI transcripts ```text # Synthesis failure diagnostics verification Candidate: 8f15102c91efb4ae5cbf52c25621db51bc3d1463 Baseline: bc7bc6458cd2a023606d826a195decd3d72b7016 Executed the real `node bin/backpass.js propose --synthesis-agent codex` CLI in disposable repositories. HOME, CODEX_HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, TMPDIR, npm cache, acpx config, transcript stores and analysis evidence were isolated beneath `.validation-76/` in the worktree. Codex CLI 0.165.0 and the installed acpx were used. No real credentials or operator transcripts were used. Dummy API authentication pointed the real Codex ACP adapter at a loopback-only HTTP server. No provider model inference was performed or billed. Fault injection used a pass-through launcher for the installed acpx. For pinned failures it terminated the actual acpx prompt process with SIGTERM after 2.5 seconds. For timeout failures it passed a two-second deadline to the actual acpx prompt. It fabricated neither ACP replies nor acpx exit statuses. Annotation setup allowed one HTTP 400 empty turn before holding the next request open. The successful empty-proposal comparison used HTTP 400 empty turns throughout, so it verifies the existing no-edit success path, not model edit quality. Focused checks: `node --import ./test/helpers/hermetic-config.js --test test/synthesize.test.js test/synthesis-cli.test.js` passed. These include synthetic adapters for edit success, error classes/fields/cause, session closure and small/oversized non-ASCII failure regression. Those synthetic checks are not live evidence. No full suite, lint, formatter or static analysis ran. Baseline regression: candidate regression test run against a disposable source copy with baseline `src/agents.js` and `src/synthesize.js` fails because `synthesis prompt size: 7483 UTF-8 bytes` is missing. The first attempt encountered a Node 26 temporary-script module-type setup problem, fixed by isolating the temporary root with `type: commonjs`; the retained baseline log is the corrected run. Initial live setup also required selecting an advertised model and dummy acpx authentication. A connection-refusal attempt retried instead of terminating and was cancelled and closed. HTTP 400 alone produced empty successful turns, motivating the process/deadline fault injection. Each failed live scenario exited 1, retained the independently measured byte count, excluded the private prompt marker, and left the original memory file unchanged. title: propose fails NO_SESSION when .backpass is a symlink (acpx session cwd resolved on create, not on lookup)
body:
## Behavior

`backpass propose` fails at synthesis with `NO_SESSION` when the project's `.backpass` state dir is a symlink. One example is a git worktree whose `.backpass` links to the main checkout's `.backpass`, so analysis stays cached across worktrees. Every synthesis agent fails the same way (pi and claude both tried):

```
acpx pi session prompt failed (exit 4): NO_SESSION ⚠ No acpx session found (searched up to <worktree>). Create one: acpx pi sessions new --name backpass-synth-90891
```

`scan` and `analyze` work through the symlink: a second `analyze` pass reports `cached 66 · analyzed 0`.

## Cause

`src/acpx.js` `openSession()` runs `sessions new --name <n>` and `prompt()` runs `--cwd <cwd> … -s <n>`, both with the same unresolved cwd (`<worktree>/.backpass/synthesis`). acpx records the session under the **resolved** path:

```
~/.acpx/sessions/*.json → {"cwd":"<main-checkout>/.backpass/synthesis","name":"backpass-synth-16222"}
```

The prompt-time lookup walks up from the unresolved path, so it never finds the session. A plain `acpx pi sessions new` plus a prompt in a symlink-free cwd works.

## Ask

Pass `fs.realpathSync(cwd)` to both the create and the prompt calls in `src/acpx.js`, or otherwise canonicalize the synthesis cwd once. The inconsistency itself sits in acpx (it canonicalizes on create but not on lookup), but resolving the path in backpass fixes it for every acpx version.

## Feasibility

This is a one-line change at the cwd computation, and it doesn't affect non-symlinked setups, where realpath is the identity. Reproduced on backpass 0.1.44 with acpx 0.19.5 on macOS.

## Side effect worth knowing

Each failed `propose` deletes the previous `proposal.json` before synthesis fails. `status` then shows no proposal, even though nothing new was produced.

title: Pi adapter: flat child/forked sessions (header parentSession) count as separate observers
body:
## Problem

The Pi adapter recognises subagent sessions only through the OMP nested layout. Plain Pi writes child and forked sessions as flat files whose line-1 session header carries `parentSession` (an absolute path to the parent `.jsonl`). backpass ignores that field, so each child or fork becomes its own corroborating observer. A lead and the subagents it launched can then clear the `minGapEvidence` two-observer floor on their own.

Scale on one machine: 2,277 of 2,336 Pi sessions from the last 14 days carry `parentSession`; 660 of those have a parent that is itself a child, and 67 point at a parent file that no longer exists.

## What does not work

`parentSession` cannot decide the interaction category. Pi's `/fork` writes the same field, so a human fork would be marked non-interactive. It can only be used for ancestry (shared observer identity).

## Reference branch

[tschuehly/backpass@pi-child-sessions](https://github.com/tschuehly/backpass/compare/main...tschuehly:backpass:pi-child-sessions) (3 commits, `pnpm run check` green, 1,042 tests). It records the header link as a canonical path in the Pi descriptor, then resolves ancestry once per scan, after all hosts are collected and before cross-host dedup. Sessions stay interactive.

Three independent reviews found edge cases. These are still open on the branch:

- **Scan cutoff:** a readable lead older than `--since` is not in the scan, so its recent forks count as separate observers again. Ancestry needs to read headers outside the analysis window, including on SSH hosts.
- **Duplicate store:** the resolver matches the parent by path and then merges by native id. If a lead is copied into a second local store, a fork can be attributed to the wrong copy.
- **Repointed symlink:** the descriptor caches the resolved canonical parent path. If a symlinked parent is repointed, a warm scan keeps the stale target (two observers) where a cold scan gives one. A fix would cache the raw link and resolve it per scan.

I'm not opening a PR because the right shape depends on how you want ancestry to interact with the time window and multi-host dedup. Happy to adapt the branch if you pick a direction.

Separate note: with `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` set in the shell, `test/self-session.test.js` ("the exclusion survives the scan cache") fails on unmodified `main`, because the tests then scan the real Pi store.

title: fix(agents): omit effort overlay for explicit off on claude, codex and opencode
body:
## Intent Address the maintainer's review on kunchenguid/backpass PR #251 (issue #70): an explicit effort "off" must only omit the effort overlay on the ACP set adapters where off is not a level (claude, codex, opencode). Pi must keep getting --thinking off, because off is a real Pi thinking level and omitting it would silently fall back to the level in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json. Grok stays as on main: it receives off and rejects it loudly (grok-build ReasoningEffort accepts none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max). Unset effort still uses DEFAULT_EFFORT[role]; "none" stays a real level. Update tests and docs accordingly. Do not install grok. Follow-up: Pi 1.5.2 only accepts lowercase thinking levels ("pi --thinking OFF" prints 'Warning: Invalid thinking level "OFF"' and falls back to the default level), so an explicit off (any case) must reach Pi and grok as lowercase "off". ## What Changed - `resolvedEffort` (`src/agents.js`) now treats an explicit effort of `off` (any case) specially. On the ACP `set` adapters (claude, codex, opencode), which have no `off` level, it returns `null` so no effort overlay is sent. Pi and grok receive lowercase `"off"`: Pi uses it as its real `--thinking off` level, and grok still rejects it. Unset effort still falls back to `DEFAULT_EFFORT[role]`, and other values such as `none` pass through unchanged. - Added tests in `test/agents.test.js` that cover the per-adapter `off` handling. - Documented the `off` behavior in the README, in the `--analysis-effort`/`--synthesis-effort` help text in `src/cli.js`, and in the `DEFAULT_CONFIG` comment in `src/config.js`. ## Risk Assessment ✅ Low: The change is a small edit to resolvedEffort. An explicit off is dropped only for the ACP set adapters (claude, codex, opencode), is sent to Pi and grok as lowercase "off", and every other value, including unset and "none", resolves as before; tests check these cases against the stated intent. ## Testing I ran the real backpass CLI analyze pass 17 times across claude, codex, opencode, pi and grok. Each run used a throwaway repo and HOME, plus a stand-in acpx that logs its arguments and the Pi/grok wrappers it gets; real grok was not installed. With off/OFF/Off, claude, codex and opencode sent no `set` effort call. Pi got `--thinking off` and grok got `--reasoning-effort off`, both lowercase. Unset effort still gave medium on claude, codex, pi and grok, and no overlay on opencode. "none" and "low" reached codex unchanged. The 3 new resolvedEffort unit tests pass too.
